replication_target_quote: These results support those reported by Hudesman and Wiesner (1979) on a similar sample.
outcome_quote: At the end of the treatment semester, results indicated that students who participated in the program had improved their academic averages more than the control group, as measured by Mann-Whitney U test.
review_note: The replication used a larger self referred community college sample and compared GPA improvement with controls.

effect_name: Instructor sexual orientation credibility bias
effect_claim: Students rate a male instructor as less credible when he identifies as gay than when he identifies as straight.
effect_claim_quote: Findings indicate that students perceive a gay teacher as significantly less credible than a straight teacher.
original_title: Coming Out in the Classroom... An Occupational Hazard?: The Influence of Sexual Orientation on Teacher Credibility and Perceived Student Learning
replication_title: Is Coming Out in the Community College Classroom an “Occupational Hazard?”
replication_target_quote: This study is a replication of Russ et al.’s (2002) work, which showed that students’ credibility beliefs about and perceived learning from a male university instructor were negatively affected when he identified as gay.
outcome_quote: Participants as a collective did not provide significantly different ratings for any dimension of credibility nor for perceptions of learning in either condition.
review_note: Replication uses community college students rather than the university students in the original.

effect_name: Fast mapping of novel constructions
effect_claim: Children learn a novel sentence construction from examples and apply it to new appearance scenes.
effect_claim_quote: Children who watched the videos and heard the accompanying description were able to match new descriptions that used the novel construction with new scenes of appearance.
original_title: Fast mapping between a phrasal form and meaning
replication_title: Can children use similarity between actions to learn grammar?
replication_target_quote: The present study was a replication and extension of Casenhiser and Goldberg (2005).
outcome_quote: The children in both conditions performed significantly worse on the appearance items than the causative trials, which fails to replicate the original study.
review_note: Later thesis varies training conditions but explicitly reports failure of the original novel construction result.

effect_name: Social class and income estimates
effect_claim: Middle class children estimate occupational incomes higher than working class children do.
effect_claim_quote: Middle‐class children, as compared to working‐class children, not only made higher overall estimates of income for all the occupations considered but also perceived a greater spread in incomes and a clearer division between manual and non‐manual occupations.
original_title: Children's representation of economic inequalities: The effects of social class
replication_title: Children's representations of economic inequality: A replication
replication_target_quote: In a study of children's estimates of occupational incomes Emler & Dickinson (1985) found substantial social class but no age differences in a Scottish sample, a result they interpreted as supporting Moscovici's theory of social representation. The main part of that study was replicated with West German children of the age range 8–12, whose parents were also interviewed.
outcome_quote: Significant age but no social class differences were found, estimates of both types progressively converging upon true values.
review_note: Replication is in West German children rather than the original Scottish sample.

original_title: THE EFFECTS OF A SELF‐INSTRUCTIONAL PACKAGE ON OVERACTIVE PRESCHOOL BOYS
replication_title: EFFECTS OF SELF‐INSTRUCTIONAL TRAINING ON SECOND‐ AND THIRD‐GRADE HYPERACTIVE CHILDREN: A FAILURE TO REPUCATE
effect_name: Self-instructional training increases classroom on-task behavior
effect_claim: A brief self-instructional package increased classroom on-task behavior among overactive preschool boys.
effect_claim_quote: On-task behaviors increased dramatically concomitant with the introduction of the self-instructional package
replication_target_quote: Bornstein and Quevillon (1976) demonstrated generalization from a 2-hour self-instructional training session to on-task behavior in the classroom
outcome_quote: The results of Bornstein and Quevillon's (1976) study were not replicated
review_note: Replication tested 7- and 8-year-old children rather than preschoolers; a later token program increased on-task behavior, but self-instruction alone did not.

original_title: Inter- vs Intra-Modal Performance of College Men and Women
replication_title: Inter- vs Intramodal Performance of College Men and Women: A Replication
effect_name: Women outperform men on an auditory-visual matching task
effect_claim: Female college students made more correct responses than male college students on temporal auditory-visual matching tasks.
effect_claim_quote: Women made significantly more correct responses than men.
replication_target_quote: Results are consistent with an earlier report by Gould (1977).
outcome_quote: women made significantly more correct responses than men.
review_note: The unexpected sex difference replicated; the absence of an intermodal versus intramodal performance difference also recurred but is outside this claim.

original_title: Incidental Learning and Long‐Term Retention of New Word Meanings From Stories: The Effect of Number of Exposures
replication_title: Contextual Learning of New Meanings for Familiar Word Forms from Reading and Listening to Stories
effect_name: More story exposures improve recall of new word meanings
effect_claim: Repeated story encounters with new meanings of familiar words incrementally improved later recall of those meanings.
effect_claim_quote: Accuracy in cued recall of novel meanings showed a linear, incremental increase with more exposures.
replication_target_quote: Study 1 was a conceptual replication and extension of Hulme et al. (2018).
outcome_quote: more explicit knowledge of the meaning was produced with more exposures.
review_note: Study 1 of a university-repository thesis supplies the replication; its immediate recall supports the exposure gradient, but does not test the original one-week retention claim.

original_title: Gifted Adolescents' Attitudes Toward Their Giftedness
replication_title: Gifted Adolescents' Attitudes Toward Their Giftedness: A Partial Replication
effect_name: Gifted adolescents hold multifaceted views of giftedness
effect_claim: Gifted adolescents held mixed, multidimensional views of their own giftedness.
effect_claim_quote: Gifted adolescents have strongly mixed attitudes about their giftedness.
replication_target_quote: Kerr, Colangelo, and Gaeth (1988) assessed gifted adolescents' perceptions of their own and others' views
outcome_quote: views of the gifted label and its effects are multifaceted
review_note: Specific positive and negative facets differed from the original, so only the multidimensional pattern is coded as replicated.

original_title: The IAT shows no evidence for Kandinsky's color-shape associations
replication_title: Color-Shape Associations Revealed with Implicit Association Tests
effect_name: Kandinsky color-shape pairs show little implicit-association evidence
effect_claim: Implicit Association Tests gave little support for Kandinsky's proposed yellow-triangle, red-square, and blue-circle pairings.
effect_claim_quote: there is no implicit association between the original color-form combinations.
replication_target_quote: Makin and Wuerger tested the theory using the Implicit Association Test (IAT) and did not find clear evidence for Kandinsky's color-shape associations
outcome_quote: found similar results to those of Makin and Wuerger, showing little support for Kandinsky's theory.
review_note: British null pattern recurred in a Japanese sample; a different Japanese color-shape mapping did show positive IAT evidence.

original_title: Improving the interview skills of college students using behavioral skills training
replication_title: Using Web-Based Behavioral Skills Training to Teach Online Interview Skills to College Students
effect_name: Behavioral-skills training improves college interview skills
effect_claim: Behavioral skills training improved college students' targeted job-interview skills.
effect_claim_quote: All participants acquired targeted skills
replication_target_quote: replicated previous research on teaching interview skills with BST by using this procedure to teach interview skills to college students
outcome_quote: All participant performance improved from baseline to post-training across all targeted dependent variables.
review_note: Replication moved from simulated in-person interview practice to synchronous web-based video; it is a procedural extension.

effect_name: Toddlers trust accurate speakers
effect_claim: Toddlers learn new words more reliably from speakers who previously labeled familiar objects correctly.
effect_claim_quote: children performed less systematically in response to an inaccurate than to an accurate source.
original_title: Sensitivity of 24-month-olds to the prior inaccuracy of the source: Possible mechanisms.
replication_title: Knowing How You Know: Toddlers Reevaluate Words Learned From an Unreliable Speaker
replication_target_quote: Experiment 1 replicated previous research (Koenig & Woodward, 2010)
outcome_quote: children displayed better performance in a word learning test when they learned words from a speaker who has previously revealed themself as reliable
review_note: Original toddlers were 24 months old; replication toddlers averaged 30 months. Verdict concerns the initial word-learning contrast, not the later reevaluation experiment.

effect_name: Fractions draw more negative math attitudes
effect_claim: People report more negative attitudes toward fractions than toward whole numbers.
effect_claim_quote: The vast majority of children and adults reported negative attitudes toward fractions despite having positive attitudes toward whole numbers.
original_title: Children’s and Adults’ Math Attitudes Are Differentiated by Number Type
replication_title: Perceptions of ease and difficulty, but not growth mindset, relate to specific math attitudes
replication_target_quote: Replicating prior work (Sidney, Thompson, Fitzsimmons, & Taber, 2021)
outcome_quote: college students endorsed more negative attitudes about fractions than WNs and percentages.
review_note: Original covered children and adults; replication sampled college students and also compared percentages.

effect_name: False certainty in low-risk HIV counseling
effect_claim: Many counselors tell low-risk clients that a positive HIV test means infection is certain, despite possible false positives.
effect_claim_quote: half of the counsellors told the client that if he tests positive, it is 100% certain that he is infected with the virus.
original_title: AIDS counselling for low-risk clients
replication_title: What Counselors Tell Low-Risk Clients About HIV Test Performance
replication_target_quote: Sixteen years later we assessed whether HIV counseling in Germany has improved by replicating the original study
outcome_quote: About half of professional counselors communicated the illusion of certainty for sensitivity (15 of 30), specificity (16 of 30), and the PPV (18 of 30).
review_note: The paper describes failure to improve counseling. For this original finding, continued false certainty is a successful replication. Test performance itself improved between studies.

effect_name: Visual change detection without awareness
effect_claim: People can detect visual changes even when they are unaware that a change occurred.
effect_claim_quote: sensitivity to change does occur in the absence of awareness
original_title: Change Detection Without Awareness: Do Explicit Reports Underestimate the Representation of Change in the Visual System?
replication_title: Implicit detection of change: Can we do without awareness?
replication_target_quote: D. Fernandez-Duque and I. M. Thornton (2000) seemingly demonstrated “unconscious detection of change”
outcome_quote: both experiments failed to replicate D. Fernandez-Duque and I. M. Thornton’s finding of an increase in change detection for unaware trials.
review_note: Follow-up found above-chance detection when adding a control condition, but argues a conscious strategy can explain that result; the original unaware-trial increase did not recur.

effect_name: Thirteen-month-olds comprehend familiar words
effect_claim: Thirteen-month-old infants look longer at the named object when hearing a familiar word than when hearing a nonsense word.
effect_claim_quote: 13-month-olds directed their looking time significantly longer at the referent of the known word when that word was uttered than when the nonsense word was uttered.
original_title: Semantic Comprehension in Infancy: A Signal Detection Analysis
replication_title: Overextensions in early language comprehension: evidence from a signal detection approach
replication_target_quote: Experiment 1 replicated the original findings of Thomas et al.
outcome_quote: 13-month-olds understand a word that a parent reported they would understand and did not understand a word that a parent reported they would not.
review_note: Verdict is for Experiment 1 using parent-reported known versus unknown words; Experiment 2 examined overextension.

effect_name: Message interpretation and false-belief tasks
effect_claim: Young children find a false-belief message task easier than a classic false-belief prediction task.
effect_claim_quote: children performed better on the message-desire discrepant task than on a false belief task.
original_title: Children's Interpretation of Messages from a Speaker with a False Belief
replication_title: Young children's false-belief reasoning: Interpretation of messages is no easier than the classic task.
replication_target_quote: In Study 3 we followed the Robinson and Mitchell procedure precisely
outcome_quote: failed to replicate the contrast reported previously.
review_note: The original advantage appeared in one of five investigations; follow-up found no advantage in matched tasks or in a close procedural replication.

effect_name: Heavy TV viewing and accessible social estimates
effect_claim: Heavier television viewers give higher frequency estimates about social phenomena and answer those questions faster.
effect_claim_quote: those subjects who watch comparatively more television not only overestimate frequency or probability but also give faster responses to various types of cultivation questions.
original_title: Processes and Effects in the Construction of Social Reality
replication_title: Psychological Processes Underlying Cultivation Effects Further Tests of Construct Accessibility
replication_target_quote: replicating the findings of Shrum and O'Gunn (1993)
outcome_quote: Heavy viewers gave significantly higher frequency estimates (cultivation effect) and responded significantly faster (accessibility effect) than did light viewers
review_note: Replication focused on soap-opera viewing and tested several social topics; mediation held for some but not all.

effect_name: Infant attachment distress and serotonin allele
effect_claim: Infants carrying the short 5-HTTLPR allele show greater distress in attachment assessments.
effect_claim_quote: The short allele for 5-HTTLPR was associated with attachment classifications characterized by higher emotional distress.
original_title: Genetic and Caregiving-Based Contributions to Infant Attachment
replication_title: Molecular-genetic correlates of infant attachment: A cautionary tale
replication_target_quote: this paper attempts, but fails, to replicate a recent finding by Raby et al. (2012)
outcome_quote: this paper attempts, but fails, to replicate a recent finding by Raby et al. (2012)
review_note: Verdict is for short-allele variation in distress during the Strange Situation, not the broader caregiver-responsiveness finding.

effect_name: Team-task ratings distinguish interdependent work
effect_claim: Ratings of team relatedness and workflow distinguish interdependent tasks from individual tasks.
effect_claim_quote: the scales differentiated between tasks that were predetermined to be individual versus team based.
original_title: Team Task Analysis: Identifying Tasks and Jobs That Are Team Based
original_journal: Human Factors The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
replication_title: Team Task Analysis
replication_journal: Human Factors The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
replication_target_quote: constructive replication and extension of Arthur, Edwards, Bell, Villado, and Bennett (2005)
outcome_quote: team relatedness and team workflow effectively differentiated between tasks with varying levels of interdependency
review_note: Original used student teams in a combat simulation; follow-up used F-16 pilot teams and expert-rated task interdependency.

effect_name: Distinct coercive-sexuality subtype of psychopathy
effect_claim: Early and coercive sexual behavior forms a distinct category among male sex offenders assessed for psychopathy.
effect_claim_quote: Taxometric analyses gave evidence of a natural discontinuity underlying coercive and precocious sexuality.
original_title: Coercive and Precocious Sexuality as a Fundamental Aspect of Psychopathy
replication_title: In search of the psychopathic sexuality taxon: Indicator size does matter
replication_target_quote: attempted to replicate the hypothesized psychopathic sexuality taxon
outcome_quote: Clearly dimensional results, however, were obtained when higher correlating and more valid quasi-continuous indicators were analyzed
review_note: Original taxon was found with weaker dichotomized indicators; follow-up found dimensional results with stronger indicators and several methods.

effect_name: Mortality salience and worldview defence
effect_claim: Mortality reminders increase positive reactions to worldview supporters and negative reactions to worldview critics.
effect_claim_quote: mortality salience led to especially positive reactions to someone who directly praised subjects ' cultural worldviews and especially negative reactions to someone who criticized them
original_title: Evidence for terror management theory II: The effects of mortality salience on reactions to those who threaten or bolster the cultural worldview
replication_title: Mild Depression, Mortality Salience and Defense of the Worldview Evidence of Intensified Terror Management in the Mildly Depressed
replication_target_quote: Two studies were conducted in which mildly depressed and nondepressed American college students contemplated their own mortality or a neutral topic and then evaluated targets who supported or threatened aspects of their worldviews.
outcome_quote: Replicating previous research, subjects who contemplated their own mortality engaged in more defense of the worldview (more positive reactions to worldview supporters and more negative reactions to worldview threateners).
review_note: The later study adds depression as a moderator but reports the original mortality salience worldview defence effect.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

effect_name: Older target overaccommodation
effect_claim: People endorse unnecessary helping behaviour more toward older than younger adults.
effect_claim_quote: In the older conditions, hypotheses were confirmed that participants approved overaccommodative behaviors, endorsed higher warmth and lower competence, and attitudes were modified when the older women contradicted the paternalistic stereotype by declining assistance.
original_title: Benevolent ageism: Attitudes of overaccommodative behavior toward older women
replication_title: Expanding Benevolent Ageism: Replicating Attitudes of Overaccommodation to Older Men
replication_target_quote: In prior work, a female target was offered unnecessary assistance, which is replicated in the current study with a male target.
outcome_quote: Our findings replicated earlier work in that overaccommodative behaviors were endorsed more so for the older target than the younger target, which corroborates support for the Stereotype Content Model in that older adults are viewed paternalistically.
review_note: The original vignette used a female target; the replication includes male and female targets.

original_title: The effect of leg-to-body ratio on male attractiveness depends on the ecological validity of the figures
replication_title: The influence of leg-to-body ratio, arm-to-body ratio and intra-limb ratio on male human attractiveness
effect_name: Slightly longer male legs are rated most attractive
effect_claim: For detailed male-body figures, heterosexual women rated leg-to-body ratios about half a standard deviation above average as most attractive.
effect_claim_quote: optima for more detailed computer-generated images was approximately 0.5 s.d. above the baseline
replication_target_quote: Previous work has focused on leg-to-body ratio (LBR) as a determinant of male attractiveness
outcome_quote: the optimally attractive LBR is approximately 0.5 standard deviations above the baseline.
review_note: The claim is restricted to detailed body figures; the original silhouette condition had a different optimum.

original_title: Happy Now, Tired Later? Extraverted and Conscientious Behavior Are Related to Immediate Mood Gains, but to Later Fatigue
replication_title: Sociable behavior is related to later fatigue: moment-to-moment patterns of behavior and tiredness
effect_name: Extraverted behavior predicts fatigue hours later
effect_claim: Momentary extraverted behavior predicted increased fatigue two to three hours later.
effect_claim_quote: Extraverted and conscientious behavior were concurrently related to positive mood and lower fatigue, but to higher fatigue after a 3-hour delay.
replication_target_quote: The present research attempted to replicate this finding and rule out some alternative explanations.
outcome_quote: extraverted behavior was indeed related to feeling tired 2–3 h later.
review_note: The replication tested extraversion-related delayed fatigue, not the original conscientiousness result.

original_title: Giving Leads to Happiness in Young Children
replication_title: Toddlers Are Happier Giving to Others Than to Themselves
effect_name: Toddlers are happier giving than receiving treats
effect_claim: Toddlers showed greater happiness after giving treats to another person than after receiving treats themselves.
effect_claim_quote: toddlers exhibit greater happiness when giving treats to others than receiving treats themselves.
replication_target_quote: This study examined the emotional benefits of sharing in toddlers
outcome_quote: toddlers displayed greater happiness after giving than receiving.
review_note: The original additional costly-versus-costless comparison is outside this claim.

original_title: Diet Pill and Laxative Use for Weight Control and Subsequent Incident Eating Disorder in US Young Women: 2001–2016
replication_title: Diet pill and laxative use for weight control predicts first‐time receipt of an eating disorder diagnosis within the next 5 years among female adolescents and young adults
effect_name: Diet-pill or laxative use predicts later eating-disorder diagnosis
effect_claim: Young women using diet pills or laxatives for weight control had higher risk of a first eating-disorder diagnosis later.
effect_claim_quote: women who reported diet pill (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 5.6; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 3.0, 10.5) or laxative (AOR = 6.0; 95% CI = 4.2, 8.7) use for weight control had higher odds
replication_target_quote: To replicate findings from a prior study which identified prospective associations between use of products for weight control
outcome_quote: participants using diet pills (risk ratio [RR] = 3.58, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.96–6.54) and laxatives (RR = 2.77, 95% CI: 1.01–7.64) had greater risk
review_note: Observational prospective associations, not evidence that these products cause eating disorders; follow-up and cohorts differed.

original_title: Pavlovian impatience: The anticipation of immediate rewards increases approach behaviour
replication_title: Intertemporal Pavlovian biases and links with mental health in the general population
effect_name: Immediate reward cues increase go responding
effect_claim: Anticipating immediate rather than matched delayed rewards increased approach or go responses.
effect_claim_quote: Go responding was increased in trials in which an immediate reward was available compared with trials in which a preference-matched delayed reward was available.
replication_target_quote: aimed to replicate this intertemporal Pavlovian bias effect
outcome_quote: We replicated the intertemporal Pavlovian bias effect on the probability of go responding
review_note: Mental-health symptom associations were an extension and did not consistently follow the response bias.

original_title: House-edge information yields lower subjective chances of winning than equivalent return-to-player percentages: New evidence from support forum participants
replication_title: How does the phrasing of house edge information affect gamblers’ perceptions and level of understanding? A Registered Report
effect_name: House-edge wording lowers gamblers' perceived chance of winning
effect_claim: Equivalent gambling-cost information expressed as house edge produced lower perceived chances of winning than return-to-player wording.
effect_claim_quote: house-edge information (e.g., “This game keeps 10% of all money bet on average”) is associated with lower perceived chances of winning, as opposed to equivalent return-to-player information.
replication_target_quote: experimentally tested this original phrasing of the house edge against an alternative phrasing
outcome_quote: Compared to return-to-player information, the original phrasing had both lower perceived chances of winning and higher rates of correct understanding
review_note: Registered report used a larger UK online-gambler sample; the original used support-forum members.

original_title: EXPERIMENTAL ANALYSIS OF PRECURSORS TO SEVERE PROBLEM BEHAVIOR
replication_title: Implementation of interventions informed by precursor functional analyses with young children: A replication
effect_name: Precursor-based intervention reduces severe problem behavior
effect_claim: Function-based treatment aimed at mild precursor behavior reduced precursors while severe problem behavior stayed low.
effect_claim_quote: this treatment strategy was effective for behaviors maintained by positive and negative reinforcement.
replication_target_quote: replicates and extends previous research by examining precursor assessments and interventions with three preschool-aged children.
outcome_quote: reductions in precursor behavior and continued low or zero rates of severe problem behavior.
review_note: The replication used three preschoolers; the original tested treatment analyses for two subjects.

original_title: Do 9-month-old infants expect distinct words to refer to kinds?
replication_title: Bilingualism affects 9‐month‐old infants’ expectations about how words refer to kinds
effect_name: Monolingual infants expect distinct words to name distinct kinds
effect_claim: At nine months, monolingual infants expected two distinct count-noun labels to refer to different object kinds.
effect_claim_quote: infants may expect distinct labels to refer to distinct kinds of objects.
replication_target_quote: comparing monolingual and bilingual 9-10-month-olds' expectations about the relationship between labels and object kinds.
outcome_quote: This replicated previous findings showing that monolinguals expect that distinct words label distinct object kinds
review_note: Bilingual infants in the extension did not show the same expectation; the effect name is restricted to monolingual infants.

effect_name: Affective word-response compatibility
effect_claim: People respond faster when the emotional meaning of a word matches the emotional meaning of the required response.
effect_claim_quote: reaction times were faster when the affective connotation of the presented word and the correct response was the same than when it differed.
original_title: An Affective Variant of the Simon Paradigm
replication_title: Revisiting the affective Simon effect
replication_target_quote: We replicated the affective Simon effect found by De Houwer and Eelen (1998)
outcome_quote: We replicated the affective Simon effect found by De Houwer and Eelen (1998)
review_note: Replication used the same grammatical-category response task and explored how the proportion of strongly emotional words changes effect size.

effect_name: Single-trial audiovisual timing recalibration
effect_claim: One asynchronous sight-and-sound event shifts the timing at which later sights and sounds seem simultaneous.
effect_claim_quote: exposure to a single, brief asynchrony is sufficient to produce strong recalibration effects.
original_title: Rapid Recalibration to Audiovisual Asynchrony
replication_title: Rapid Audiovisual Temporal Recalibration Generalises Across Spatial Location
replication_target_quote: Van der Burg et al. (2013, J Neurosci, 33, pp. 14633-14637) reported results showing that recalibration to asynchronous audiovisual events can happen extremely rapidly.
outcome_quote: Here we replicate the finding that shifts in perceived timing occur following exposure to a single, asynchronous audiovisual stimulus
review_note: Replication also tested different spatial locations; the named effect is the single-trial timing shift.

effect_name: Tact instruction improves bidirectional vocabulary
effect_claim: Teaching children to say foreign words for pictured objects produces stronger bidirectional vocabulary than teaching them to select matching pictures.
effect_claim_quote: Tact instruction consistently produced higher levels of emergent intraverbal responding compared to listener instruction
original_title: Learning a foreign language: Effects of tact and listener instruction on the emergence of bidirectional intraverbals
replication_title: Teaching a foreign language to students with autism via telehealth in inclusive school settings
replication_target_quote: replicate previous research that examined the effects of tact and listener instruction on the emergence of bidirectional intraverbals
outcome_quote: both forms of instruction led to bidirectional intraverbal relations, with tact instruction being relatively more effective
review_note: Original involved typically developing Brazilian children; replication involved Chinese-speaking students with autism taught by telehealth.

effect_name: Learner control improves multimedia transfer
effect_claim: Controlling the pace of a narrated animation improves performance on later transfer tests.
effect_claim_quote: learners who were allowed to exercise control over the pace of the narrated animation across 2 presentations (part-part presentation) performed better on transfer but not retention tests
original_title: When learning is just a click away: Does simple user interaction foster deeper understanding of multimedia messages?
replication_title: Learner control in animated multimedia instructions
replication_target_quote: We tested this guideline by comparing a learner-paced instruction with a system-paced instruction.
outcome_quote: We successfully replicated the interactivity principle in terms of better transfer.
review_note: Follow-up found learner control increased time on task, so the gain does not establish equal-time efficiency.

effect_name: People avoid effortful empathy
effect_claim: People choose to avoid empathizing with others partly because they expect empathy to be mentally effortful.
effect_claim_quote: a robust preference to avoid empathy, which was associated with perceptions of empathy as more effortful and aversive and less efficacious.
original_title: Empathy is hard work: People choose to avoid empathy because of its cognitive costs
replication_title: Are Observers Differentially Motivated to Empathize With Stigmatized Targets? An Investigation Using the Empathy Selection Task
replication_target_quote: people prefer to avoid empathy due to its perceived cognitive costs.
outcome_quote: Results replicate previous findings that people prefer to avoid empathy due to its perceived cognitive costs.
review_note: Follow-up tested stigmatized versus other targets; target group membership did not moderate the avoidance effect.

effect_name: Relationship inventory separates three dimensions
effect_claim: A short relationship inventory distinguishes regard, empathy, and congruence in responses from married couples.
effect_claim_quote: moderate, though tentative, support for the expected dimensionality of the abbreviated inventory.
original_title: The Dimensionality of an Abbreviated Relationship Inventory for Couples
replication_title: Dimensionality of an Abbreviated Version of the Relationship Inventory: An Urban Replication with Married Couples
replication_target_quote: to replicate an earlier study involving a sample of 83 rural married couples.
outcome_quote: the same dimensions were found across four different groups of respondents in the two studies.
review_note: Original tested rural couples; replication tested urban couples. This is a measurement-structure finding rather than a causal effect.

effect_name: Spouses show different body-space changes in pregnancy
effect_claim: Wives and husbands do not show similar patterns of perceived body-space change during and after pregnancy.
effect_claim_quote: The results did not duplicate previous study findings of similarity in spouses' patterns of change in perceived body space.
original_title: Spouses?? Body Image Changes During and After Pregnancy
replication_title: Spouses' Body Image Changes During and After Pregnancy: A Replication in Canada
replication_target_quote: replicated an investigation of the relationship between wives' and husbands' strength of identification and similarities in their patterns of change
outcome_quote: no similarities in wives' and husbands' changes in perceived body space or global body attitude
review_note: The original paper itself revisited an earlier study and reported no similarity. Follow-up was a Canadian sample; other body-attitude outcomes differed.

effect_name: Category labels accentuate line-length differences
effect_claim: People judge line lengths across systematic categories as farther apart than lengths in an uncategorized series.
effect_claim_quote: the stimuli belonging to different classes are judged as farther apart on that scale than in an unclassified series.
original_title: CLASSIFICATION AND QUANTITATIVE JUDGEMENT
replication_title: On the Role of Familiarity with Units of Measurement in Categorical Accentuation: Tajfel and Wilkes (1963) Revisited and Replicated
replication_target_quote: On the Role of Familiarity with Units of Measurement in Categorical Accentuation: Tajfel and Wilkes (1963) Revisited and Replicated
outcome_quote: categorical accentuation was higher when the lines were systematically categorized than when they were not
review_note: Replication also found a stronger effect with unfamiliar units of measurement.

effect_name: Vocabulary and reasoning mutual growth
effect_claim: Higher vocabulary predicts subsequent gains in nonverbal reasoning, and higher reasoning predicts gains in vocabulary.
effect_claim_quote: We found that individuals with higher scores in vocabulary showed greater gains in matrix reasoning and vice versa.
original_title: Mutualistic Coupling Between Vocabulary and Reasoning Supports Cognitive Development During Late Adolescence and Early Adulthood
replication_title: Mutualistic coupling of vocabulary and non‐verbal reasoning in children with and without language disorder
replication_target_quote: The current study tests whether language and non‐verbal reasoning show mutualistic coupling in children with and without language disorder using three waves of data from a longitudinal cohort study that over‐sampled children with poor language at school entry (N = 501, 7–13 years).
outcome_quote: Specifically, children with higher initial language abilities showed greater growth in non‐verbal ability and vice versa.
review_note: Original cohort comprised older adolescents and adults; replication tests reciprocal growth in younger children including language disorders.

effect_name: CW FIT and on task behavior
effect_claim: Class Wide Function related Intervention Teams increases pupils’ on task behavior.
effect_claim_quote: Group on-task data improved during CW-FIT over baseline levels.
original_title: Class-Wide Function-Related Intervention Teams: Effects of Group Contingency Programs in Urban Classrooms
replication_title: Improving Behavior in a Self-Contained Elementary Classroom for Students With Emotional or Behavioral Disorders: A Study of CW-FIT
replication_target_quote: In the present replication study, researchers examined the effects of CW-FIT in a self-contained U.S. elementary EBD classroom.
outcome_quote: Results revealed the teacher was able to implement CW-FIT with fidelity with corresponding increases in student on-task behavior and teacher praise, though there was little effect on teacher reprimands.
review_note: Replication tests CW FIT in a small self contained classroom of five pupils with EBD.

effect_name: Prompt exposure and intraverbal learning
effect_claim: Recent exposure to a prompt type makes that prompt more efficient for teaching new intraverbal responses.
effect_claim_quote: For all participants, the prompt method most recently used to teach intraverbal responses required fewer trials to teach new intraverbal responses compared to a prompt method that had not been used recently.
original_title:
The role of
 
 increased exposure to transfer-of-stimulus control
 
 procedures on the acquisition of intraverbal behavior
replication_title: Exposure to a specific prompt topography predicts its relative efficiency when teaching intraverbal behavior to children with autism spectrum disorder
replication_target_quote: The current study was an attempt to replicate these results with 3 children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder.
outcome_quote: For all participants, increased exposure to one prompt topography was sufficient to make it relatively more efficient as measured by number of trials to criterion.
review_note: Original tested typically developing preschool children; replication tests children with autism.

effect_name: Recall direction and subjective distance
effect_claim: Recalling related events backward makes a past target event feel closer than recalling them forward.
effect_claim_quote: people feel closer to a target event when they recall a stream of related events in a backward direction (i.e., a reverse-chronological order ending with the target event) rather than a forward direction (i.e., a chronological order beginning with the target event).
original_title: Trips Down Memory Lane: Recall Direction Affects the Subjective Distance of Past Events
replication_title: The influence of recall direction on judgments of subjective temporal distance from the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns
replication_target_quote: In a conceptual replication of their Study 2, we asked participants how close they felt to the first day that lockdowns were imposed in response to the Covid-19 pandemic in the U.S. (federally mandated on March 13, 2020) following either backward or forward recall of a stream of related events.
outcome_quote: The results of the present study ran directly counter to those of Lam and Buehler: participants rated the first day of lockdowns as feeling closer following forward recall than following backward recall.
review_note: Conceptual replication substitutes pandemic lockdown memory for university acceptance and finds the reverse direction.

effect_name: Failure experience and test anxiety
effect_claim: A single failure experience raises pupils’ test anxiety relative to a success experience.
effect_claim_quote: The failing group scored significantly higher than the successful group in the TASC which was administered immediately after the treatments.
original_title: The effect of a single experience of success or failure on test anxiety
replication_title: The Effect of a Single Success or Failure Experience on Test Anxiety: A Replication
replication_target_quote: Comparison of students' TASC scores indicated that the success group recorded a lower test-anxiety score on the posttest than they had done on the pretest, while the failure group's TASC score had shown an increase.
outcome_quote: Comparison of students' TASC scores indicated that the success group recorded a lower test-anxiety score on the posttest than they had done on the pretest, while the failure group's TASC score had shown an increase.
review_note: The later study assesses pre to post test anxiety changes rather than only post treatment group differences.

effect_name: Subliminal conditioning and implicit self esteem
effect_claim: Pairing self words with positive traits subliminally increases implicit self esteem relative to control pairing.
effect_claim_quote: Relative to control conditions, this procedure enhanced implicit self-esteem.
original_title: I Like Myself but I Don't Know Why: Enhancing Implicit Self-Esteem by Subliminal Evaluative Conditioning.
replication_title: Converging evidence that subliminal evaluative conditioning does not affect self‐esteem or cardiovascular activity
replication_target_quote: Subliminal evaluative conditioning (SEC), which subliminally couples self-words with positive words, has previously been successfully used to boost self-esteem, but the existing studies are in need of replication.
outcome_quote: Across the 3 experiments, no effects were found of SEC on implicit or explicit self-esteem or affect or on cardiovascular (re)activity compared to a control condition in which the self was coupled with neutral words.
review_note: Original and replication abstracts identify the same measured effect and result.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

effect_name: Pride expression and audience relevance
effect_claim: People express less pride when an achievement matters to the audience than when it does not.
effect_claim_quote: Pride expressions were reported to be less intense when the achievement was relevant to the observer of those expressions, both in hypothetical (Experiments 1a, b, c, 2a, b, and 3) and actual pride experiences (Experiment 4; first four experiments Hedge's g = 0.50).
original_title: Show or hide pride? Selective inhibition of pride expressions as a function of relevance of achievement domain.
replication_title: Who expresses their pride when? The regulation of pride expressions as a function of self-monitoring and social context
replication_target_quote: Specifically, pride expressions are lower when the domain of the achievement is of high relevance to observers. We set out to replicate this effect in a non-Western sample.
outcome_quote: Data from two preregistered studies (N1 = 913; N2 = 1081) replicated the effect that pride expressions are inhibited when the achievement domain is relevant.
review_note: Later preregistered studies use a non Western sample and also test self monitoring as a separate moderator.

effect_name: Physical education skills and exercise
effect_claim: Behavioral skill training in physical education increases adolescents’ exercise and sport participation.
effect_claim_quote: The intervention also had a positive impact on adolescents’ self-reported sport/exercise behaviour (p < .001).
original_title: Impact of a physical education-based behavioural skill training program on cognitive antecedents and exercise and sport behaviour among adolescents: a cluster-randomized controlled trial
replication_title: Effects of behavioural skill training on cognitive antecedents and exercise and sport behaviour in high school students: a cluster-randomised controlled trial
replication_target_quote: The goal of this paper was to replicate a prior cluster-randomised controlled trial, in which behavioural skill training resulted in significant improvements in adolescents' self-reported exercise/sport behaviour, exercise/sport intention, motivation, coping planning and self-efficacy.
outcome_quote: The results showed that the intervention did neither result in increased self-reported exercise/sport participation, objectively assessed physical activity, nor in improvements in the assessed cognitive antecedents of exercise/sport behaviour compared to the control condition.
review_note: The later trial uses a shorter training program and objective activity measure alongside the same self report outcome.
replication_journal: International Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology

effect_name: Culture and spontaneous social inferences
effect_claim: North Americans make more spontaneous trait inferences relative to situation inferences than Japanese people do.
effect_claim_quote: we hypothesized that European Canadians would be more likely to produce STIs than SSIs because of the individualistic/independent social orientation and the analytic thinking style dominant in North America, whereas Japanese would produce both STIs and SSIs equally because of the collectivistic/interdependent social orientation and the holistic thinking style dominant in East Asia. Employing the savings-in-relearning paradigm, we presented information that affords both STIs and SSIs and examined cultural differences in the extent of both inferences. The results supported our hypotheses.
original_title: Cultural Differences in Spontaneous Trait and Situation Inferences
replication_title: Attention allocation is a possible mediator of cultural variations in spontaneous trait and situation inferences: Eye-tracking evidence
replication_target_quote: Two studies sought to replicate previous work on cultural differences in the co-occurrence of spontaneous trait (STI) and situation (SSI) inferences
outcome_quote: Both studies replicated previous findings of cultural differences. European Americans made more STIs relative to SSIs than did Asian American or Japanese participants.
review_note: Original compares European Canadians and Japanese; later tests European Americans, Asian Americans and Japanese.

effect_name: Nostalgia and financial risk taking
effect_claim: Nostalgia increases financial risk taking.
effect_claim_quote: In Study 1, we established the basic effect of nostalgia and increased risk taking.
original_title: Nostalgia Increases Financial Risk Taking
replication_title: A Closer Look on the Relation Between Nostalgia and Risk-Taking
replication_target_quote: we tested in Study 3 if the link between nostalgia and financial risk-taking reported by Zou et al. could be replicated and extended to other domains of risk-taking.
outcome_quote: By and large, the relation between nostalgia and financial risk-taking could not be replicated nor extended to any other domains of risk-taking.
review_note: Later study separately tests functional and dysfunctional risk and directly retests the original finance link in Study 3.

original_title: Cognitive principles of multimedia learning: The role of modality and contiguity.
replication_title: Examining the Effects of Multimodal Presentations on Learning Spatial Layouts
effect_name: Auditory narration improves multimedia learning over on-screen text
effect_claim: Students learned more when verbal material was spoken rather than displayed as on-screen text alongside visual material.
effect_claim_quote: students learned better when verbal input was presented auditorily as speech rather than visually as text.
replication_target_quote: Presenting information appropriately in multiple modalities
outcome_quote: text alone was always the worst performer, and that presentations that capitalized on the auditory channel led to significantly better learning
review_note: Conceptual replication changed the learning target from lightning animation to a navigable spatial layout.

original_title: The regulatory effect of choice in Situation Selection reduces experiential, exocrine and respiratory arousal for negative emotional stimulations
replication_title: Situation selection for the regulation of emotion responses: Non-meaningful choice options retain partial physiological regulatory impact
effect_name: Choosing an upcoming negative image reduces negative experience
effect_claim: Being able to choose a forthcoming negative image reduced negative emotional experience relative to having that image imposed.
effect_claim_quote: having the choice in negative contexts decreased negative experience
replication_target_quote: wanted to replicate results on Situation selection efficiency and explore its limits
outcome_quote: The effect of Situation selection for negative experience was replicated.
review_note: The meaningful-choice condition replicated; non-meaningful choice did not reduce negative experience.

effect_name: Children follow others vegetable-eating norms
effect_claim: Children eat more vegetables when told that other children have eaten a large amount.
effect_claim_quote: Children ate more carrots when they believed that other children had eaten a large amount of carrots, compared to all other conditions.
original_title: Perceived eating norms and vegetable consumption in children
original_journal: International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity
replication_title: Perceived eating norms and children's eating behaviour: An informational social influence account
replication_target_quote: we aimed to replicate the effect that perceived eating norms have on children's vegetable consumption
outcome_quote: In both studies children were influenced by perceived eating norms, eating more when led to believe others had eaten a large amount compared to when led to believe others had eaten no vegetables.
review_note: Original tested carrot intake; replication examined vegetable consumption in two settings and found the social-norm effect in both.

effect_name: Animal setting alters docility and vigor ratings
effect_claim: Animals shown in less natural settings are judged more docile and less vigorous.
effect_claim_quote: Zoo animals were seen as restricted, tame, and passive while wild animals were characterized as free, wild, and active.
original_title: People's Perceptions of Animals
replication_title: An Animal’s Environment Influences Perceptions of Docility and Vigor But Not Aesthetic Appeal: A Constructive Replication
replication_target_quote: The current study replicated and expanded upon that prior work.
outcome_quote: Perceptions of docility increased and vigor decreased as the naturalness of the environment declined.
review_note: Outcome is for docility and vigor, which matched; replication did not find an environmental effect on aesthetic appeal.

effect_name: Question choice changes lie-detection accuracy
effect_claim: Diagnostic questioning changes how accurately observers distinguish truthful from deceptive answers.
effect_claim_quote: The different questioning sets produced a 36-point swing in accuracy from 42% to 78% accuracy.
original_title: Strong Diagnostic Questioning Effects on Deception Detection Accuracy With U.S. Customs Agents
replication_title: Deception detection and question effects: testing truth-default theory predictions in South Korea
replication_target_quote: The current experiment (n = 81) tested truth-default theory’s proposition 13 and diagnostic questioning module with a student sample from South Korea.
outcome_quote: questioning was found to significantly enhance (65%) and reduce (30%) deception-detection accuracy
review_note: Original used U.S. Customs agents; replication used South Korean students, and both found large accuracy changes by question set.

effect_name: Ruminative thinking and obsessive-compulsive severity
effect_claim: More ruminative thinking accompanies greater obsessive-compulsive symptom severity.
effect_claim_quote: Tendency to ruminate was positively correlated with the severity of OC symptoms and particularly with obsessive rumination, even after controlling for depression.
original_title: Relations between a ruminative thinking style and obsessive–compulsive symptoms in non-clinical samples
replication_title: Is a Ruminative Thinking Style Related to Obsessive-Compulsive Symptom Severity Beyond Its Associations with Depressive and Anxiety Symptom Severity?
replication_target_quote: We sought to replicate this association in a sample of individuals with OCD
outcome_quote: an RTS continued to predict the questionnaire, but not the interview measure of obsessive-compulsive symptom severity.
review_note: Original used nonclinical student questionnaires; follow-up used clinically diagnosed participants and found the association on a questionnaire but not an interview measure.

effect_name: Psychedelic experiences increase mind attribution
effect_claim: After a psychedelic experience, people attribute more mental awareness to living and nonliving things.
effect_claim_quote: attribution of consciousness to various entities increases.
original_title: A Single Belief-Changing Psychedelic Experience Is Associated With Increased Attribution of Consciousness to Living and Non-living Entities
replication_title: Psychedelic Experiences Increase Mind Perception but do not Change Atheist-Believer Status: A Prospective Longitudinal Study
replication_target_quote: Replicating previous findings, we observed increases in mind perception
outcome_quote: we observed increases in mind perception across a variety of living and non-living targets (e.g. plants, rocks).
review_note: Original retrospective survey asked people with a belief-changing experience; replication prospectively followed people planning psilocybin use.

effect_name: One social threat blunts response to another
effect_claim: Experiencing one social threat reduces the later response to a different social threat.
effect_claim_quote: Both effects were significantly reduced when the exclusion was preceded by preexposure to a loss of control
original_title: From Loss of Control to Social Exclusion: ERP Effects of Preexposure to a Social Threat in the Cyberball Paradigm
replication_title: Preexposure to one social threat alters responses to another social threat: Behavioral and electrophysiological evidence
replication_target_quote: A recent Cyberball study has indicated that the experience of loss of control can affect how people process subsequent social exclusion.
outcome_quote: these effects were significantly reduced by the preexposure to an independent social threat (here: social exclusion).
review_note: Conceptual reverse-order test: original loss of control before exclusion; replication exclusion before loss of control. The P3 and self-report reduction generalized; continuity effects differed.

effect_name: Health outranks economy in Brazilian pandemic perceptions
effect_claim: In Brazilian pandemic perceptions, health and social distancing concerns are more salient than economic concerns.
effect_claim_quote: Brazilian society privileged prophylaxis and health, via social isolation, to the detriment of the country’s economic preservation.
original_title: Universalists or Utilitarianists? The Social Representation of COVID-19 Pandemic in Brazil
replication_title: Sustainability and the Social Representation of the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Missing Link
replication_target_quote: our aim is to replicate a previous study carried out in Brazil in mid-2020
outcome_quote: categories such as economy and employment and changes and the new normal were mentioned less.
review_note: A later 2021 Brazilian sample placed politics, distancing, death, and fear centrally while economy remained peripheral; broader representation changed.

effect_name: Menstrual cycle and speech disfluency
effect_claim: Women produce more speech disfluencies at premenstruation than at ovulation.
effect_claim_quote: The mean total frequency of the women's speech disfluencies produced at premenstruation was significantly greater than the mean total of their speech disfluencies produced at ovulation.
original_title: Speech Fluency Fluctuations during the Menstrual Cycle
replication_title: Replication of “Speech Fluency Fluctuations during the Menstrual Cycle”
replication_target_quote: 20 women read contexual material aloud at ovulation (when the typical woman experiences her greatest feelings of well-being) and at premenstrution (when she experiences a significant increase in anxiety level).
outcome_quote: They were no less fluent at premenstruation than at ovulation.
review_note: The original used extemporaneous speech; the replication used reading aloud, so this is a changed-task conceptual test.
original_journal: Journal of Speech and Hearing Research

effect_name: Mother child mediated learning and resilience
effect_claim: Mother-child mediated learning strategies predict psychological resilience and cognitive modifiability in children with learning disabilities.
effect_claim_quote: The findings showed that mother-child MLE strategies, HOME, and socio-economic level contributed significantly to prediction of psychological resilience (78%) and cognitive modifiability (51%).
original_title: The effects of mother‐child mediated learning strategies on psychological resilience and cognitive modifiability of boys with learning disability
replication_title: The Effects of Mother-Child Mediated Learning Strategies on Cognitive Modifiability and Psychological Resilience of Children With Learning Disabilities: A Replication of Tzuriel and Shomron’s Study (2018) With Nigerian Children
replication_target_quote: This study determined the effects of mother-child mediated learning (MCML) strategies on the psychological resilience (PR) and cognitive modifiability (CM) of children with learning disabilities (LD) using a structural equation modeling (SEM) approach.
outcome_quote: MCML had a significant effect on the PR as well as CM of children with LD.
review_note: Original studied boys; replication includes boys and girls in Nigeria. Neither abstract gives a direction for the separate MLE coefficient.

effect_name: Alternative reinforcement and resistance to extinction
effect_claim: Adding reinforcers independent of the target response increases that response’s resistance to extinction.
effect_claim_quote: Resistance to satiation and extinction, in contrast, was positively related to the overall rate of reinforcement in the component.
original_title: ALTERNATIVE REINFORCEMENT INCREASES RESISTANCE TO CHANGE: PAVLOVIAN OR OPERANT CONTINGENCIES?
replication_title: Additional free reinforcers increase persistence of problem behavior in a clinical context: A partial replication of laboratory findings
replication_target_quote: Results of several investigations have shown that alternative reinforcement can increase the resistance to change of a target response during extinction.
outcome_quote: For 2 out of 3 participants, problem behavior tended to be more resistant to extinction following periods in which additional fixed-time reinforcers were delivered.
review_note: Original was pigeon key pecking; partial clinical replication tests human problem behavior and supports the effect in two of three participants.
original_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior
replication_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

effect_name: Dyadic complex skill training efficiency
effect_claim: Dyadic practice achieves equivalent complex skill performance to individual training with half the training resources.
effect_claim_quote: Trainer time and resources were half for the dyadic group, and performance was equivalent.
original_title: A dyadic protocol for training complex skills
replication_title: A Dyadic Protocol for Training Complex Skills: A Replication Using Female Participants
replication_target_quote: the present study investigated the generalizability of the effectiveness and efficiency gains to women.
outcome_quote: women trained in the AIM-dyad condition performed as well as those trained in the individual condition.
review_note: Original sample was undergraduates; replication explicitly tests women.
original_journal: Human Factors The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
replication_journal: Human Factors The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society

effect_name: Teasing and adolescent body disturbance
effect_claim: A history of weight related teasing is associated with body dissatisfaction and eating disturbance in adolescent girls.
effect_claim_quote: teasing history was significantly related to the development of body image and eating disturbance.
original_title: Development of body image, eating disturbance, and general psychological functioning in female adolescents: Covariance structure modeling and longitudinal investigations
replication_title: Development of body image, eating disturbance, and general psychological functioning in adolescent females: a replication using covariance structure modeling in an Australian sample
replication_target_quote: The current study is a follow up to a covariance structure modeling (CSM) investigation of predictors of body image, eating dysfunction, and general psychological functioning in U.S. adolescent females.
outcome_quote: The results support previous research indicating that teasing and body dissatisfaction are risk factors for the development of eating disturbances.
review_note: Replication uses an Australian adolescent sample and covariance structure modeling.

effect_name: CBT for PTSD in severe mental illness
effect_claim: Individual cognitive behavioral treatment reduces PTSD diagnoses in people with severe mental illness.
effect_claim_quote: Clinical outcomes were good, with reductions in PTSD diagnoses, based on the Clinician Administered PTSD Scale (CAPS), from 100% at baseline to 64% at post-treatment and 50% at three-month follow-up.
original_title: Cognitive-Behavioral Treatmenzt of PTSD in Severe Mental Illness: Results of a Pilot Study
replication_title: Cognitive-Behavioral Treatment of PTSD in Severe Mental Illness: Pilot Study Replication in an Ethnically Diverse Population
replication_target_quote: A parent study conducted in New Hampshire examined the effects of a 12- to 16-week cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) intervention for PTSD among people with SMI.
outcome_quote: Results showed high levels of retention in treatment and improvement at three and six months posttreatment in PTSD.
review_note: Both are small uncontrolled pilots; later sample is ethnically diverse and urban.

effect_name: Social behavior training in deaf children
effect_claim: A multifaceted training program increases appropriate social behavior in children with severe language disabilities.
effect_claim_quote: Results showed a functional relationship between introduction of the training procedure and increases in percentage of appropriate target behaviors for all 9 children.
original_title: EFFECTS OF A MULTIFACETED TRAINING PROCEDURE ON THE ACQUISITION AND GENERALIZATION OF SOCIAL BEHAVIORS IN LANGUAGE‐DISABLED DEAF CHILDREN
replication_title: EFFECTS OF A MULTIFACETED TRAINING PROCEDURE ON THE SOCIAL BEHAVIORS OF HEARING‐IMPAIRED CHILDREN WITH SEVERE LANGUAGE DISABILITIES: A REPLICATION
replication_target_quote: The effectiveness of a training package on the social behaviors of 20 hearing-impaired children with severe language disabilities was assessed.
outcome_quote: Results showed that the training package was effective in increasing greeting, turn waiting, initiating interaction, and giving help and these effects were maintained over several weeks.
review_note: Training package differs in implementation, but target social behaviors and population substantially overlap.

effect_name: Feedback reception skills training
effect_claim: Training employees to receive feedback improves their appropriate feedback receiving behavior.
effect_claim_quote: The results showed that participants were able to acquire and maintain appropriate feedback receiving behavior.
original_title: Teaching Employees How to Receive Feedback: A Preliminary Investigation
replication_title: Teaching Appropriate Feedback Reception Skills Using Computer-based Instruction: A Systematic Replication
replication_target_quote: The current study investigated the efficacy of training individuals to receive feedback in an appropriate manner using computer-based instruction (CBI).
outcome_quote: All three participants demonstrated increases in accuracy of appropriate feedback behaviors following CBI.
review_note: Original used in-person behavioral skills training; later systematic replication used computer instruction.

effect_name: Token reinforcement and disruptive classroom behavior
effect_claim: A classroom token reinforcement program reduces disruptive behavior in children.
effect_claim_quote: With the introduction of the token reinforcement program, an abrupt reduction in deviant behavior occurred.
original_title: Behavior Modification of an Adjustment Class: A Token Reinforcement Program
replication_title: A TOKEN REINFORCEMENT PROGRAM IN A PUBLIC SCHOOL: A REPLICATION AND SYSTEMATIC ANALYSIS1
replication_target_quote: When the Token Reinforcement Program was introduced, the frequency of disruptive behavior declined in five of the six remaining children.
outcome_quote: Withdrawal of the Token Reinforcement Program increased disruptive behavior in these five children, and reinstatement of the Token Reinforcement Program reduced disruptive behavior in four of these five.
review_note: Later classroom study replicates the core decrease and also tests withdrawal; original generalization result did not repeat and is outside this paired claim.

effect_name: Active error correction and word learning
effect_claim: Having students repeat the correct response after an error improves later recall compared with teacher modeling alone.
effect_claim_quote: For all 6 students, the active student response error-correction procedure resulted in more words read correctly during instruction, same-day tests, next-day tests, 2-week maintenance tests, and generality tests (words read in sentences).
original_title: EFFECTS OF ACTIVE STUDENT RESPONSE DURING ERROR CORRECTION ON THE ACQUISITION, MAINTENANCE, AND GENERALIZATION OF SIGHT WORDS BY STUDENTS WITH DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES
replication_title: EFFECTS OF ACTIVE STUDENT RESPONSE DURING ERROR CORRECTION ON THE ACQUISITION, MAINTENANCE, AND GENERALIZATION OF SCIENCE VOCABULARY BY ELEMENTARY STUDENTS: A SYSTEMATIC REPLICATION
replication_target_quote: We compared active student response (ASR) error correction and no-response (NR) error correction while teaching science terms to 5 elementary students.
outcome_quote: ASR error correction was superior on each of the study's seven dependent variables.
review_note: Original taught sight words; replication taught science vocabulary with the same active versus no-response correction.

effect_name: Preschool Life Skills increases learned skills
effect_claim: Teaching the Preschool Life Skills curriculum increases preschoolers' use of classroom social and communication skills.
effect_claim_quote: more than four-fold increase in preschool life skills.
original_title: EVALUATION OF A CLASSWIDE TEACHING PROGRAM FOR DEVELOPING PRESCHOOL LIFE SKILLS
replication_title: Preschool Life Skills: A Systematic Replication with Children with Developmental Disabilities
replication_target_quote: adaptations made to the original preschool life skills curriculum
outcome_quote: skill acquisition with all nine participants
review_note: Original taught typically developing children classwide; follow-up adapted the curriculum for nine children with developmental disabilities.

effect_name: Equalized-cost schedules and reinforcement maximization
effect_claim: When response costs are equalized across concurrent schedules, animals favor the schedule that maximizes reinforcement.
effect_claim_quote: The bias toward the latter component predicted by maximization theory was found.
original_title: MATCHING AND MAXIMIZING WITH CONCURRENT RATIO‐INTERVAL SCHEDULES
original_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior
replication_title: MORE ON CONCURRENT INTERVAL‐RATIO SCHEDULES: A REPLICATION AND REVIEW
replication_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior
replication_target_quote: To evaluate this hypothesis, pigeons were tested in a procedure in which interval and ratio schedules had equal response costs.
outcome_quote: Pigeons did not maximize rate of reinforcement on this procedure. Instead, their times spent on the alternative schedules matched the relative rates of reinforcement
review_note: Follow-up used a related variable-time versus variable-ratio-time schedule with equalized response costs and found matching rather than the original maximizing bias.

effect_name: Connotatively mismatched colors slow naming
effect_claim: People name ink colors more slowly when a word and its color have conflicting emotional connotations.
effect_claim_quote: color-naming speed is slower for inconsistent than for consistent color-word combinations
original_title: The Color-Word Connotative Incongruity Effect
replication_title: Color-Word Connotative Incongruity: A Replication
replication_target_quote: The previously reported effect of slower color-naming speed for connotatively inconsistent color-word combinatios was investigated.
outcome_quote: As before, the effect was found when connotatively consistent cards were presented for color naming before connotatively inconsistent cards.
review_note: Replication found the effect only when consistent cards came before inconsistent cards; outcome applies to that tested order.

effect_name: Audience laughter improves speaker evaluations
effect_claim: People evaluate a speaker more favorably when an audience laughs at the jokes in the speech.
effect_claim_quote: They preferred the speaker who elicited laughter
original_title: Audience's Response to Jokes in Speeches with and without Recorded Laughs
replication_title: Evaluative Responses to Jokes in Informative Speech with and without Laughter by an Audience: A Partial Replication
replication_target_quote: Evaluative Responses to Jokes in Informative Speech with and without Laughter by an Audience: A Partial Replication
outcome_quote: Mean responses of 39 students shown a videotaped speech with laughter were higher than those of 33 students viewing the speech without laughter
review_note: Original noted a speaker-order interaction; replication contrasted videotaped speeches with versus without audience laughter.

effect_name: American and Chinese college dating norms
effect_claim: American college students report more liberal dating attitudes and earlier dating than Chinese college students.
effect_claim_quote: American college students generally entertain a liberal attitude towards dating, tend to date young
original_title: Dating attitudes and behaviors of American and Chinese college students
replication_title: Dating attitudes and behaviors of American and Chinese college students: A partial replication
replication_target_quote: One such study from nearly two decades ago found more liberal attitudes and behavior regarding dating among American college students compared to their relatively conservative Chinese counterparts.
outcome_quote: The American students continue to use a dating script that is far more liberal. They also initiate the dating stage at much younger ages.
review_note: New U.S. and Chinese university samples were assessed roughly two decades later; broader courtship differences persisted.

effect_name: Facial muscle responses distinguish depression
effect_claim: Facial muscle patterns during imagined emotions distinguish depressed from nondepressed people.
effect_claim_quote: facial expression patterns differentiate depressed from nondepressed subjects.
original_title: Facial Muscle Patterning to Affective Imagery in Depressed and Nondepressed Subjects
replication_title: Facial Muscle Electromyography in Depressed and Nondepressed Hospitalized Subjects: A Partial Replication
replication_target_quote: Previous investigators have observed differences in the facial EMG patterns of depressed and nondepressed subjects who were not hospitalized
outcome_quote: The depressed and nondepressed subjects could not be differentiated on the basis of muscle activity
review_note: Original participants were not hospitalized; follow-up studied hospitalized depressed and nondepressed people, a material population change.

effect_name: Lunar phase does not predict hockey aggression
effect_claim: Lunar cycles do not predict aggressive penalties in ice hockey games.
effect_claim_quote: support for lunar influence was not forthcoming.
original_title: LUNAR INFLUENCES ON HUMAN AGGRESSION
original_journal: Social Behavior and Personality An International Journal
replication_title: LUNAR CYCLES AND HUMAN AGGRESSION: A REPLICATION
replication_journal: Social Behavior and Personality An International Journal
replication_target_quote: tests of a lunar-aggression hypothesis using the aggressive penalties awarded in ice hockey over a season of competition.
outcome_quote: Interpersonal aggression was found to be unrelated to either the synodic or anomalistic cycles
review_note: Both papers used a season of hockey penalties; this is replication of an absence, not a claim of equivalent aggression on every lunar phase.

effect_name: Fathers rate own mathematical intelligence higher
effect_claim: Fathers estimate their own mathematical and spatial intelligence more highly than mothers do.
effect_claim_quote: males (fathers) rated themselves as more intelligent on mathematical and spatial intelligence than females (mothers)
original_title: Parents’ estimates of their own and their children's multiple intelligences
replication_title: Sex Differences in Parents' Estimations of their Own and their Children's Multiple Intelligences: A Portuguese Replication
replication_target_quote: Sex Differences in Parents' Estimations of their Own and their Children's Multiple Intelligences: A Portuguese Replication
outcome_quote: Men's self-estimates were not significantly higher than women's on any of the 11 estimates.
review_note: The original son-versus-daughter rating pattern partly recurred; verdict concerns only the parent self-rating sex difference.

effect_name: Recorded teacher messages improve school performance
effect_claim: Daily recorded messages from teachers to parents improve students' academic performance.
effect_claim_quote: the inclusion of academic information in the daily message resulted in improved academic performance by every student in the class
original_title: Improving Parent-Teacher Communication through Recorded Telephone Messages1
replication_title: Improving Parent-Teacher Communication through Recorded Telephone Messages: Systematic Replication in a Special Education Classroom
replication_target_quote: daily recorded telephone message as a communications link between parents and the students' teacher.
outcome_quote: three of the six students' spelling performance improved as a function of the message system
review_note: Original regular first-grade class reported gains for all 21 students; follow-up special-education class found spelling gains in three of six.

effect_name: Borderline psychotherapy and symptom improvement
effect_claim: Patients with borderline personality disorder improve across symptoms and functioning after a year of structured outpatient psychotherapy.
effect_claim_quote: The subjects showed statistically significant improvement from the initial assessment to the end of the year of follow-up on every measure.
original_title: An outcome study of psychotherapy for patients with borderline personality disorder
replication_title: Borderline personality disorder treated with the conversational model: a replication study
replication_target_quote: original cohort previously reported by Stevenson and Meares
outcome_quote: The rate and degree of improvement in the later cohort are very similar to the original 1992 cohort
review_note: Original study was an uncontrolled treated cohort; follow-up compared another cohort with treatment-as-usual controls.

effect_name: Dyslexia changes phase of speech entrainment
effect_claim: Children with developmental dyslexia show a different phase of low-frequency neural entrainment to rhythmic speech than other children.
effect_claim_quote: significant group difference in the preferred phase of entrainment in the delta band
original_title: Neural entrainment to rhythmic speech in children with developmental dyslexia
replication_title: Neural entrainment to speech and nonspeech in dyslexia: Conceptual replication and extension of previous investigations
replication_target_quote: conceptually replicate previous studies on auditory entrainment in dyslexia
outcome_quote: We failed to observe any of the significant group differences that had previously been reported in delta, theta and gamma frequency bands
review_note: Follow-up found some differences in amplitude cross-correlation for nonspeech noise, but not the original phase-of-speech entrainment contrast.

effect_name: Tailored biofeedback helps psychophysiologic insomnia
effect_claim: Biofeedback matched to the initial tension profile improves sleep in people with psychophysiologic insomnia.
effect_claim_quote: Those treated with the biofeedback that seemed appropriate for their specific deficiencies showed significant sleep improvements
original_title: Treating Psychophysiologic Insomnia With Biofeedback
replication_title: The treatment of psychophysiologic insomnia with biofeedback: A replication study
replication_target_quote: To replicate a previous study, 16 psychophysiological insomniacs
outcome_quote: tense and anxious insomniacs benefited only from Theta feedback but not from SMR feedback, while those who were relaxed at intake but still could not sleep benefited only from SMR but not from Theta feedback.
review_note: Follow-up compared theta with sensorimotor-rhythm feedback and repeated a subgroup-specific benefit; original had additional arms and no universal benefit versus controls.

effect_name: Pornography predicts later extramarital-sex attitudes
effect_claim: Among married adults, earlier pornography use predicts more favorable later attitudes toward extramarital sex.
effect_claim_quote: prior pornography consumption was correlated with more positive subsequent extramarital sex attitudes in both samples
original_title: More than a dalliance? Pornography consumption and extramarital sex attitudes among married U.S. adults.
replication_title: Pornography Consumption and Extramarital Sex Attitudes Among Married U.S. Adults: Longitudinal Replication
replication_target_quote: replicative of the Wright et al.
outcome_quote: the association between baseline pornography consumption and interindividual change in extramarital sex attitudes was not significant.
review_note: Both studies used longitudinal attitudes; the follow-up reports a null adjusted association.

effect_name: Eye movements reduce later visual-memory accessibility
