effect_claim: Gender differences appear across the ten aspects beneath the Big Five personality domains.
effect_claim_quote: significant gender differences appearing in both aspects of every Big Five trait
original_title: Gender Differences in Personality across the Ten Aspects of the Big Five
original_authors: Weisberg YJ, Deyoung CG, Hirsh JB.
replication_title: Revisiting gender differences in 10 aspects of personality
replication_target_quote: This study aimed to replicate and extend the work of Weisberg et al. (2011)
outcome_quote: Overall, the results largely replicated Weisberg et al.'s findings, while also revealing meaningful contextual variations
review_note: Corrected original to Weisberg et al. 2011, not the machine-linked personality paper. Brazilian replication supports many aspect-level differences but reports cross-cultural divergences and age/education moderation; mixed for the all-aspect pattern.

effect_name: A general psychopathology factor explains comorbidity across disorders
effect_claim: A shared general psychopathology factor helps explain the structure of multiple psychiatric disorders beyond narrower symptom groups.
effect_claim_quote: Psychiatric disorders were initially explained by three higher-order factors (Internalizing, Externalizing, and Thought Disorder) but explained even better with one General Psychopathology dimension.
original_title: The p Factor: One General Psychopathology Factor in the Structure of Psychiatric Disorders?
original_authors: Caspi A, Houts RM, Belsky DW, Goldman-Mellor SJ, Harrington H, Israel S, Meier MH, Ramrakha S, Shalev I, Poulton R, Moffitt TE.
replication_title: The Structure of Psychopathology in Adolescence
replication_target_quote: This study aimed to replicate a study by Caspi and colleagues
outcome_quote: the structure of psychopathology is best characterized by a model including a general factor, in addition to smaller internalizing and externalizing factors
review_note: Corrected original to Caspi et al. 2014. Later adolescent self/parent data support a general factor alongside narrower internalizing and externalizing factors; conceptual replication with different age/sample measures.

effect_name: Positive affect and trait anger predict perceived workplace incivility
effect_claim: Positive affect and trait anger are the strongest personality predictors of how uncivil people perceive ambiguous workplace behavior to be.
effect_claim_quote: PA and trait anger explained the most variance in incivility perceptions
original_title: It Happened, or You Thought It Happened? Examining the Perception of Workplace Incivility Based on Personality Characteristics
replication_target_quote: replicate the findings from Sliter, Withrow, and Jex (2015)
outcome_quote: In both replications, positive affect and trait anger were the strongest predictors
review_note: The later proceedings abstract explicitly names Sliter, Withrow, and Jex (2015) and reports two replications. The author-uploaded primary article abstract confirms the named original DOI and the same effect. Later abstract contains a grammatical omission after “workplace”; outcome quote stops before it. Psychology of workplace incivility is within scope.
replication_title: Replications Further Examining Workplace Incivility Perceptions based on Personality Characteristics

effect_name: Memory of a pairing supports transfer of negative valence
effect_claim: Negative pairings reduce how pleasant a neutral item feels, with this transfer of valence depending on episodic memory for the pairing.
effect_claim_quote: transfer of valence is contingent on episodic memory
original_title: Transfer of negative valence in an episodic memory task
replication_target_quote: Palombo, D. J., Elizur, L., Tuen, Y. J., Te, A. A., & Madan, C. R. (2021)
outcome_quote: We successfully replicated the EC effect and did not find an association between EC and episodic memory
review_note: The later Cognition & Emotion abstract explicitly cites the complete Palombo et al. (2021) original identity and tests single-trial evaluative conditioning in a VR paradigm. It reproduced the valence-transfer effect but not its association with episodic memory. This row is scoped to the memory-dependence component and labels the overall outcome mixed.
replication_title: Evaluative conditioning using virtual reality events
Religiosity and Support for Killing Animals: A Replication of the Curvilinear Relationship
effect_name: Moderate religiosity and lower support for killing animals
effect_claim: Support for killing animals was lower at moderate religiosity than at low or very high religiosity.
effect_claim_quote: The results indicated that, in support of our hypothesis, the relationship between religiosity and support for killing animals is curvilinear, as moderate levels of religiosity were related to less support for killing animals.
original_title: Religiosity and Support for Killing Animals: Evidence of a Curvilinear Relationship
replication_target_quote: Lifshin et al. (2018) theorized and found that this relationship may in fact be curvilinear, as moderate levels of religiosity relate to less support for killing animals compared to low religiosity (atheism) or to high religiosity (religious extremism or fundamentalism).
outcome_quote: Findings supported the hypothesis and suggest that moderate religiosity and belief in God are associated with less negative attitudes toward animals than atheism and disbelief on the one hand, and religious extremism on the other.
review_note: Corrected original DOI from unrelated Lifshin 2017 study to explicitly cited Lifshin et al. 2018. Original abstract on author university site; replication publisher abstract is cached in frozen packet. Same curvilinear attitude effect, sample and measure are conceptual replication.

replication_title: Generality of Creativity across Performance Domains: A Replication
effect_name: Creativity shows little generality across performance domains
effect_claim: Creative performance scores across different kinds of products were not correlated after accounting for IQ and academic achievement.
effect_claim_quote: When the effects of IQ reading achievement, and math achievement were controlled through multiple regression analyses, creativity scores on the four tasks were not correlated.
original_title: Generality of creativity across performance domains
replication_target_quote: A replication of a 1991 study in which Baer questioned the importance of general creativity-thinking skills was conducted using a larger sample with a broader range of abilities, as suggested in a 1994 published review by Kogan.
outcome_quote: The correlation between these two measures of creativity was .19. This is similar to previous results.
review_note: 1994 paper explicitly calls itself a replication of Baer 1991. Both compare expert-rated creative products across performance domains. Replication weak correlation .19 deemed similar by authors; partial tasks were poems and stories.

replication_title: Ego depletion does not negatively impact novice sprinters’ start performance during a timed 20m all-out sprint
effect_name: Ego depletion increases false sprint starts for novices
effect_claim: After a demanding self-control task, athletes without track-and-field experience made more false starts in a sprint task than non-depleted controls.
effect_claim_quote: In line with our assumption, we found a significant interaction as there was only a significant increase in the number of false starts from T1 to T2 for the depletion group while this was not the case for the non-depletion group.
original_title: The influence of ego depletion on sprint start performance in athletes without track and field experience
replication_target_quote: the current study performed a conceptual replication of a previous study examining the effects of ego depletion on sprint start performance (i.e., Englert et al., 2015)
outcome_quote: The number of false starts decreased significantly with ego depletion, while sprint start reaction times and sprint finish times remained unaffected.
review_note: Corrected original DOI from a 2015 cycling study to expressly named Englert et al. 2015 novice sprint-start experiment. Later 20-m novice sprinter conceptual replication reports fewer false starts after depletion, opposite original direction.

effect_name: Instructive feedback elicits emergent verbal responses
effect_claim: Embedding feature statements in mastered listener trials increases untrained related verbal responses in children with autism.
effect_claim_quote: We observed increased correct responses for related verbal responses
original_title: Promoting the development of verbal responses using instructive feedback
replication_title: The Use of Instructive Feedback to Promote Emergent Tact and Intraverbal Control: A Replication
replication_target_quote: The current study replicated Frampton and Shillingsburg with two children with ASD
outcome_quote: The other participant emitted correct responses for secondary targets and emergent operants with the first set but not with the other two sets of stimuli
review_note: Later published paper is reviewed as its own DOI; no duplicate candidate alias is claimed. Exact original Frampton & Shillingsburg (2020) is named in the PubMed/PMC abstract. The procedure yielded responses across all three sets for one child, only the first set for the other, so mixed/idiosyncratic. Existing FORRT sibling for this original, DOI 10.1002/bin.1836, is a distinct successful study. Repository thesis manuscript: https://doi.org/10.12794/metadc1833527. It reports this same replication sample and is linked here, counted once.

effect_name: AND groups items while OR separates them in mental images
effect_claim: When matching language to pictures, people associate conjunctions with visually grouped items and disjunctions with visually separate items.
effect_claim_quote: reasoners associate conjunction descriptions with perceptually-dependent stimuli and disjunction descriptions with perceptually-independent stimuli
original_title: Gestalt Reasoning with Conjunctions and Disjunctions
replication_target_quote: Dumitru and Joergensen, 2016
outcome_quote: Response times highlight correlations between the Gestalt arity of connective simulations and visual attention patterns
review_note: The 2018 Frontiers in Psychology paper by the same authors explicitly names their 2016 Gestalt reasoning paper and says it seeks to replicate and extend the one-versus-two Gestalt finding in a language-picture task focused on visuospatial properties. Original 2016 primary PLOS fulltext/abstract states the perceptual grouping effect; later abstract reports compatible attention patterns. Conceptual extension, so successful at the broad grouping effect.
replication_title: Logical Connectives Modulate Attention to Simulations Evoked by the Constituents They Link Together

effect_name: Hypnosis simulation ability correlates with child hypnotic susceptibility
effect_claim: Children better able to simulate hypnosis score higher on a hypnotic susceptibility scale.
effect_claim_quote: a positive relationship between hypnotic susceptibility and the ability to stimulate hypnosis
original_title: Role playing and hypnotic susceptibility in children
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Role playing and hypnotic susceptibility in children: II. An extension and partial replication
replication_journal: International Journal of Clinical and Experimental Hypnosis
replication_target_quote: compared to a previous sample of 42 children who had received the same tests in reverse order
outcome_quote: Hypnotic Simulation, was uncorrelated with overall susceptibility in the present sample, unlike the previous one
review_note: Same original authors and nearly identical title; the later 1969 paper compares its 34-child sample with the original 42-child sample and reverses test order. Original author/publisher primary preview states positive hypnosis-simulation association; later abstract explicitly reports no overall association in new sample while dramatic acting was unrelated in both. This is failed for the specific simulation-susceptibility relationship.

replication_title: Patterns of Competence and Adjustment Among Adolescents from Authoritative, Authoritarian, Indulgent, and Neglectful Homes: A Replication in a Sample of Serious Juvenile Offenders
effect_name: Authoritative parenting predicts better adolescent adjustment
effect_claim: Adolescents reporting authoritative parents had higher competence and lower dysfunction than those reporting neglectful parents.
effect_claim_quote: Results indicate that adolescents who characterize their parents as authoritative score highest on measures of psychosocial competence and lowest on measures of psychological and behavioral dysfunction; the reverse is true for adolescents who describe their parents as neglectful.
original_title: Patterns of competence and adjustment among adolescents from authoritative, authoritarian, indulgent, and neglectful families
replication_target_quote: Patterns of Competence and Adjustment Among Adolescents from Authoritative, Authoritarian, Indulgent, and Neglectful Homes: A Replication in a Sample of Serious Juvenile Offenders
outcome_quote: juvenile offenders who describe their parents as authoritative are more psychosocially mature, more academically competent, less prone to internalized distress, and less prone to externalizing problems than their peers,whereas those who describe their parents as neglectful are less mature, less competent, and more troubled.
review_note: Corrected original DOI from longitudinal Steinberg et al. 1994 follow-up to 1991 Lamborn et al. original, which has same lead author as replication, nearly identical title, same four parenting categories and adjustment outcomes. Later study is a conceptual replication in juvenile offenders; target quote is exact later title.

replication_title: Critical Incident History Questionnaire Replication: Frequency and Severity of Trauma Exposure Among Officers From Small and Midsize Police Agencies
effect_name: Police rank injuring a colleague through error as most severe incident
effect_claim: Among Critical Incident History Questionnaire events, accidentally causing serious injury or death to a fellow officer received the highest mean severity rating.
effect_claim_quote: The item rated as most severe was “Making a mistake that led to the serious injury or death of a fellow officer” (M = 3.81,
original_title: Frequency and severity approaches to indexing exposure to trauma: The Critical Incident History Questionnaire for police officers
replication_target_quote: The purpose of this study was to replicate the CIHQ findings from Weiss et al.
outcome_quote: Making a mistake that kills or injures a colleague had the highest mean nomothetic severity rating in both studies.
review_note: Corrected original DOI from unrelated Weiss 2008 twin study. Original quote is from Table 1/results of original published paper PDF hosted by US Office for Victims of Crime, not abstract. Later article explicitly cites Weiss et al. 2010 DOI in publisher reference list and reports exact same highest-ranked severity item.

replication_title: Improving Social Behaviour and Academic Performance of a Secondary School Pupil through Self‐recording: a replication of Merrett and Blundell
effect_name: Classroom self-recording improves on-task behavior
effect_claim: Self-recording of classroom behavior increased on-task activity and reduced maladaptive behavior among secondary-school pupils.
effect_claim_quote: On-task behaviour increased whilst maladaptive responses were reduced and there was a pronounced improvement in the boy's attitude to school work.
original_title: Self-recording as a Means of Improving Classroom Behaviour in the Secondary School
replication_target_quote: Improving Social Behaviour and Academic Performance of a Secondary School Pupil through Self‐recording: a replication of Merrett and Blundell
outcome_quote: Inappropriate behaviour decreased whilst on‐task behaviour and the percentage of work completed correctly increased.
review_note: Corrected original DOI from McNamara 1979 to Merrett & Blundell 1982, explicitly named in later title. Original abstract is indexed by Scispace/EurekaMag with DOI and matches reported self-recording behavior effect. Later paper repeats pupil self-recording and finds same directional classroom outcomes. Original publisher DOI is cited as source URL.

effect_name: Vigilance response bias becomes more conservative over time
effect_claim: During a vigilance task, response bias shifts over time toward fewer responses, a change that can resemble declining perceptual sensitivity.
effect_claim_quote: Second, we present the results of an experiment that demonstrates that shifts in response bias (the observer's "willingness to respond") over time can masquerade as a loss in sensitivity.
original_title: A critical examination of the evidence for sensitivity loss in modern vigilance tasks.
replication_title: Can vigilance tasks be administered online? A replication and discussion.
replication_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Human Perception & Performance
replication_target_quote: The present study partially replicated the results of a newly developed online vigilance task (Thomson, Besner, & Smilek, 2016).
outcome_quote: response bias tended to shift toward more conservatism over time in the lure and standard conditions.
review_note: Same semantic vigilance task, recreated in laboratory; later author manuscript identifies Thomson et al. 2016 and finds the same more conservative response bias over time. Later sensitivity estimates differ by index, so this outcome applies only to response bias, not all original interpretations.

effect_name: Think manager, think male stereotype
effect_claim: Successful managers were rated as more similar to men than to women on stereotyped personality attributes.
effect_claim_quote: There was a significant resemblance between the mean ratings of men and managers, whereas there was no resemblance between women and managers.
original_title: The relationship between sex role stereotypes and requisite management characteristics
replication_title: Think scientists—Think male: Science and leadership are still more strongly associated with men than with women in Germany
replication_target_quote: we kept the original three conditions used by Schein (1973)
outcome_quote: We also found more overlap in stereotypes for men and managers versus women and managers.
review_note: Corrected original DOI from Heilman et al. 1989 to expressly named Schein 1973. Later Wiley paper states it retained Schein’s original three conditions and 92-item Descriptive Index, then reports stronger men-manager than women-manager stereotype overlap. It adds a scientist condition, but effect page targets only manager stereotype.

effect_name: Gambling disorder liability has a substantial genetic component
effect_claim: Twin analyses attributed substantial disordered gambling liability to genetic influences, with no detectable shared environmental component.
effect_claim_quote: The estimate of the proportion of variation in liability for DG due to genetic influences was 49.2% (95% confidence interval, 26.7-60.9). There was no evidence for shared environmental influences contributing to variation in DG liability.
original_title: Genetic and environmental influences on disordered gambling in men and women
replication_title: Genetic and environmental influences on gambling disorder liability: a replication and combined analysis of two twin studies
replication_authors: Davis, Slutske, Martin, Agrawal, and Lynskey
replication_target_quote: this did not significantly differ from the original study
outcome_quote: there was evidence for significant genetic (60%; 95% confidence interval (CI) 45-76%) and unique environmental (40%; 95% CI 24-56%), but not shared environmental contributions (0%; 95% CI 0-0%) to GD liability; this did not significantly differ from the original study.
review_note: Corrected machine link from Beaver et al. US adolescent twin study to the explicitly cited Slutske et al. 2010 original Australian Twin Registry study (same original sample of 4764 and original author among replication authors). Replication used a separate Australian twin cohort of 3292; genetic estimate 60% versus original 49.2%, no significant shared environment in either. Outcome quote uses lower GD threshold; higher thresholds were similar. Psychology/behavioral genetics scope. Replication published online 30 August 2018; issue dated 2019.

effect_name: Tetris after a trauma film reduces later intrusions
effect_claim: Playing Tetris shortly after a trauma film reduces intrusive memories during the following week.
effect_claim_quote: Results indicated that compared to the no-task condition, the "Tetris" condition produced a significant reduction in flashback frequency over 1-week.
original_title: Can playing the computer game "Tetris" reduce the build-up of flashbacks for trauma? A proposal from cognitive science
replication_title: Do Cognitive Tasks Reduce Intrusive-Memory Frequency After Exposure to Analogue Trauma? An Experimental Replication
replication_target_quote: Our study provides an independent replication study to test and verify findings that have primarily originated from a single research group.
outcome_quote: the cognitive task including Tetris was associated with fewer intrusions for the TFP compared with both the D-Corsi-intervention and control conditions
review_note: Corrected machine link from Lau-Zhu et al. 2019 to Holmes et al. 2009, the original Tetris-after-trauma-film experiment explicitly cited in the replication publisher references. Conceptual independent replication of the narrow Tetris versus no-task effect on one-week intrusion frequency, with a D-Corsi comparator; the reported Tetris reduction versus control matches the original. Multiple Holmes-group studies preceded the replica, so this row identifies the first demonstration rather than asserting an exact procedural repeat.

effect_name: Cannabis problems lie on a continuum
effect_claim: Cannabis dependence and related problems vary along a continuum rather than forming a distinct category.
effect_claim_quote: Both taxometric methods provided support for a dimensional structure of cannabis dependence
original_title: Pothead or pot smoker? a taxometric investigation of cannabis dependence
original_journal: Substance Abuse Treatment, Prevention, and Policy
replication_title: Replicating the Dimensional Structure of Cannabis Problems: A Taxometric Analysis
replication_target_quote: replicate a previous report of the dimensional structure of problems related to cannabis consumption
outcome_quote: All three procedures confirmed the continuous, dimensional nature of these cannabis problems
review_note: The later 2020 paper shares both original authors and explicitly replicates a previous taxometric report on cannabis dimensionality. Its OpenAlex reference list includes the exact 2006 Denson–Earleywine original (W2117458145). Original assessed DSM-IV dependence in NESARC; later assessed the Marijuana Problems Scale in more than 4,000 users, so this is conceptual across related measures. Later OpenAlex field Psychology; original indexed Medicine but studies a psychological latent construct.

effect_name: 16PF personality factors track Millon personality-disorder scales
effect_claim: Sixteen Personality Factor scores correlate with Millon personality-disorder concept scales.
effect_claim_quote: 10 of 11 correlations with the Millon were significant
original_title: Personality Disorder Concept Scales and 16 PF Dimensions
replication_title: Broad Factor Scales of the 16 PF Fifth Edition and Millon Personality Disorder Scales: A Replication
replication_target_quote: replication of the link between broad personality factors from the 16 PF and personality disorder scales based on Millon's typology of personality
outcome_quote: 15 of the 18 expectations were in the expected direction. Of these 10 were significant.
review_note: The later 1994 Psychological Reports paper lists DeLamatre–Schuerger 1992 among just two referenced works (OpenAlex W2010240006), shares author Schuerger, and expressly labels its 16PF–Millon association a replication. The original used 16PF primary scores and a clinical/student cross-validation; the later study uses the fifth-edition broad factors in students. Thus this is a conceptual replication of the association, not an identical scale or sample. Both OpenAlex works classify as Psychology/Clinical Psychology.

effect_name: Sexual word Stroop bias among sexual offenders
effect_claim: Sexual offenders showed greater Stroop interference for sexual words than non-offender controls.
effect_claim_quote: offenders convicted of both sexual and violent offences were significantly slower than undergraduates to color-name words relating to sexual offending
original_title: Processing Bias for Sexual Material: The Emotional Stroop and Sexual Offenders
replication_title: A modified Stroop task with sexual offenders: Replication of a study
replication_target_quote: The current study replicates and extends Smith and Waterman's results
outcome_quote: Both Smith and Waterman and the current study found significant differences between the sexual offenders and their non-offender comparison groups for the sexual bias scores.
review_note: Original article and directly targeted replication are exact Smith and Waterman 2004 versus Price/Hanson 2007. In the author-uploaded publisher PDF, both studies show sexual-word Stroop bias versus non-offender controls. Evidence is mixed because the crucial sexual-versus-other-offender contrast was not significant in either study or pooled, and the replica sexual offender group was slower for neutral words too. This is forensic psychology; source text is the actual published article uploaded by its coauthor.

effect_name: Tactile interference with trauma-report intrusions
effect_claim: Shaping plasticine while listening to a traumatic verbal report reduced later intrusive images relative to listening without a concurrent task.
effect_claim_quote: intrusion frequency was reduced in both the visuospatial and the verbal condition compared to the no task control condition.
original_title: “I see what you’re saying”: intrusive images from listening to a traumatic verbal report
replication_title: Can Listening to a Verbal Trauma Report Induce Intrusions? – Replication of a Randomized Trial
replication_target_quote: The present study aimed to replicate the findings of Krans et al. (Citation2010), which indicated that (1) intrusions can result from exposure to a purely verbal description of a traumatic event and (2) might be less likely to emerge if the listener is simultaneously engaging in a tactile task.
outcome_quote: the tactile task interfered with intrusion formation as indicated by the primary diary measure, but not the retrospective self-report.
review_note: Exact Krans 2010 procedural replication, preregistered as aspredicted #9865. Diary measure supported fewer intrusions, retrospective report did not; full text says a secondary intrusion provocation measure went in the opposite direction. Later OpenAlex primary topic Clinical Psychology, field Psychology.

effect_name: Mindfulness group clinical gains in psychosis
effect_claim: People with distressing psychosis showed improved clinical functioning after a six-session mindfulness group.
effect_claim_quote: There was a significant pre-post drop in scores on the CORE (z=−2.655, p=.008).
original_title: Mindfulness Groups for People with Psychosis
replication_title: Mindfulness Groups for Distressing Voices and Paranoia: A Replication and Randomized Feasibility Trial
replication_target_quote: to replicate clinical gains observed in one small uncontrolled study
outcome_quote: There were no significant differences between intervention and waiting-list participants. Secondary analyses combining both groups and comparing scores before and after mindfulness training revealed significant improvement in clinical functioning (p = .013)
review_note: Later randomized feasibility trial explicitly targets the Chadwick et al. 2005 small uncontrolled study. Replicated within-person improvement, but no significant randomized intervention-versus-waitlist difference. Later OpenAlex primary topic Mindfulness and Compassion Interventions, field Psychology.

effect_name: Negative emotional inertia and depressive symptoms
effect_claim: Greater persistence of negative affect during a standardized film sequence was associated with more depressive symptoms.
effect_claim_quote: depressive symptoms were independently associated with higher inertia of negative affect in the lab
original_title: Affect dynamics in relation to depressive symptoms: variable, unstable or inert?
replication_title: Emotional Inertia is Associated with Lower Well-Being when Controlling for Differences in Emotional Context
replication_target_quote: We have previously assessed emotional inertia in response to a standardized sequence of stimuli and found a positive association between inertia of negative emotions (NE) and depressive symptoms, supporting the view that endogenously caused emotional inflexibility is related to lower well-being (Koval et al., 2013).
outcome_quote: emotional inertia correlated more consistently with negative indicators (e.g., depressive symptoms) than positive indicators (e.g., life satisfaction) of well-being
review_note: Later authors explicitly identify Koval et al. 2013 as their own prior standardized-stimulus emotional inertia study, cite its DOI 10.1037/a0033579, and describe the same negative inertia/depressive-symptom association. Later two studies find the association with negative well-being. Later OpenAlex W2267996957 primary field Psychology. Original proposed broad personality meta-analysis was the wrong link.

replication_title: Childhood trauma has dose‐effect relationship with dropping out from psychotherapeutic treatment for bulimia nervosa: A replication
effect_name: Childhood trauma dose effect on bulimia psychotherapy dropout
effect_claim: Among women treated for bulimia, more childhood trauma was associated with higher risk of dropping out of psychotherapy.
effect_claim_quote: Experiences of childhood trauma had a dose-effect relationship with dropping out.
original_title: Do broken relationships in childhood relate to bulimic women breaking off psychotherapy in adulthood?
replication_target_quote: The primary goal of this study was to replicate the finding that experiences of childhood trauma have a dose-effect relationship with dropping out from psychotherapeutic treatment for bulimia nervosa.
outcome_quote: The dose-effect relationship between experiences of childhood trauma and dropping out was confirmed.
review_note: Corrected to Mahon et al. March 2001 original, 111-patient cohort; September 2001 later Mahon study tested an independent 114-patient cohort. Same lead authors, unique earlier cohort and identical trauma-dropout claim. Original date is conservative end-of-March bound because publisher gives month only; replication first published online July 6 (Crossref).

effect_name: Honesty information raises facial attractiveness ratings
effect_claim: Describing a photographed person as honest, rather than dishonest, increased ratings of that person’s facial attractiveness.
effect_claim_quote: the honest target, as opposed to the dishonest target, was seen as being more fit and in better health and as having a face that looked more kind, feminine, and attractive
original_title: You are honest, therefore I like you and find you attractive
replication_title: Good conduct makes your face attractive: The effect of personality perception on facial attractiveness judgments
replication_target_quote: We conducted four experiments to replicate and extend the results of Paunonen’s study
outcome_quote: We successfully replicated Paunonen’s [60] honesty premium effect in Experiments 1 and 2 (but not in Experiment 4).
review_note: Corrected wrong body-size original to Paunonen 2006, explicitly targeted and DOI-cited in the PLOS replication article. Same honesty-description manipulation and facial attractiveness rating. Experiments 1 and 2 reproduced the premium in Japanese and diverse-age samples; Experiment 4 did not, so mixed. Later paper OpenAlex primary Field Psychology; no existing pair/FORRT verdict.

effect_name: Happy-expression speech perception advantage
effect_claim: Happily expressed audiovisual speech was recognized better than speech expressed with other emotions.
effect_claim_quote: happy expressions tended to improve speech performance on both sides of the face relative to all other emotions
original_title: Audiovisual speech from emotionally expressive and lateralized faces
replication_title: Visual and acoustic information supporting a happily expressed speech-in-noise advantage
replication_target_quote: a replication of previous research with the happily expressed speech advantage was completed with a novel inclusion of a learning paradigm
outcome_quote: the happily expressed speech advantage persisted despite constraints to the amount of frequency modulation and with distortions to the talker's face
review_note: Later publisher abstract explicitly calls its happy speech advantage test a replication of previous research. Same lead author Gordon, paper references Gordon and Hibberts 2011 (DOI verified), and acknowledgment credits Mary Hibberts for her work on the precursor of this research. The original and later papers both compare happy versus other speech expressions; later adds noise and acoustic/visual manipulations. Later OpenAlex W2238485881 primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Sad child witnesses rated most credible
effect_claim: In mock interviews about physical abuse, children displaying sadness received the highest credibility ratings compared with neutral, angry, or positive displays.
effect_claim_quote: Highest ratings were found for sad condition, and lowest for positive condition.
original_title: Expressed Emotions and Perceived Credibility of Child Mock Victims Disclosing Physical Abuse
replication_title: The Emotional Child Witness Effect Survives Presentation Mode
replication_target_quote: In the present study, mock police interviews were carried out with female child actors, role-playing the victims of physical abuse by their stepfather, telling the same story with four emotional expressions (neutral, sad, angry, or positive).
outcome_quote: Replicating previous results, the "sad" expression elicited the highest credibility ratings across all modes of presentations.
review_note: Corrected wrong male-suspect original to Wessel, Magnussen, and Melinder 2013 child physical-abuse witness study. The three original authors coauthored the later paper, which repeats the same child witness scenario, emotional-expression manipulation, credibility rating, and sad-highest outcome across three presentation modes. Original quote from original author's published-paper upload; later abstract from PubMed. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology. No existing pair or FORRT outcome.

effect_name: Valuing happiness correlates with depressive symptoms
effect_claim: In U.S. samples, people who placed greater value on feeling happy reported more depressive symptoms.
effect_claim_quote: valuing happiness was associated with increased depressive symptoms in a community sample with remitted major depressive disorder
original_title: Desperately Seeking Happiness: Valuing Happiness Is Associated With Symptoms and Diagnosis of Depression
original_journal: Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology
replication_title: Wanting to Be Happy but Not Knowing How: Poor Attentional Control and Emotion-Regulation Abilities Mediate the Association Between Valuing Happiness and Depression
replication_target_quote: The present study first sought to replicate the previously reported associations between valuing happiness and depressive symptoms
outcome_quote: In both studies, we found that valuing happiness was related to increased depression
review_note: Corrected bipolar-disorder original to Ford et al. 2014, explicitly cited by the later Springer paper as the U.S. depression association it replicated. Same valuing-happiness scale and depressive-symptoms association in UK university samples; two later studies positive. Original abstract from UC Berkeley author archive, later abstract and citation from open-access Springer publisher. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology. No existing pair/FORRT verdict.

replication_title: A Multilab Replication of the Ego Depletion Effect
effect_name: Stroop-induced ego depletion on antisaccade self-control
effect_claim: An incongruent Stroop task produced a significant ego-depletion effect on subsequent antisaccade performance.
effect_claim_quote: we preregistered the current experiment with the aim to examine whether there would be an ego depletion effect when the Stroop task is used as the depleting task. The results demonstrated a significant ego depletion effect.
original_title: The ego could be depleted, providing initial exertion is depleting: A preregistered experiment of the ego depletion effect
replication_target_quote: we preregistered and conducted a high-powered multilab project to replicate the experiment by Dang and colleagues in a standardized way.
outcome_quote: Data from 12 labs across the globe ( N = 1,775) revealed a small and significant ego depletion effect, d = 0.10.
review_note: Later primary full text explicitly identifies Dang et al. 2017 Stroop-antisaccade study and contrasts original g=0.48 with later significant d=0.10. Original author-university abstract verified; later full text and abstract verified on PMC.

replication_title: Evaluating the effectiveness of a consumer delivered anti-stigma program: Replication with graduate-level helping professionals.
effect_name: In Our Own Voice improves mental-health knowledge and attitudes
effect_claim: Undergraduates who attended the In Our Own Voice presentation improved their mental-health knowledge and attitudes more than controls.
effect_claim_quote: Results indicated that the IOOV group showed significant positive change across time, as well as significantly greater improvement than a control group in their knowledge and attitude scores on all measures.
original_title: Evaluating the effectiveness of a consumer-provided mental health recovery education presentation
replication_target_quote: replicating a previous study with undergraduates.
outcome_quote: Paired samples t-tests showed increases in attitude (p < .001), knowledge (p < .05), and social distance (p < .001).
review_note: Later paper explicitly repeats undergraduate IOOV study; OpenAlex indexed references confirm it cites Wood and Wahl 2006 (W2091521027). Same program and knowledge/attitude measures, later sample is MSW students with no control group.

effect_name: Work overload and role ambiguity dominate technostress
effect_claim: Work overload and role ambiguity are the strongest workplace technostress stressors.
effect_claim_quote: Work overload and role ambiguity are found to be the two most dominant stressors
original_title: Technostress: Technological Antecedents and Implications1
replication_title: Replication of Technostress: Technological Antecedents and Implications in the Post-Pandemic Context
replication_journal: Communications of the Association for Information Systems
replication_target_quote: This study is a conceptual replication of the work of Ayyagari et al. (2011)
outcome_quote: work overload and role ambiguity are still the two most significant stressors
review_note: The later study repeats the Ayyagari technostress model in Brazilian workers and reports the same two dominant stressors; ten of sixteen model hypotheses agreed.

effect_name: Physiological signals anticipate future emotional stimuli
effect_claim: Physiological measures showed pre-stimulus responses associated with future emotional pictures.
effect_claim_quote: found evidence of non-local intuition in both entrepreneurs and non-entrepreneurs
original_title: Non-local intuition in entrepreneurs and non-entrepreneurs: results of two experiments using electrophysiological measures
original_journal: International Journal of Entrepreneurship and Small Business
replication_title: Nonlocal Intuition: Replication and Paired-subjects Enhancement Effects
replication_journal: Global Advances in Health and Medicine
replication_target_quote: nonlocal intuition was investigated in a replication and extension of experiment using measures of heart rate variability (HRV)
outcome_quote: the results of the single-participant experiment confirm previous finding
review_note: The later Tehran study repeats the physiological pre-stimulus paradigm and reports a corresponding signal; this records the published finding without endorsing its interpretation.

effect_name: Faces appear more attractive in groups
effect_claim: Faces presented in a group appear more attractive than the same faces shown alone.
effect_claim_quote: people seem more attractive in a group than in isolation
original_title: Hierarchical Encoding Makes Individuals in a Group Seem More Attractive
replication_title: Replicating and reversing the group attractiveness effect: Relatively unattractive groups are perceived as less attractive than the average attractiveness of their members
replication_target_quote: we aimed to replicate the GA-effect as well as reverse it
outcome_quote: the data replicated a GA effect for relatively attractive groups
review_note: The later study explicitly retests the group-attractiveness effect, finds it for relatively attractive groups, and separately tests a reversal for unattractive groups.

effect_name: Single-session body image lesson improves short-term outcomes
effect_claim: The teacher-led Dove Confident Me lesson improved some short-term body image and eating outcomes.
effect_claim_quote: post-intervention improvements for intervention students relative to control in body esteem (TL; girls only)
original_title: Effectiveness of a brief school-based body image intervention ‘Dove Confident Me: Single Session’ when delivered by teachers and researchers: Results from a cluster randomised controlled trial
replication_title: Independent pragmatic replication of the Dove Confident Me body image program in an Australian Girls Independent Secondary School
replication_target_quote: this research aimed to investigate whether the universal co-educational prevention program developed for audiences in the United Kingdom (Dove Confident Me, DCM), was an acceptable and effective intervention
outcome_quote: No improvements were observed on outcome measures between the comparison and intervention girls over the three time points.
review_note: Independent pragmatic replication in a single-sex Australian school found no measured benefit; setting and delivery differ from the original trial.

effect_name: Personality dimensions correlate with social attitudes
effect_claim: Neuroticism and psychoticism correlated with particular social attitudes in the original sample.
effect_claim_quote: Neuroticism was related to ethnocentrism and the intolerance of minority groups
original_title: SOCIAL ATTITUDE CORRELATES OF EYSENCK'S PERSONALITY DIMENSIONS
original_journal: Social Behavior and Personality An International Journal
replication_title: IS PERSONALITY RELATED TO SOCIAL ATTITUDES? AN ATTEMPT AT REPLICATION
replication_journal: Social Behavior and Personality An International Journal
replication_target_quote: An attempt was made to replicate previous work relating Eysenck's personality dimensions to social attitudes.
outcome_quote: No significant correlation was obtained between psychoticism, neuroticism, extraversion, Lie Scale, and any of the six social attitude variables.
review_note: The later paper explicitly attempts replication in student nurses and finds none of the original personality-attitude correlations in that sample.

effect_name: Missing intake information predicts suicidal thinking
effect_claim: Missing demographic answers on client intake forms indicate greater severity of suicidal thinking.
effect_claim_quote: missing information on education, income, and/or number of persons living with the respondent were valid indicators of the severity of suicidal thinking
original_title: Does the Fact that a Client has Failed to Provide Requested Information Predict Severity of Suicidal Thinking?: A Criterion Validity Study of Missing Client Information
replication_title: The Criterion Validity of Omitted Client Information as an Indicator of Suicide Risk: A Partial Replication
replication_target_quote: replicate findings reported by Nugent and Williams-Hayes that suggested that there is a relationship between missing information on demographic items found on client intake forms and severity of suicidal ideation
outcome_quote: The results partially replicated those of Nugent and Williams-Hayes
review_note: The later study explicitly retests the original intake-form finding and reports only partial replication.

effect_name: Parents favor aerobic over strength exercise for adolescents
effect_claim: Parents view aerobic exercise for their children more favorably than strength exercise.
effect_claim_quote: Parents consistently reported a positive attitude towards aerobic exercises, but a less positive attitude regarding strength exercises.
original_title: Aerobic and strength exercises for youngsters aged 12 to 15: what do parents think?
replication_title: Turkish Parents’ Attitudes Towards Strength and Aerobic Exercises in their Children: A Replication of Ten Hoor et al. (2015)
replication_target_quote: a Dutch study by ten Hoor et al. (2015) was replicated in Turkey
outcome_quote: Turkish parents had more positive attitudes for aerobic exercises compared to strength exercises.
review_note: The later Turkish parent survey explicitly repeats the Dutch study and finds the same difference in attitudes.

effect_name: Anhedonia predicts suicidal thinking beyond depression
effect_claim: Anhedonia was associated with suicidal ideation after accounting for other depressive symptoms.
effect_claim_quote: Anhedonia was associated with suicidal ideation, even when accounting for depressive symptoms.
original_title: The Association between Anhedonia, Suicidal Ideation, and Suicide Attempts in a Large Student Sample
replication_title: The Association Between Anhedonia, Suicide Ideation, and Suicide Attempts: A Replication in a Persian Student Sample
replication_target_quote: this study attempted to replicate a recent anhedonia and suicide study (conducted in a western culture) in a Persian sample
outcome_quote: anhedonia was associated with suicide risk, even when it was statistically accounting for other depressive symptoms.
review_note: Cross-cultural replication in a Persian student sample retains the association after accounting for other depressive symptoms.

effect_name: Brief habit reversal reduces public-speaking disfluencies
effect_claim: Brief habit reversal training reduced speech disfluencies during public speaking.
effect_claim_quote: Brief habit reversal combined with an interdependent group contingency resulted in a meaningful reduction in speech disfluencies
original_title: Using brief habit reversal and an interdependent group contingency to reduce public‐speaking speech disfluencies
replication_title: Using Brief Habit Reversal to Decrease Speech Disfluencies in Public Speaking. A Systematic Replication
replication_target_quote: The study was systematically replicated to evaluate the benefit of brief habit reversal training for social workers in decreasing speech disfluencies.
outcome_quote: all participants reduced speech disfluencies during brief habit reversal.
review_note: Later systematic replication in social-work students reports reduced disfluencies during the training and sustained improvement.

effect_name: Internal locus of control predicts small-group leadership
effect_claim: Students who became task leaders tended to have a more internal locus of control than followers.
effect_claim_quote: Task leaders tended to show a belief in internal control and followers a belief in external control.
original_title: Status-Role Consequences of Internal-External Control of Reinforcement
replication_title: Replications of Association between Internal Locus of Control and Leadership in Small Groups
replication_target_quote: An internal locus of control, as measured by Rotter's ( 5 ) internal-external (I-E) scale has been associated (2 ) with sociometrically determined task-leadership
outcome_quote: leaders tended to be more external than followers, although this was not statistically significant
review_note: Later authors explicitly retest their earlier small-group result with matched participants; the leadership association does not repeat.

effect_name: Men receive more and longer newspaper obituaries
effect_claim: Men were more likely than women to receive obituaries and photographs, and women’s obituaries were shorter.
effect_claim_quote: A disproportionately low number of women received obituaries, and female obituaries were also shorter.
original_title: Sex Discrimination after Death
original_journal: OMEGA - Journal of Death and Dying
replication_title: Sex Discrimination after Death: A Replication, Extension and a Difference
replication_journal: OMEGA - Journal of Death and Dying
replication_target_quote: The present work is an extension of that initiated by Kastenbaum, Peyton and Kastenbaum on subtle expressions of sex discrimination after death.
outcome_quote: The earlier work of Kastenbaum and his associates is weakly confirmed
review_note: Denver obituaries show some male excess, but differences lessen or disappear across time and after accounting for occupational content.

effect_name: Most child-maltreatment studies omit ethnicity from analysis
effect_claim: Most child-maltreatment research papers in the sampled journals did not use ethnicity in analyses.
effect_claim_quote: three quarters of the articles published in the most recent years examined (1995-1998) did not include ethnicity in their analyses or design.
original_title: Ethnicity in Child Maltreatment Research: A Content Analysis
replication_title: Ethnicity in Child Maltreatment Research: A Replication of Behl et al.'s Content Analysis
replication_target_quote: Ethnicity in Child Maltreatment Research: A Replication of Behl et al.'s Content Analysis
outcome_quote: 33.8% use ethnicity of participants in analyses
review_note: Later content analysis repeats the journal survey; it finds greater inclusion than the original, yet most articles still omit ethnicity from analysis.

effect_name: Future-oriented web searches track regional GDP
effect_claim: Places with more searches about the future relative to the past tend to have higher GDP.
effect_claim_quote: We analyse Google logs and find a striking correlation between the country's GDP and the predisposition of its inhabitants to look forward.
original_title: Quantifying the Advantage of Looking Forward
replication_title: Seeking Forward, Looking Forward: A Replication and Generalization of the Future Orientation Index Utilizing Baidu Index
replication_target_quote: Our study aimed to replicate and extend correlations between the FOI and key development indicators, such as GDP and Human Development Index (HDI)
outcome_quote: Our results successfully replicated the correlation between the Baidu-based FOI and province-level GDP
review_note: The later study repeats the future-orientation index using Baidu and finds a group-level GDP association; it separately reports no individual-level patience prediction.

effect_name: First-trial versus all-trials measurement in autism treatment
effect_claim: Measuring only the first trial generally indicated quicker skill acquisition, while measuring every trial indicated stronger maintenance.
effect_claim_quote: When differences were detected, quicker acquisition was typically associated with discontinuous measurement, and stronger maintenance was typically associated with continuous measurement.
original_title: EVALUATING PROGRESS IN BEHAVIORAL PROGRAMS FOR CHILDREN WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDERS VIA CONTINUOUS AND DISCONTINUOUS MEASUREMENT
replication_title: COMPARISON OF DATA‐COLLECTION METHODS IN A BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTION PROGRAM FOR CHILDREN WITH PERVASIVE DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS: A REPLICATION
replication_target_quote: Cummings and Carr (2009) compared two methods of data collection in a behavioral intervention program for children with pervasive developmental disorders: collecting data on all trials versus only the first trial in a session.
outcome_quote: In the current replication, no such differences in indication of mastery or maintenance were observed when data were collected on all trials or the first trial.
review_note: OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W2068866708). Original and replication both 2009, original Spring/March precedes replication Winter/December.

effect_name: Glucose and fructose boosts to anagram solving
effect_claim: Consuming glucose or fructose before an anagram task increased the number of anagrams solved relative to placebo.
effect_claim_quote: It was observed that consuming fructose and glucose resulted in the resolution of more anagrams than the placebo.
original_title: Can you enhance executive control without glucose? The effects of fructose on problem solving
replication_title: What Enables Self-Control? A Test of Glucose, Fructose, and Vagus Nerve Activation as Possible Factors
replication_target_quote: This study replicated the study by Miller, Bourrasseau, and Blampain (2013) on the effects of fructose and glucose on\nself-control.
outcome_quote: it was found that fructose, glucose, and VM did not increase the participants' levels of self-control
review_note: OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W2149227176). Published article; later full text explicitly cites Miller, Bourrasseau, and Blampain (2013).

replication_title: Plasticity in older adults’ theory of mind performance: the impact of motivation
effect_name: Closeness motivation removes older adults’ faux pas recognition deficit
effect_claim: Older adults whose sense of closeness to the experimenter was increased performed as well as younger adults on faux pas recognition.
effect_claim_quote: When closeness was experimentally increased, older adults enhanced their performance, and they now performed at a comparable level as younger adults.
original_title: Perspective taking in older age revisited: A motivational perspective
replication_target_quote: Following a previous paradigm, 171 Chinese adults (87 younger adults and 84 older adults) were recruited, and we experimentally manipulated the level of perceived closeness between participants and the experimenter before administering the ToM tasks in order to enhance participants' motivation.
outcome_quote: Results showed that, for the Faux Pas task, we replicated previous findings such that older adults under the enhanced motivation conditions performed equally well as younger adults.
review_note: Corrected to Zhang et al. 2013 Study 1: same lead author, closeness manipulation and faux-pas task. Later primary PDF methods explicitly cite Zhang et al. 2013 Study 1 and reference DOI 10.1037/a0031211. Narrows effect to faux-pas age-gap attenuation; animation task did not generalize.

effect_name: Posted speed feedback reduces speeding
effect_claim: Public signs showing the share of drivers obeying the speed limit reduced speeding.
effect_claim_quote: public posting was highly effective in reducing the percentage of speeding drivers
original_title: A COMPARISON OF THE EFFECTS OF POSTED FEEDBACK AND INCREASED POLICE SURVEILLANCE ON HIGHWAY SPEEDING
replication_title: A REPLICATION OF THE USE OF PUBLIC POSTING IN TRAFFIC SPEED CONTROL
replication_target_quote: a reversal design was used to assess the effects of publicly posted feedback on vehicle speed reduction
outcome_quote: Results from the two feedback conditions indicated no speed reduction in comparison to baseline levels.
review_note: The later paper explicitly cites the 1981 Van Houten and Nau study among the public-posting experiments it retests; its two feedback conditions did not reduce speeding.

effect_name: Triggers for change and coping differ
effect_claim: The life events that prompt change are not associated with events that prompt coping.
effect_claim_quote: stimuli that prompt change were not associated with the stimuli that prompt coping
original_title: The experience of changing and the relationship between changing and coping: an adult perspective
replication_title: Changing and coping, and the stimulus to change from an adolescent perspective: A replication of adult research
replication_target_quote: The aims of this research is to replicate an adult study
outcome_quote: There was no association between what the adolescents reported as stimuli to change and the stimuli to cope.
review_note: Same authors repeat their change-versus-coping interview study among adolescents and again find no association between the two reported sets of triggers.

effect_name: European suicide rates form a geographic J-shaped pattern
effect_claim: Latitude and its interaction with longitude account for substantial variation in European suicide rates.
effect_claim_quote: The interaction term explains 40.8% and 29.1% of men's and women's suicide rate, respectively
original_title: The Finno-Ugrian Suicide Hypothesis: Variation in European Suicide Rates by Latitude and Longitude
replication_title: Testing the Finno-Ugrian Suicide Hypothesis: Replication and Refinement with Regional Suicide Data from Eastern Europe
replication_target_quote: The present research replicated and extended 2003 findings of Voracek, Fisher, and Marusic with new data.
outcome_quote: an interaction term of squared latitude multiplied with longitude (quantifying the J-shaped belt) accounted for 32% of the cross-national variance in total suicide rates alone
review_note: The same authors rerun the geographic correlation with newer and regional data. This records a spatial association, not a genetic explanation.

effect_name: Test-anxiety worry relates to expected performance
effect_claim: The worry component of test anxiety is more strongly related to performance expectancy than emotionality.
effect_claim_quote: W was found to be negatively related to expectancy. E was not consistently related to expectancy
original_title: Cognitive and Emotional Components of Test Anxiety: Temporal Factors
replication_title: Worry and Emotionality as Components of Test Anxiety: Replication and Further Data
replication_target_quote: Worry and Emotionality as Components of Test Anxiety: Replication and Further Data
outcome_quote: W was more highly correlated with expectancy of success ratings than E
review_note: The later test-anxiety paper again finds worry more related to expected success than emotionality, while probing temporal change separately.

effect_name: Girls continuing in mathematics have more positive math attitudes
effect_claim: High-school girls who continue more years of math report more positive attitudes toward mathematics.
effect_claim_quote: Math enrollment groups differed significantly on the following scales: Usefulness of Mathematics, Confidence in Learning Mathematics
original_title: Continuing in Mathematics: A Longitudinal Study of the Attitudes of High School Girls
replication_title: Girls Talk About Mathematics and Their Future: A Partial Replication
replication_target_quote: Girls Talk About Mathematics and Their Future: A Partial Replication
outcome_quote: girls continuing in math had more positive attitudes toward math
review_note: The same author partially repeats her earlier longitudinal comparison and again finds more positive math attitudes in girls who continue math study.

effect_name: Learning-disabled children underattribute failure to effort
effect_claim: Underachieving children assign less importance to lack of effort as a cause of their failures.
effect_claim_quote: underachievers believed lack of effort played less of a role in their failures than did control children
original_title: Learning Disabled Children's Attributions for Success and Failure
replication_title: LD Children's Attributions for Success and Failure: A Replication with a Labeled LD Sample
replication_target_quote: LD Children's Attributions for Success and Failure: A Replication with a Labeled LD Sample
outcome_quote: failure is not necessarily viewed as something that can be overcome with effort
review_note: Later paper repeats the attribution question in labeled learning-disabled children and reports the same general direction, but its abstract does not report the original between-group contrast.

effect_name: Expansive poses raise felt power
effect_claim: Adopting expansive rather than contracted postures increased self-reported feelings of power.
effect_claim_quote: increased feelings of power and tolerance for risk
original_title: Power Posing
replication_title: Power vs. persuasion: can open body postures embody openness to persuasion?
replication_target_quote: In the current study, we sought to replicate the finding that adopting an open/expansive body posture increases subjective feelings of power
outcome_quote: Results failed to replicate the previously found effect of body posture on subjective feelings of power.
review_note: The later authors name Carney, Cuddy, and Yap 2010 in their author-hosted manuscript, and test the original subjective-power endpoint. Later primary Psychology. No existing original/replication pair or conflicting FORRT verdict.

effect_name: First Step improves behavior in at-risk kindergarteners
effect_claim: The First Step to Success intervention improved behavior among at-risk kindergarten children.
effect_claim_quote: Results indicated a measurable intervention effect for both cohorts
original_title: First Step to Success: An Early Intervention Approach for Preventing School Antisocial Behavior
original_journal: Journal of Emotional and Behavioral Disorders
replication_title: First Step to Success: Replication and Social Validation of an Early Intervention Program
replication_journal: Journal of Emotional and Behavioral Disorders
replication_target_quote: the replication sample were nearly identical to those for the original field-test sample
outcome_quote: Results indicated that the replication was successful
review_note: Same intervention, kindergarten population, and two-cohort original field test; three overlapping authors. Crossref published-online dates April 1 and October 1, 1998, respectively. Later primary Psychology. No existing original/replication pair or conflicting FORRT verdict.

effect_name: Sugar drink reverses impaired self-control
effect_claim: After an initial self-control task, consuming a glucose drink prevented impaired performance on a subsequent self-control task.
effect_claim_quote: consuming a glucose drink eliminated these impairments
original_title: Self-control relies on glucose as a limited energy source: Willpower is more than a metaphor
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Turn It All You Want: Still No Effect of Sugar Consumption on Ego Depletion
replication_target_quote: so-called ego-depletion effect is assumed to be alleviated by the consumption of sugar-containing drinks
outcome_quote: Results suggest that sugar consumption does not counteract ego depletion even when dissimilar self-control tasks are used.
review_note: Later paper explicitly cites Gailliot et al. 2007 as original support for glucose drink counteracting depletion and tests sugar vs artificial sweetener between two self-control tasks. Later primary Psychology. No existing original/replication pair or conflicting FORRT verdict.

effect_name: Automated analysis aids interpretation of behavioral assessments
effect_claim: Automated nonparametric statistical analysis can support interpretation of functional analysis data.
effect_claim_quote: Results showed that exact behavior function agreement between ANSA and the publications authors was 83.1%, exact agreement between ANSA and PHVI was 75.4%, and exact agreement across all 3 methods was 64.6%.
original_title: Interpreting functional analysis outcomes using automated nonparametric statistical analysis
replication_title: Application of automated nonparametric statistical analysis in clinical contexts
replication_target_quote: Recently, Hall et al. (2020) provided a proof of concept for using automated nonparametric statistical analysis (ANSA) to interpret FA data.
outcome_quote: Our results were consistent with Hall et al.'s, indicating ANSA may augment clinical interpretation of FA data.
review_note: OpenAlex W3094555283 primary field Psychology. PubMed abstracts match exact DOI pair and later explicitly cites Hall et al. 2020.

effect_name: Repeated risk assessment improves prediction of recidivism
effect_claim: Recent repeated assessments of dynamic risk factors improve prediction of imminent criminal recidivism beyond initial scores.
effect_claim_quote: In this sample, reassessments consistently improved prediction as demonstrated by (1) incremental prediction over initial baseline scores and (2) improved model fit of the most recent assessment compared with the average of earlier scores.
original_title: Reassessment improves prediction of criminal recidivism: A prospective study of 3,421 individuals in New Zealand
replication_title: Does Reassessment Enhance the Prediction of Imminent Criminal Recidivism? Replicating Lloyd et al. (2020) With High-Risk Parolees
replication_target_quote: Lloyd et al. (2020) proposed and tested a novel three-step framework for examining the extent to which reassessment of dynamic risk and protective factors enhances the prediction of imminent criminal recidivism.
outcome_quote: The results of the previous study were largely reproduced: reassessment consistently enhanced prediction, with the most pronounced effects observed for a scale derived from theoretically acute dynamic risk factors.
review_note: Corrected wrong proposed Lloyd 2022 PNAS DOI to exact Lloyd et al. 2020 Psychological Assessment DOI 10.1037/pas0000813, confirmed in original PubMed and later SAGE primary abstracts. Later OpenAlex W3131119082 primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Response interruption and redirection reduces vocal stereotypy
effect_claim: Response interruption and redirection reduced noncommunicative vocal stereotypy in children with autism.
effect_claim_quote: For each child, RIRD produced levels of vocal stereotypy substantially lower than those observed in baseline.
original_title: Assessing and treating vocal stereotypy in children with autism
replication_title: RESPONSE INTERRUPTION AND REDIRECTION FOR VOCAL STEREOTYPY IN CHILDREN WITH AUTISM: A SYSTEMATIC REPLICATION
replication_target_quote: This study systematically replicated and extended previous research on response interruption and redirection (RIRD)
outcome_quote: Results showed that RIRD produced substantial decreases in vocal stereotypy.
review_note: Corrected proposed same-issue 2011 link to exact Ahearn et al. 2007 target identified in later full-text Introduction. Later OpenAlex W1965505739 primary field Psychology. Same original effect label and claim as existing curated row; only vocal stereotypy reduction is claimed here, since appropriate vocalizations did not increase in later study.

effect_name: Income rank predicts life satisfaction beyond absolute income
effect_claim: A person’s income rank predicts life satisfaction even when absolute and reference income are considered.
effect_claim_quote: We find that the ranked position of an individual’s income predicts general life satisfaction, while absolute income and reference income have no effect.
original_title: Money and Happiness: Rank of Income, Not Income, Affects Life Satisfaction
replication_title: Buying Happiness in an Unequal World: Rank of Income More Strongly Predicts Well-Being in More Unequal Countries
replication_target_quote: we followed Boyce et al. (2010) and defined income rank
outcome_quote: Consistent with Boyce et al. (2010), the inclusion of income rank removed the effect of absolute income
review_note: The later study explicitly cites and follows Boyce et al. (2010), then repeats the income-rank association using Gallup data from 24 countries. It additionally tests moderation by inequality.

replication_title: Volitional saccade performance in a large sample of patients with obsessive‐compulsive disorder and unaffected first‐degree relatives
effect_name: OCD volitional saccade selection deficit in patients and unaffected relatives
effect_claim: Patients with OCD and unaffected first-degree relatives had slower volitional saccade response selection than healthy controls.
effect_claim_quote: Our results showed that unaffected first-degree relatives and OCD patients were significantly slowed compared to healthy comparison subjects in volitional response selection.
original_title: Impaired volitional saccade control: first evidence for a new candidate endophenotype in obsessive-compulsive disorder
original_journal: European Archives of Psychiatry and Clinical Neuroscience
replication_target_quote: Recent evidence indicates that patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) as well as their unaffected first-degree relatives show deficits in the volitional control of saccades, suggesting that volitional saccade performance may constitute an endophenotype of OCD.
outcome_quote: In contrast to previous reports, neither patients nor relatives showed impairments in the performance of volitional saccades compared to healthy controls.
review_note: Corrected machine link from schizophrenia saccades to Kloft et al. 2012 OCD patients-and-relatives study. Later paper includes original coauthor Kloft and specifically retests the same familial volitional saccade endophenotype in a larger independent sample; both primary PubMed abstracts support the direction and result. Later primary OpenAlex field Psychology, checked before rate limit.

effect_name: Resurgence during reinforcement thinning
effect_claim: Destructive behavior commonly resurged as reinforcement schedules were thinned during functional communication training.
effect_claim_quote: We observed resurgence in 19 of the 25 (76%) applications of reinforcement schedule thinning.
original_title: Prevalence of resurgence of destructive behavior when thinning reinforcement schedules during functional communication training
replication_title: Prevalence of resurgence during thinning of multiple schedules of reinforcement following functional communication training
replication_target_quote: replicating previous research (Briggs et al., 2018)
outcome_quote: resurgence was observed in 97 of those steps (40.6%), similar to results of Briggs et al. (2018).
review_note: Corrected unrelated machine original to explicitly cited Briggs et al. 2018. Original 47/111 thinning steps (42%) and later 97/239 (40.6%) of the same FCT phenomenon; source Springer/Wiley primary abstracts. No existing original/replication pair or conflicting FORRT verdict.

effect_name: Segmented instructional animation improves far transfer
effect_claim: Segmenting instructional animations improved students’ ability to apply teaching skills to new scenarios.
effect_claim_quote: SE groups outperformed no-SE groups on all learning measures
original_title: Optimising learning from animations by minimising cognitive load: cognitive and affective consequences of signalling and segmentation methods
replication_title: Impacts of segmenting principle on learner performance and attitude in a 3D environment: a mixed-method multiple case study
replication_journal: Journal of Computing in Higher Education
replication_target_quote: conceptual replication of Moreno’s (Appl Cogn Psychol 21:765–781. 10.1002/acp.1348, 2007) study
outcome_quote: Results indicate benefits for both cases in far transfer of learning.
review_note: Corrected machine original to Moreno 2007 exact DOI explicitly named in later abstract. Later 3D multimedia setting tests segmented instruction and finds far-transfer benefit in both synchronous and asynchronous cases. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology. No existing original/replication pair or conflicting FORRT verdict.

effect_name: Precognitive guessing of erotic image location
effect_claim: Participants purportedly guessed the future location of erotic pictures above chance, at a 53.1% hit rate.
effect_claim_quote: future position of the erotic pictures significantly more frequently than the 50% hit rate expected by chance: 53.1%
original_title: Feeling the future: Experimental evidence for anomalous retroactive influences on cognition and affect.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Raising the value of research studies in psychological science by increasing the credibility of research reports: the transparent Psi project
replication_target_quote: replication of Bem’s Experiment 1
outcome_quote: We found 49.89% successful guesses, while Bem reported 53.07% success rate, with the chance level being 50%.
review_note: Later exact-DOI PubMed Central paper and original published PDF identify Bem Experiment 1, erotic-picture location guessing, and incompatible hit rates; later OpenAlex primary Psychology. No existing original/replication pair or conflicting FORRT verdict.

effect_name: Negative social events correlate with suicide indicators
effect_claim: Annual social stress scores were associated with attempted suicide in Hong Kong.
effect_claim_quote: this stress is associated with attempted suicide but not with diabetes mellitus or coronary heart disease.
original_title: Negative social events, stress, and health in Hong Kong.
replication_title: Social Stress and Suicide: Replicating an Asian Study with American Data
replication_target_quote: A study purporting to show an association between social stress and attempted suicide in Hong Kong
outcome_quote: social stress was positively associated with suicide rates.
review_note: The later American time-series repeats the social-stress test with a corrected regression and finds association with suicide mortality, whereas the original examined attempted suicide.

effect_name: Sex differences peak for casual partner criteria
effect_claim: In the original sample, men set lower mate-selection criteria than women for casual sexual relationships.
effect_claim_quote: Sex differences were greatest for casual sexual liaisons, with mens criteria being consistently lower than women's.
original_title: Integrating evolutionary and social exchange perspectives on relationships: Effects of gender, self-appraisal, and involvement level on mate selection criteria.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Evolutionary Theory and Mating Preferences: A Partial Replication of Kenrick et al.’s (1993) Study
replication_journal: Psi Chi Journal of Psychological Research
replication_target_quote: quantitative partial replication of Kenrick and colleagues’ (1993) analysis
outcome_quote: men and women were more similar than different.
review_note: Partial replication tests a selected subset of mate criteria and finds little of the broad sex-difference pattern; sample and measures differ.

effect_name: No bilingual advantage in prospective memory accuracy
effect_claim: The original Turkish-English bilingual group did not outperform monolinguals on prospective-memory accuracy.
effect_claim_quote: The results showed no direct evidence for a bilingual advantage in PM.
original_title: Do bilinguals have an advantage in prospective memory?
replication_title: Re-examining the Bilingual Advantage in Prospective Memory: A Partial Replication with Turkish Bilingual and Monolingual Young Adults
replication_target_quote: the present study offers a partial replication of Yörük et al.’s (2023) research investigating the effect of bilingualism on EB-PM
outcome_quote: consistent with the original study, provided no support for a bilingual advantage in PM accuracy.
review_note: Published 2026 partial replication by an original coauthor again finds no bilingual advantage in prospective-memory accuracy; it also changes the sample setting.

effect_name: Attractive online models increase weight-loss intentions
effect_claim: Exposure to attractive online model photos increased women’s planned weight-loss behavior.
effect_claim_quote: Participants exposed to attractive model pictures showed higher intentions, attitudes, and subjective norms to lose weight compared with unattractive models.
original_title: The Exposure Effects of Online Model Pictures and Weight-Related Persuasive Messages on Women’s Weight-Loss Planned Behaviors
replication_title: A replication and expansion of the exposure effects of online model photos and social comparison goals on planned behaviors and self-efficacy to lose weight
replication_target_quote: This study replicated and expanded social comparison theory predictions in regard to how exposure to online models
outcome_quote: Women and men exposed to online photos of more attractive models reported higher planned behaviors to lose weight relative to those who were exposed to photos of less attractive models
review_note: Same authors repeat the model-attractiveness comparison in an expanded sample including men and report the same direction for planned weight-loss behavior.

effect_name: Token rewards improve selected residential-treatment behaviors
effect_claim: Token reinforcement changed several appropriate and inappropriate behaviors in a home-style program for boys.
effect_claim_quote: The frequencies of aggressive statements and poor grammar decreased while tidiness, punctuality, and amount of homework completed increased.
original_title: ACHIEVEMENT PLACE: TOKEN REINFORCEMENT PROCEDURES IN A HOME‐STYLE REHABILITATION SETTING FOR “PREDELINQUENT” BOYS1
replication_title: REPLICATION OF THE ACHIEVEMENT PLACE MODEL IN CALIFORNIA1
replication_target_quote: Attempting to replicate procedures from Achievement Place
outcome_quote: Contingent point fines reduced the frequency of interruptions. Point rewards improved table-setting, but even large point rewards did not substantially increase savings.
review_note: California residential setting repeats Achievement Place token procedures; interruptions and table-setting improved, savings did not.

effect_name: Positive self-monitoring fails as criticism inoculation
effect_claim: Positive self-monitoring did not protect basketball learners from adverse effects of criticism in the original experiment.
effect_claim_quote: positive self-monitoring also decreased performance.
original_title: Criticism Inoculation Training: Concept in Search of Strategy
replication_title: Still searching for effective criticism inoculation procedures: An example of the value of replication and process analyses in applied sport psychology research
replication_target_quote: This study replicated and extended some aspects of the research reported by Kirschenbaum et al. (1984)
outcome_quote: As in the prior study, CIT proved surprisingly ineffective
