review_note: Later study repeats the basketball criticism-inoculation setting and again finds the training ineffective, although it adds imagery and expectancy components.

effect_name: Developmental Trauma Disorder interview validity
effect_claim: The Developmental Trauma Disorder interview yielded a reliable three-factor construct with convergent and criterion validity in children.
effect_claim_quote: The DTD-SI yielded reliable, structurally meaningful, and valid item- and criterion-level data for the proposed DTD syndrome.
original_title: Toward an Empirically Based Developmental Trauma Disorder Diagnosis for Children: Factor Structure, Item Characteristics, Reliability, and Validity of the Developmental Trauma Disorder Semi-Structured Interview
replication_title: Toward an empirically based Developmental Trauma Disorder diagnosis and semi‐structured interview for children: The DTD field trial replication
replication_target_quote: This study aimed to determine whether the assessment of DTD with an independent sample of children in mental health treatment will replicate results from an initial validation study.
outcome_quote: Results supported the criterion and convergent validity of the DTD construct.
review_note: Corrected wrong proposed original to Ford et al. 2018 DTD-SI validation DOI 10.4088/JCP.17m11675. Later Wiley primary full text reference 29 gives exact study title/authors/year; both original and later test DTD-SI structure and validity. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: DRO suppresses target responding more than yoked reinforcement
effect_claim: Differential reinforcement of other behavior produced a larger drop in the target response than matched noncontingent reinforcement.
effect_claim_quote: response-decrement was more rapid and more marked in the differential-reinforcement-of-other-behavior animals than in the controls
original_title: DIFFERENTIAL REINFORCEMENT OF OTHER BEHAVIOR (DRO): A YOKED‐CONTROL COMPARISON1
original_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior
replication_title: The role of adventitious reinforcement during differential reinforcement of other behavior: A systematic replication
replication_target_quote: The present study systematically replicated previous research assessing whether adventitious reinforcement of alternative behavior contributes to the effectiveness of DRO.
outcome_quote: DRO schedules resulted in the lowest target-response rate and highest alternative-response rate.
review_note: Conceptual systematic replication changes rats to a computer task with students but repeats the DRO versus yoked schedule comparison and the response-rate reduction.

effect_name: Edible items often outrank leisure items in autism preference tests
effect_claim: Edible items were more likely than leisure items to rank highly in preference assessments of children with autism.
effect_claim_quote: edible items were more likely than leisure items to rank highly in our preference assessments
original_title: Relative preferences for edible and leisure stimuli in children with autism
replication_title: A replication of preference displacement research in children with autism spectrum disorder
replication_target_quote: The purpose of this paper was to replicate previous research on preference displacement with edible and leisure stimuli.
outcome_quote: complete displacement by edible stimuli for four participants and complete displacement by leisure stimuli for two participants
review_note: The later sample again shows edible-item displacement for some children, but leisure items fully displace edibles for others; it does not establish the original group tendency in its abstract.

effect_name: Greater social distance from stigmatized nonethnic groups
effect_claim: People in stigmatized nonethnic groups, including those dying, were more socially avoided than members of ethnic groups.
effect_claim_quote: ethnic groups (e.g. Negro, Mexican-American) were less avoided than the nonethnic groups (e.g. drug addict, dying person, alcoholic).
original_title: Social distance and the dying
replication_title: The Stigma against Dying and Suicidal Patients: A Replication of Richard Kalish's Study Twenty-Five Years Later
replication_journal: OMEGA - Journal of Death and Dying
replication_target_quote: replicated the results reported by Richard Kalish twenty-five years ago.
outcome_quote: The deviant and psychiatric groups, including people dying from cancer and who had attempted suicide, were the recipients of more prejudice than the religious and ethnic groups.
review_note: Later paper OpenAlex W1979479551 primary field Psychology. Exact Kalish original identity corroborated by original abstract and later title/abstract. Original abstract retrieved by exact DOI from Europe PMC.

effect_name: Edible rewards increase compliance with difficult hygiene routines
effect_claim: Providing a preferred edible item for cooperation increased a child’s tolerance of haircuts without requiring escape extinction.
effect_claim_quote: Results indicated that the intervention eliminated the child's escape responses and increased his sitting to a duration that permitted regular haircuts by his mother.
original_title: Increasing compliance with haircuts in a child with autism
replication_title: Effects of reinforcement without extinction on increasing compliance with nail cutting: A systematic replication
replication_target_quote: We conducted a systematic replication of Schumacher and Rapp (2011), Shabani and Fisher (2006), and Bishop et al. (2013)
outcome_quote: treatment reduced participants' escape responses and increased their compliance with nail cutting.
review_note: The later paper names Schumacher and Rapp as a source for its systematic replication and applies edible-item reinforcement to nail cutting; both studies report increased compliance without escape extinction.

replication_title: Geophysical Variables and Behavior: XXXI. Global Geomagnetic Activity during Spontaneous Paranormal Experiences: A Replication
effect_name: Low geomagnetic activity during reported telepathic crises
effect_claim: Reported telepathic experiences involving crises occurred on days with below-average geomagnetic activity.
effect_claim_quote: All 25 experiences were reported to have occurred on days when the geomagnetic activity was less than the means for those months.
original_title: Geophysical Variables and Behavior: XXX. Intense Paranormal Experiences Occur during Days of Quiet, Global, Geomagnetic Activity
replication_target_quote: A retrospective analysis was completed of the global geomagnetic activity (aa indices) for the day, month, and year in which subjective experiences of telepathy-clairvoyance
outcome_quote: The aa values for the days on which the telepathy-clairvoyance experiences occurred were also significantly less than the average geomagnetic activity for the months or years in which the experiences occurred.
review_note: Sequential Persinger geophysical variables studies XXX and XXXI; independent Stevenson cases versus FATE first-hand reports. Later same geomagnetic aa index and telepathic crisis outcome; positive only for telepathy, not precognition/postmortem. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Crossref online dates verified.

replication_title: Race and cardiovascular reactivity. A replication.
effect_name: Race difference in children’s video-game cardiovascular stress reactivity
effect_claim: Black children showed greater cardiovascular response to a psychological video-game stressor than white children.
effect_claim_quote: Black children demonstrated significantly greater reactivity than white children; the racial difference was more reliably observed for systolic and diastolic blood pressure than for heart rate.
original_title: Race and cardiovascular reactivity. A neglected relationship.
replication_target_quote: In a previous study, we reported that black children demonstrated greater cardiovascular reactivity than did white children to the psychological stress of a television video game.
outcome_quote: Results indicated greater heart rate and blood pressure reactivity among black children than among white children.
review_note: Corrected machine link from same authors’ 1988 Psychophysiology normative-data article to Murphy et al. 1986 original that reports the exact directional black-versus-white finding. Later 1988 replication used an independent rural third-grade sample with the same video-game stressor. Both primary PubMed abstracts exact; later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Adjustment and acceptance of damaging self-descriptions
effect_claim: Better-adjusted children accepted more damaging statements about themselves than poorly adjusted children.
effect_claim_quote: The better-adjusted group checked significantly more items.
original_title: Self-acceptance and adjustment.
replication_title: Self-Acceptance and Adjustment Revisited: A Replication
replication_target_quote: Taylor and Combs (1952) found that adjusted children are more capable of accepting threatening statements than poorly adjusted children. The present study was an attempt to repeat their research with college students.
outcome_quote: Critical ratios were not significant and a correlation of .01 between indices was obtained. When the measures were later administered to 109 Ss without requiring names, r = .04.
review_note: Later paper OpenAlex W2069282705 primary field Psychology. Later publisher references Taylor and Combs 1952 exact original. Original publisher preview hosted by ResearchGate states result.

replication_title: A systematic replication of teaching children with autism to respond appropriately to lures from strangers
effect_name: Behavioral skills training teaches children with autism abduction-prevention responses
effect_claim: Behavioral skills training with in situ feedback taught children with autism safe responses to stranger abduction lures.
effect_claim_quote: All children acquired the skills, which were maintained at a 1-month follow-up assessment.
original_title: Teaching abduction-prevention skills to children with autism
replication_target_quote: We evaluated the effects of behavioral skills training in the home for teaching children with autism to abstain from going with strangers and immediately inform a familiar adult of the stranger's attempt to lure them in the natural environment.
outcome_quote: All participants learned to respond correctly to lures in the home and demonstrated concomitant changes in untrained natural settings.
review_note: Corrected machine link to Gunby, Carr and LeBlanc 2010—the primary predecessor identified in later Wiley reference list and actual systematic-replication target. Same behavioral-skills-training safety response for autism children; later independent home/natural-setting extension. Distinct Gunby & Rapp 2014 article was a concurrent extension with added high-probability lures. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

replication_title: Effects of background noise and extraversion on reading comprehension performance
effect_name: Greater distraction effect of background noise for introverts
effect_claim: Background music or noise impaired introverts’ cognitive test performance more than extraverts’ performance.
effect_claim_quote: It was predicted that introverts would do less well on all of the tasks than extraverts in the presence of music and noise but in silence performance would be the same. A significant interaction was found on all three of the tasks.
original_title: The effect of background music and noise on the cognitive test performance of introverts and extraverts
replication_target_quote: Thus, the findings partially replicated previous research in terms of distraction but were inconsistent with regard to the Eysenckian theory of arousal differences between introverts and extraverts.
outcome_quote: There were no introvert–extravert effects.
review_note: Later author-deposited primary PDF explicitly cites Dobbs, Furnham and McClelland 2011 in its reference list; same extraversion-by-noise interaction is retested in a reading-comprehension task with sirens/white noise. Noise impairment itself replicated, but focal introversion moderation did not. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

replication_title: Estimating WAIS IQ from the Shipley institute of living scale: A replication
effect_name: Shipley continuous norming estimates WAIS IQ accurately
effect_claim: A linear-regression and continuous age-norming formula estimated WAIS IQ from Shipley scores with high agreement in psychiatric samples.
effect_claim_quote: Estimated scores based on the cross-validation sample correlated .76 and .74, respectively, with WAIS Full Scale scaled scores and IQs and did not over- or underpredict, which indicates a high degree of concordance between these two procedures.
original_title: Estimating WAIS IQ from the Shipley Institute of Living Scale using continuously adjusted age norms
replication_target_quote: This study represents a replication of the linear regression techniques and continuous norming used to estimate age-adjusted WAIS IQ from the Shipley Institute of Living Scale.
outcome_quote: The overall correlation coefficient between observed and estimated IQs was .79.
review_note: Corrected machine link from generic WAIS-R continuous-norming article to Zachary, Paulson and Gorsuch 1985 Shipley-to-WAIS formula, explicitly titled in later Wiley reference list. Later independent 125-patient sample tested same prediction formula. Original itself includes cross-validation, but later Schear and Harrison is a separate subsequent replication. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Creativity predicts standardized test scores beyond grades and personality
effect_claim: Creative potential, ability, and trait measures accounted for additional variance in standardized educational test scores beyond GPA and personality.
effect_claim_quote: creative potential, ability, and trait measures accounted for 18% of unique variance in ATAR scores over and above the contribution of GPA
original_title: Explaining standardized educational test scores: The role of creativity above and beyond GPA and personality
original_journal: Psychology of Aesthetics Creativity and the Arts
replication_title: Creativity predicts standardized educational outcomes beyond GPA and personality
replication_target_quote: an extension and conceptual replication of Kaufman et al. (2023)
outcome_quote: The addition of creativity-related variables (higher flexibility) explained an additional 7.5 % variance in NAPLAN literacy scores above GPA and personality, whereas an additional 9.2 % of variance was explained in NAPLAN numeracy scores by creativity-related variables
review_note: Later paper tests the same incremental creativity prediction on a different Australian standardized test (NAPLAN versus ATAR). Original author-university repository confirms DOI, 2023 journal volume, result; later abstract explicitly names Kaufman 2023. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology.

effect_name: More support offered than sought in casual friendships
effect_claim: Adults offered support to potential friends more often than they sought identical support for themselves, with weaker asymmetry in close friendships.
effect_claim_quote: This effect was more pronounced for casual than established friendships.
original_title: Offering more support than we seek
replication_title: When do we offer more support than we seek? A behavioral replication and developmental extension
replication_journal: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships
replication_target_quote: Beck and Clark (2009) found self-report evidence that adults are more likely to offer support to a potential friend than to seek identical support from that potential friend
outcome_quote: Adults were more likely to offer support than to request identical support from potential friends, whereas adults were just as likely to request support as they were to offer support to close friends
review_note: Behavioral replication of explicitly cited Beck and Clark 2009; original journal issue 2009 despite DOI registration 2008. Original and later publisher abstracts support the same casual-versus-close friendship asymmetry. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology.

effect_name: Repeated checking reduces memory confidence
effect_claim: Repeated checking of objects lowered memory confidence and increased automatization of checking behavior.
effect_claim_quote: Results showed that repeated checking led to reductions in memory confidence. Furthermore, re-checking led to automatization of checking procedures
original_title: Automatization and familiarity in repeated checking
replication_title: Automatization and familiarity in repeated checking: A replication
replication_target_quote: Experimental research suggests that this is caused by increased familiarity with perceptual characteristics of the stimulus and automatization of the checking procedure (Dek, van den Hout, Giele, & Engelhard, 2014).
outcome_quote: In both experiments, perseverative checking reduced memory confidence, vividness, and detail, and led to automatization of checking behavior.
review_note: Later same-author replication explicitly names Dek et al. 2014 and repeats the exact checking/metamemory effect in two experiments. Defamiliarization manipulations vary and are excluded from this narrower effect. Original author-university abstract and later publisher abstract. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology.

effect_name: DRD4 genotype interaction predicts disorganized infant attachment
effect_claim: The DRD4 7-repeat allele interacted with the minus-521 T promoter allele to increase odds of disorganized infant attachment.
effect_claim_quote: In the presence of both risk alleles the odds ratio for disorganized attachment increased tenfold.
original_title: Further evidence for the role of the dopamine D4 receptor (DRD4) gene in attachment disorganization: interaction of the exon III 48-bp repeat and the −521 C/T promoter polymorphisms
replication_title: No association of the dopamine D4 receptor (DRD4) and -521 C/T promoter polymorphisms with infant attachment disorganization
replication_target_quote: In a first molecular genetic study Lakatos and colleagues found an association between attachment disorganization and the dopamine D4 receptor (DRD4) gene polymorphism, in particular in the presence of the -521 T allele
outcome_quote: Replication of their study in a sample of 132 infants did not confirm the role of the DRD4 7+ -allele and the -521C/T promoter gene in disorganized attachment.
review_note: Exact Lakatos et al. 2002 original publisher abstract reports 7-repeat by -521 T interaction; later abstract specifically tests that interaction in 132 infants and fails to find it. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology.

effect_name: Light feedback in operant verbal conditioning
effect_claim: A light flash did not reinforce target sentence responses in a verbal conditioning task.
effect_claim_quote: Light, as applied in this study, does not function as a reinforcer in a verbal situation.
original_title: Anxiety and the conditioning of verbal behavior.
replication_title: Anxiety and the conditioning of verbal behavior: A replication.
replication_target_quote: A study by Taffel which investigated the relationship between anxiety and operant verbal conditioning was replicated.
outcome_quote: Results indicated that both verbal and light reinforcement groups conditioned while only Ss with low anxiety demonstrated the conditioning effect.
review_note: Later paper OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Original APA publisher preview hosted on ResearchGate supplies exact light-feedback result; later paper names Taffel and reverses that result.

effect_name: Commerce students and primary psychopathy traits
effect_claim: Commerce students reported higher primary psychopathy than students in other disciplines, after accounting for social desirability.
effect_claim_quote: Even after accounting for social desirability, commerce students reported higher levels of primary psychopathy than other students, regardless of sex.
original_title: Greed is good? Student disciplinary choice and self-reported psychopathy
replication_title: Using the Triarchic model of psychopathy to replicate ``Greed is good? Student disciplinary choice and self-reported psychopathy''
replication_target_quote: The present study is a replication of Wilson and McCarthy (2011) [Greed is good?Student disciplinary choice and self-reported psychopathy.Personality and Individual Differences, 51(7), 873-876].
outcome_quote: We replicated the previous findings, supporting higher levels of primary psychopathic traits, as measured by Meanness, in commerce students in comparison to students from other disciplines.
review_note: Later primary field Psychology. Later abstract cites exact original title/authors/year/journal and tests commerce vs other disciplines with a different psychopathy measure. Original quote from ScienceDirect publisher abstract.

effect_name: Boys’ longer global future time perspective
effect_claim: Adolescent boys chose more distant dates than girls when asked about the world’s future.
effect_claim_quote: on the average boys chose a more distant point of time than girls
original_title: Sex Differences in Personal and Global Future Time Perspectives
replication_title: Sex and Age Differences in Personal and Global Future Time Perspectives: A Replication
replication_target_quote: a replication with 247 German adolescents of an investigation of Finnish teenagers by von Wright and Rauste von Wright in 1977
outcome_quote: Results provide empirical confirmation for findings of the Finnish investigation, especially a more distant “global” future orientation” for boys than for girls.
review_note: Later primary field Psychology. Original one-page primary paper is publicly previewed with OCR on ResearchGate; result sentence transcribed without OCR spacing. Later abstract explicitly names original authors, year, population and direction.

replication_title: The Relationship between Physical and Sexual Abuse and Illicit Drug Use: A Replication among a New Sample of Youths Entering a Juvenile Detention Center
effect_name: Childhood abuse and illicit drug use among detained youths
effect_claim: Greater childhood physical and sexual abuse was associated with greater illicit drug use among detained youths.
effect_claim_quote: The results indicate that the youths' physical and sexual abuse experiences are significantly and positively related to their use of illicit drugs.
original_title: The Relationship Between Physical and Sexual Abuse and Tobacco, Alcohol, and Illicit Drug Use Among Youths in a Juvenile Detention Center
replication_target_quote: Our previous study of this association found that a sample of detained youths' physical and sexual abuse experiences were related significantly and positively to their use of illicit drugs.
outcome_quote: Data gathered from a new sample of detained juveniles, interviewed 3 years after our first study, relating to this issue were examined and our previous findings were replicated.
review_note: Same lead-author group; later abstract explicitly identifies the prior detained-youth study and a new independent sample interviewed three years later. NLM PubMed records for original PMID 3384507 and replication PMID 3235226 explicitly state publication months 1988 Apr and 1988 Nov respectively; date fields use the first day solely as month-level schema placeholders. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Tripartite influence model fit for body dissatisfaction and eating disturbance
effect_claim: A tripartite model involving peer, parent, and media influences adequately fit adolescent girls’ body dissatisfaction and eating disturbance data.
effect_claim_quote: A resulting model was found to be an adequate fit to the data, supporting the viability of the Tripartite Model as a useful framework for understanding processes that may predispose young women to develop body image disturbances and eating dysfunction.
original_title: An evaluation of the Tripartite Influence Model of body dissatisfaction and eating disturbance with adolescent girls
replication_title: The tripartite influence model of body image and eating disturbance: A replication with a Japanese sample
replication_target_quote: An evaluation of the tripartite influence model of body dissatisfaction and eating disturbance with adolescent girls.
outcome_quote: Fit indices indicated a moderate fit to the overall tripartite model, replicating previous findings.
review_note: Later publisher references Keery et al. (2004) as reference 3; same tripartite model tested in Japanese women. Original abstract is hosted by the original author institution. Later publisher abstract reports moderate model fit and says it replicated previous findings. OpenAlex later W2090726979 primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Type A behavior and early arrival
effect_claim: People with Type A behavior arrived earlier at experimental sessions than people with Type B behavior.
effect_claim_quote: Type As) arrived earlier than those Ss who did not exhibit this behavior pattern (Type Bs).
original_title: Time urgency of the Type A behavior pattern.
original_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
replication_title: Type a Behavior Pattern, Time Urgency and Arrival Time: A Replication
replication_target_quote: The finding by Gastorf (1980) that 11 subjects classified as Type A arrived significantly earlier at experimental sessions than those 17 classed as Type B was not replicated.
outcome_quote: There were no differences between the A and B groups, but both were significantly later in arriving than 25 “average” subjects.
review_note: Later primary field Psychology. Original APA publisher preview hosted by ResearchGate provides exact Type A/B arrival result. Later abstract names Gastorf and the original result, then reports no Type A/B difference.

effect_name: Factor II psychopathy links lower self-esteem and aggression
effect_claim: Factor II psychopathic traits were associated with lower self-esteem and more aggression.
effect_claim_quote: those with more pathological narcissism and Factor 2 features of psychopathy had lower self-esteem and more aggression
original_title: Using self-esteem to disaggregate psychopathy, narcissism, and aggression
replication_title: A Replication of ``Using self-esteem to disaggregate psychopathy, narcissism, and aggression (2013)''
replication_target_quote: The purpose of the present study is to replicate the previous findings to further confirm the relationship between psychopathy, narcissism, aggression, and self-esteem in a community sample.
outcome_quote: The PPI-II of the current study was negatively associated with self-esteem and positively associated with aggression, as in previous findings
review_note: Narrow Factor-II psychopathy claim is repeated. Other narcissism/self-esteem correlations differed, so this row does not claim the whole study replicated. Later paper names exact Falkenbach, Howe, Falki 2013 original; result from publisher-hosted PDF. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology.

effect_name: Extraversion and neuroticism predict motor reminiscence
effect_claim: Extraversion and higher neuroticism were both associated with greater pursuit-rotor reminiscence after massed practice.
effect_claim_quote: The hypothesis was confirmed, and reminiscence was also found to be significantly greater for Ss high in neuroticism.
original_title: Reminiscence, drive, and personality theory
original_journal: Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology
replication_title: Reminiscence, Drive and Personality Theory: Replication
replication_target_quote: In a modified replication of Eysenck's (1956) study
outcome_quote: similar relations between extraversion and reminiscence were obtained. However, the relations between neuroticism and reminiscence contradicted Eysenck's findings.
review_note: Author archive of original published paper supports both directional personality relations. Later abstract explicitly names Eysenck 1956 and finds extraversion relation similar but neuroticism relation contradictory; hence mixed. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology.

effect_name: Moss-Harlow reward effect varies with child age
effect_claim: Young preschoolers performed object discrimination best after nonrewarded information, whereas older children did not show that benefit.
effect_claim_quote: The performance of the younger children was most efficient following nonrewarded information trials
original_title: The Moss-Harlow effect in preschool children as a function of age
replication_title: The Moss-Harlow Effect in Young Children: Replication
replication_target_quote: This finding supports the results of Cross and Vaughter (1966)
outcome_quote: younger Ss displayed the Moss-Harlow effect but older Ss did not.
review_note: Later author Cross coauthored both papers. Original publisher abstract is quoted in publisher-preview section for the exact paper on ResearchGate; later abstract explicitly says age interaction supports Cross and Vaughter 1966. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology.

effect_name: Stable identity status and lower conformity
effect_claim: People in stable identity statuses conformed less on an Asch task than people in unstable identity statuses.
effect_claim_quote: Ss in "stable" identity statuses (achievement and foreclosure) conformed less than those in "unstable" statuses (moratorium and diffusion)
original_title: Ego identity status and response to conformity pressure in college women.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Ego identity status, conformity behavior, and personality in late adolescence.
replication_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_target_quote: The investigations were undertaken to replicate the earlier research findings of Toder and Marcia (1973).
outcome_quote: However, no relation was observed between identity status and conformity on the Asch task.
review_note: Later primary field Psychology. Original APA publisher-preview abstract contains exact Asch-task result. Later paper explicitly names Toder and Marcia and reports no identity-status relation on the same Asch task; its third study supported a broader relation via other measures, so page is narrowly scoped to Asch result.

original_title: THE EFFECTS OF A SELF‐INSTRUCTIONAL PACKAGE ON OVERACTIVE PRESCHOOL BOYS
replication_title: Self-instructional training with preschoolers: an attempt to replicate
effect_name: Self-instructional training increases classroom on-task behavior
effect_claim: A brief self-instructional package increased classroom on-task behavior among overactive preschool boys.
effect_claim_quote: On-task behaviors increased dramatically concomitant with the introduction of the self-instructional package
replication_target_quote: We attempted to replicate an intervention program by Bornstein and Quevillon (1976)
outcome_quote: Although the subject population and procedures were quite similar across studies, our self-instructional training did not produce socially significant, durable increases in either appropriate classroom behavior or changes in teacher ratings of the children's behavior.
review_note: Published article explicitly names Bornstein and Quevillon (1976), the exact original already source-reviewed in another promoted pair. PubMed later abstract reports the self-instructional training did not produce durable classroom improvements. OpenAlex later W1982571853 primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Radex structure of work values
effect_claim: Work values formed a radex structure organized by outcome modality and performance contingency.
effect_claim_quote: An empirical double-ordered conceptual system, a radex structure, was obtained
original_title: Facets of work values: A structural analysis of work outcomes.
replication_title: A Cross-Cultural Replication on Elizur's Facets of Work Values
replication_target_quote: A slightly refined version of Elizur's (1984) 2-facetted theory on the structure of work values is investigated in this study.
outcome_quote: This confirms Elizur's finding of a radex structure.
review_note: Later primary field Psychology. Later publisher abstract names Elizur 1984, repeats the two-facet analysis in German samples, and explicitly confirms radex structure. Original APA publisher-preview abstract hosted by ResearchGate supplies exact radex result.

effect_name: Daily hassles predict health after accounting for major life events
effect_claim: Daily hassles remained associated with health after statistically controlling major life events.
effect_claim_quote: Hassles shared most of the variance in health that could be accounted for by life events, and when the effects of life events were statistically removed, hassles and health remained significantly related.
original_title: Relationship of daily hassles, uplifts, and major life events to health status
replication_title: Hassles and health: A replication
replication_target_quote: Contrary to findings by A. de Longis et al
outcome_quote: Hassles scores were significant predictors of overall health status when the effects due to life experiences were controlled.
review_note: Later primary OpenAlex Psychology. Narrow claimed effect is the partial association of hassles and health after adjusting life events; later abstract confirms it. Later study disagrees with the original about total variance explained, so this row does not claim that broader result replicated. Both quotes transcribed from primary APA publisher abstract previews on ResearchGate.

effect_name: Children and adults share two dimensions of facial emotion concepts
effect_claim: Children’s and adults’ facial emotion concepts share a two-dimensional structure.
effect_claim_quote: Multidimensional scaling of the word/facial expression associations yielded a two-dimensional structure able to account for the interrelationships among emotions, and this structure was the same for all age groups.
original_title: Preschool Children's Interpretation of Facial Expressions of Emotion
replication_title: The Development of Emotional Concepts: A Replication with a German Sample
replication_target_quote: Bullock & Russell 1984, 1985, 1986
outcome_quote: Although slight differences emerged for the meanings of single emotion terms we confirmed the previous findings, thus adding validity to the model outlined by Bullock and Russell (1986).
review_note: Both abstracts on original SAGE publisher pages. Later abstract explicitly cites Bullock and Russell 1984, 1985, 1986 and reports successful cross-cultural replication of the two-dimensional emotion-concept model. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Teacher verbal instructions reduce preschool aggression
effect_claim: Brief verbal instructions from a teacher decreased aggressive behavior in preschool children.
effect_claim_quote: The children who were instructed significantly decreased in their level of aggressive behavior.
original_title: The effect of verbal instructions on preschool children's aggressive behavior
replication_title: Effects of Brief Verbal Instructions on Aggression: A Replication in a Head Start Setting
replication_target_quote: The present study attempted to replicate the findings of the Zahavi and Asher(1978)study with Head Start preschoolers.
outcome_quote: Thus, no firm conclusion could be reached as to whether the significant improvements in observed positive and negative behavior evinced across this period were actually due to treatment.
review_note: Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology. Later abstract explicitly names Zahavi and Asher 1978. Original author manuscript at ERIC has same title, authors, design and result; published 1978 article abstract on author ResearchGate profile corroborates. Teacher-rated prosocial gains occurred, but observed aggression/positive behavior lacked firm treatment attribution.

effect_name: Well-being and conversation quality
effect_claim: Higher well-being was associated with less small talk and more substantive conversations.
effect_claim_quote: Higher well-being was associated with having less small talk, r = -.33, and more substantive conversations, r = .28.
original_title: Eavesdropping on Happiness: Well-being is Related to Having Less Small Talk and More Substantive Conversations
replication_title: “Eavesdropping on Happiness” Revisited: A Pooled, Multisample Replication of the Association Between Life Satisfaction and Observed Daily Conversation Quantity and Quality
replication_target_quote: individuals with higher well-being tend to spend less time alone and more time interacting with others (e.g., greater conversation quantity) and engage in less small talk and more substantive conversations (e.g., greater conversation quality).
outcome_quote: We found moderate associations between life satisfaction and amount of alone time, conversation time, and substantive conversations, but no reliable association with small talk.
review_note: Published replication DOI used; PsyArXiv 10.31234/osf.io/jnqu4 is its earlier preprint with matching authors, sample total, and result abstract, but is omitted as an alias because its title/year differ in discovery metadata. The combined original conversation-quality effect had two directions: less small talk and more substantive conversations with higher well-being. The later SAGE abstract found a moderate association for substantive conversations but no reliable association with small talk, so the exact combined effect is mixed, agreeing with existing FORRT/Flora outcome. Original result quote is in primary PMC full-text Results; later target/outcome are in SAGE publisher abstract. Later OpenAlex W2811391847 indexed primary Field Psychology (Social Psychology subfield). SAGE publisher says analyses were not preregistered.

effect_name: Word-level uncertainty during reading
effect_claim: Readers can retain uncertainty about a previously seen word and use later sentence context to revise its identity.
effect_claim_quote: readers maintain uncertain beliefs about previously read word identities
original_title: Eye movement evidence that readers maintain and act on uncertainty about past linguistic input
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
replication_title: Do readers maintain word-level uncertainty during reading? A pre-registered replication study
replication_target_quote: We present a replication of Levy, Bicknell, Slattery, and Rayner (2009).
outcome_quote: Using Bayesian statistical techniques we show that in our dataset there is evidence against the existence of the interaction Levy et al. found, and thus conclude that this study is non-replicable.
review_note: Direct high-powered replication of exact Levy/Bicknell/Slattery/Rayner 2009 original, at/as versus toward sentence-processing interaction; later journal abstract rejects it. Later OpenAlex W4280555944 primary Psychology.

effect_name: Valuing happiness correlates with depressive symptoms
effect_claim: In U.S. samples, people who placed greater value on feeling happy reported more depressive symptoms.
effect_claim_quote: valuing happiness was associated with increased depressive symptoms in a community sample with remitted major depressive disorder
original_title: Desperately Seeking Happiness: Valuing Happiness Is Associated With Symptoms and Diagnosis of Depression
original_journal: Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology
replication_title: Valuing Happiness is Not a Good Way of Pursuing Happiness, but Prioritizing Positivity is: A Replication Study
replication_target_quote: the negative association of valuing happiness on well-being measures, as reported in previous studies ( Catalino et al., 2014 ; Datu & King, 2016 ; Ford et al., 2014
outcome_quote: valuing happiness leads to feelings of depression and loneliness, and partly diminishes the happiness felt.
review_note: Later primary full-text XML explicitly cites exact Ford et al. 2014 DOI and names negative association with well-being; replicated positive association between valuing happiness and depressive symptoms. Later OpenAlex W3213666256 primary Psychology.

effect_name: Threatening animals are detected faster in visual search
effect_claim: Participants detected threat-relevant animals more rapidly than nonthreatening animals in visual search arrays.
effect_claim_quote: Both the children and the adults detected snakes more rapidly than three types of nonthreatening stimuli
original_title: Detecting the Snake in the Grass
replication_title: Many Labs 5: Registered Replication of LoBue and DeLoache (2008)
replication_journal: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science
replication_target_quote: Across three studies, LoBue and DeLoache (2008) provided evidence suggesting that both young children and adults exhibit enhanced visual detection of evolutionarily relevant threat stimuli
outcome_quote: Overall, participants were not significantly faster at detecting threatening stimuli. Thus, results were not supportive of the hypothesis that visual detection of evolutionarily relevant threat stimuli is enhanced in young children.
review_note: Registered multi-site replication of original LoBue and DeLoache 2008 snake/threat visual search, two protocols, no faster threat detection. Later OpenAlex W3100119188 primary Psychology.

effect_name: Tempting-fate actions raise perceived chance of negative outcomes
effect_claim: People judged a negative outcome as more likely after an action perceived as tempting fate.
effect_claim_quote: actions that tempt fate increase the likelihood of negative outcomes.
original_title: Why people are reluctant to tempt fate.
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Many Labs 5: Registered Multisite Replication of the Tempting-Fate Effects in Risen and Gilovich (2008)
replication_journal: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science
replication_target_quote: Risen and Gilovich (2008) found that subjects believed that “tempting fate” would be punished with ironic bad outcomes (a main effect)
outcome_quote: Results from these sites did not support the interaction or the main effect
review_note: Registered multisite replication explicitly names Risen/Gilovich 2008 and fails its main tempting-fate effect under revised protocol; later OpenAlex W3102574417 primary Psychology. Earlier manuscript version: https://doi.org/10.31219/osf.io/sy4b9. It reports this same replication sample and is linked here, counted once.

effect_name: Verb familiarity helps children correct unusual word order
effect_claim: Children corrected noncanonical word order more often with a familiar verb than with a novel verb.

original_title: What preschool children do and do not do with ungrammatical word orders
replication_title: Learning to construct sentences in Spanish: a replication of the Weird Word Order technique
replication_target_quote: As in prior studies (Abbot-Smith et al., 2001; Chang et al., 2009; Franck et al., 2011; Matthews et al., 2005, 2007)

review_note: Later PubMed abstract explicitly cites Abbot-Smith et al. 2001 among prior Weird Word Order studies and reports the same directional familiarity/frequency effect in Spanish children. Original result quote is from author-posted primary article text. This is a conceptual cross-language replication. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Quadratic growth of tense productivity in toddlers
effect_claim: Toddlers’ tense productivity growth from 21 to 30 months was best described by a quadratic model without an intercept.
effect_claim_quote: A random effects quadratic growth model with no intercept best characterized the growth of tense marking between 21 and 30 months.

replication_title: Growth of finiteness in the third year of life: replication and predictive validity

replication_target_quote: replicating the findings of Rispoli, Hadley, and Holt (2009)

effect_name: Mandarin vertical time representation
effect_claim: Mandarin speakers showed a stronger vertical spatial representation of time than English speakers, even when tested in English.

replication_target_quote: Boroditsky [Boroditsky, L. (2001). Does language shape thought? Mandarin and English speakers' conceptions of time. Cognitive Psychology, 43(1), 1-22] claimed that they do

effect_name: Maternal responses to achievement and fear of failure

replication_title: Childhood development of fear of failure motivation: a replication
replication_target_quote: Teevan and McGhee found (1972) as predicted
outcome_quote: This finding is interpreted as a validation of Teevan and McGhee's (1972) conclusions

effect_name: Care staff immediate strategies for challenging behaviour
effect_claim: Institution care staff described immediate interventions for challenging behaviour that resembled counter-habilitative strategies.

original_title: Staff strategies and explanations for intervening with challenging behaviours
replication_title: Staff strategies and explanations for intervening with challenging behaviours: a replication in a community sample
replication_target_quote: The present study replicated previous work on the beliefs of institution staff and their explanations about interventions for challenging behaviours (Hastings 1996)
outcome_quote: These basic findings confirmed those of previous research with institution staff.
review_note: Original PubMed abstract reports immediate strategies resembling counter-habilitative strategies; later university-repository abstract names Hastings (1996) and says the basic findings confirmed. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Task success and task liking
effect_claim: Higher success on a task was associated with greater liking and satisfaction in a positive linear relationship.
effect_claim_quote: In all cases there was clear evidence for a significant (positive) linear relationship between success and measures of liking and satisfaction.
original_title: The relationship of task success to task liking and satisfaction.
replication_title: Relationship of Task Success to Task Liking: A Replication
