outcome_quote: State extraversion was found to have a strong effect on positive affect in a 10-minute dyadic discussion.
review_note: Exact original is McNiel and Fleeson 2006, explicitly named as in press in the 2007 UNC dissertation. This supersedes the provisional Fleeson et al. 2002 link. DataCite primary repository metadata for DOI 10.17615/b4r2-x317 gives publicationYear 2007; 2019 is the repository DOI registration year. Thesis alters the original triadic discussions to opposite-sex dyads and reproduces the positive-affect effect. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W167386605). Exact original and later DOIs absent from local FORRT archive and raw CSV registers.

effect_name: Mortality reminders increase blame toward innocent victims
effect_claim: Mortality primes increased blame assigned to severely injured innocent victims in the original experiments.
effect_claim_quote: primes of death led to greater attributions of blame to severely injured victims
original_title: Terror management and attributions of blame to innocent victims: Reconciling compassionate and defensive responses
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Do Injustice and Mortality Salience Impact Secondary Victimization Through the Need to Believe in a Just World?
replication_target_quote: Past research has found that victimization of innocents and mortality salience prompts observers to engage in secondary victimization
outcome_quote: we failed to find any substantive effects of exposure to injustice or mortality salience on secondary victimization.
review_note: The later study conceptually replicates earlier mortality-salience victim-blame work and explicitly says a delay task was chosen to match Hirschberger 2006 Study 3; its bibliography gives the exact original DOI. Later results did not find substantive mortality-salience effects. Original abstract also documents Study 3 mortality primes increasing blame for victims of circumstance. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W4319343964). Exact original and later DOIs absent from local FORRT archive and raw CSV registers.

effect_name: Self-esteem moderates distancing after relationship threat
effect_claim: After a relationship threat, people with low self-esteem view their partner and relationship less positively than people with high self-esteem.
effect_claim_quote: Low but not high self-esteem participants read too much into problems, seeing them as a sign that their partner's affections and commitment might be waning.
original_title: When rejection stings: How self-esteem constrains relationship-enhancement processes
original_authors: Murray, Rose, Bellavia, Holmes, and Kusche
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Self-esteem, relationship threat, and dependency regulation: Independent replication of Murray, Rose, Bellavia, Holmes, and Kusche (2002) Study 3
replication_authors: Campbell, Balzarini, Kohut, Dobson, Hahn, Moroz, and Stanton
replication_target_quote: we sought to reproduce the methods and procedures of Study 3 of Murray et al. (2002)

review_note: The later paper identifies and closely reproduces Murray et al. 2002 Study 3. It reports that the threat manipulation check replicated, while the core self-esteem by threat interaction did not appear on any primary outcome. Machine candidate incorrectly linked to Murray et al. 2008 review. Original and later OpenAlex primary field Psychology; original DOI and abstracts independently confirmed by author-affiliated institutional records.

effect_name: Insecure attachment among preschoolers with externalizing problems
effect_claim: Preschool children referred for disruptive behavior are more likely to be classified as insecurely attached than matched nonproblem children.

original_title: Attachment in preschoolers with disruptive behavior: A comparison of clinic-referred and nonproblem children
replication_title: Attachment security in preschoolers with and without externalizing behavior problems: A replication
replication_target_quote: This study attempted to replicate previous findings that indicated that preschool-aged children with significant externalizing problems are more likely to have insecure attachment relations than nonproblem peers (Speltz, Greenberg, & DeKlyen, 1990).
outcome_quote: We found that 80% of the clinic-referred children were classified as insecure, whereas only 28% of the comparisons were so classified (p <.001).
review_note: Explicit replication with 25 clinic and 25 comparison children in both samples; insecure attachment 84% versus 28% originally and 80% versus 28% later. Machine original was wrong.

effect_name: Short versus long spacing for child L2 vocabulary learning
effect_claim: Child EFL learners retain more classroom vocabulary after a one-day gap between training episodes than after an eight-day gap.
effect_claim_quote: the results here indicated superior learning of the items presented under the spaced-short format

replication_title: DOES IT MATTER WHEN YOU REVIEW?
replication_target_quote: This study is a conceptual replication of Rogers and Cheung’s (2018) investigation into distribution of practice effects on the learning of L2 vocabulary in child EFL classrooms in Hong Kong.
outcome_quote: this study found large learning gains across the experimental conditions with no significant differences between the two learning schedules.
review_note: Conceptual replication of the original relative spacing advantage with Hong Kong child EFL learners; no significant schedule difference in later 66-student sample despite learning gains. Original and later first online years are 2018 and 2020; machine original was wrong.

effect_name: Infant learning of nonadjacent dependencies with variable middle elements
effect_claim: Infants can detect a dependency between the first and third elements of artificial language strings when the middle element varies enough to make adjacent dependencies unpredictable.
effect_claim_quote: Infants and adults acquired nonadjacent dependencies only when adjacent dependencies were least predictable.
original_title: Variability and Detection of Invariant Structure
replication_title: The Developmental Trajectory of Nonadjacent Dependency Learning
replication_target_quote: Experiment 1 replicated the study of Gómez with a younger age group and a more subtle variability manipulation.
outcome_quote: Twelve-month-olds failed to track nonadjacent dependencies under conditions tested here (Experiments 2a and 2b), but by 15 months, infants are beginning to track this structure (Experiment 3).
review_note: Original 18-month-old infants learned under high middle-element variability; the 2005 extension explicitly replicated the study and found an age dependent outcome: 12-month-olds failed while 15-month-olds began tracking. Wiley 2010 page date reflects digitization; version of record March 2005. Machine original was wrong.

effect_name: APOE ε4 amplifies combat exposure association with PTSD
effect_claim: Among Black Iraq/Afghanistan-era veterans, APOE ε4 dosage strengthened the association between high combat exposure and PTSD diagnosis and symptom severity.
effect_claim_quote: within the NHB sample, significant gene × environment (G × E) interactions were observed for lifetime PTSD (P = .0029) and PTSD symptom severity (P = .0009).
original_title: Effect of the APOE ε4 Allele and Combat Exposure on PTSD among Iraq/Afghanistan-Era Veterans
original_authors: Kimbrel, Hauser, Garrett, Ashley-Koch, Liu, Dennis, Klein, and Beckham
replication_title: No replication of Alzheimer’s disease genetics as a moderator of the association between combat exposure and PTSD risk in 138,592 combat veterans
replication_authors: Wolf, Miller, Zhang, Sherva, Harrington, Fonda, Daskalakis, Gaziano, and Logue

original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Heart rate change and attitudes to global warming: A conceptual replication of the visceral fit mechanism
replication_target_quote: The present research represents a conceptual replication and extension of Risen and Critcher's (2011) finding that the physical experience of warmth increases belief in global warming.
outcome_quote: In three of the studies, increased heart rate was associated with greater self-reported belief that global warming was occurring.
review_note: The later publisher introduction explicitly identifies Risen and Critcher 2011 as the target and tests a hypothesized internal warmth route by altering heart rate rather than room temperature. Increased heart rate related to global-warming belief in three of four studies, with small overall effect (d=0.20) and very small absolute change. Code mixed for conceptual support with one non-supporting study and an unmeasured warmth mediation. The machine-linked Blanchard 1972 paper supplied only a heart-rate control technique, not the effect. Both OpenAlex primary Psychology.

effect_name: CLASS increases appropriate classroom behavior
effect_claim: The CLASS classroom intervention increased appropriate behavior among acting-out primary-grade children relative to controls.
effect_claim_quote: Results indicate that the experimentals, in contrast to the controls, significantly increased their proportion of appropriate behavior
original_title: CLASS: A standardized in-class program for acting-out children: II. Field test evaluations
original_authors: Hyman Hops, Hill M. Walker, Diane Hernandez Fleischman, Jack T. Nagoshi, Robert T. Omura, Karl Skindrud, and Judson Taylor
replication_title: Replication of the CLASS Program in Costa Rica
replication_authors: Hill M. Walker, Gerardo Fonseca Retana, and Russell Gersten
replication_target_quote: The CLASS program has been applied successfully in the United States, but its effects have not been previously tested in a cross-cultural setting.
outcome_quote: mean differences favoring the experimental group were obtained at post.
review_note: Relinked the screen’s Walker and Hops 1979 program overview to the original empirical Hops et al. 1978 CLASS field test, which the Costa Rica article cites directly. Later random assignment found postintervention differences favoring CLASS. Original quote is from the abstract of a scan of the original article. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W1991721904).

effect_name: Suicide acceptability depends on illness and victim gender
effect_claim: The precipitating illness and victim gender in a hypothetical suicide scenario affected evaluators’ acceptability judgments.
effect_claim_quote: Evaluations of suicide tended to be significantly more favorable when the evaluators were male, when male victims were being judged, when elderly victims were being evaluated, or when terminal cancer was the precipitating illness.
original_title: Factors Affecting the Acceptability of Suicide
original_journal: OMEGA - Journal of Death and Dying
replication_title: Factors Affecting the Unacceptability of Suicide and the Effects of Evaluator Depression and Religiosity
replication_authors: Charles T. Lo Presto, Martin F. Sherman, and Margaret A. Dicarlo
replication_journal: OMEGA - Journal of Death and Dying
replication_target_quote: This study represents a partial replication and extension of Deluty's investigations of the factors affecting suicide unacceptability [1].
outcome_quote: the unacceptability of suicide is a function of precipitating illness and gender of victim
review_note: Later article’s reference [1] is this exact Deluty paper. This is a partial replication: both papers report dependence on precipitating illness and victim gender; the later abstract does not disclose factor directions and also reports complex interactions. Effect claim and outcome therefore concern the shared variables, not the original directional pattern or untested victim-age effect. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W2087901429).

effect_name: Isolated functional analysis identifies only the trained function
effect_claim: In a translational test with a pre-trained surrogate response, isolated functional analysis correctly identified its trained maintaining function without generating extra functions.
effect_claim_quote: The traditional FA correctly identified the previously established function of the target response in all six cases and produced no iatrogenic effects.
original_title: A translational evaluation of potential iatrogenic effects of single and combined contingencies during functional analysis
original_authors: Billie J. Retzlaff, Wayne W. Fisher, Justin S. Akers, and Brian D. Greer
replication_title: Further Translational Evaluations of Efficacy and Preference for Isolated and Synthesized Contingency Procedures
replication_authors: Emma M. Auten, Casey Irwin Helvey, and Carole Van Camp
replication_target_quote: The purpose of Experiment 1 was to replicate Retzlaff et al.
outcome_quote: Results showed that the isolated FA only identified the trained function.
review_note: Auten et al. explicitly identify and cite Retzlaff et al. 2020 and repeat the pre-trained surrogate-response comparison. The abstract reports the same isolated-FA diagnostic specificity; no claim is made here about replication of the original three-of-six SCA iatrogenic effect. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W4406643964).

effect_name: Dopamine transporter allele association with smoking cessation
effect_claim: The dopamine transporter SLC6A3-9 polymorphism is associated with smoking status through smoking cessation rather than initiation.
effect_claim_quote: A significant association between SLC6A3-9 and smoking status was confirmed and was due to an effect on cessation rather than initiation.
original_title: A genetic association for cigarette smoking behavior
replication_title: Association of smoking and personality with a polymorphism of the dopamine transporter gene: Results from a community survey
replication_target_quote: We attempted to replicate this association in a nonvolunteer community sample of 861 Caucasians.
outcome_quote: No associations were found with either smoking initiation or smoking cessation.
review_note: Jorm et al. explicitly attempted to replicate the Lerman and Sabol 1999 DAT1 smoking associations. This row targets Sabol et al. 1999, whose PubMed abstract attributes its smoking-status association to cessation. The later nonvolunteer community sample found no association for either initiation or cessation. Machine original Vandenbergh 1992 was a gene-mapping paper, not the reported association.

effect_name: Semantic and response competition components of color-word Stroop
effect_claim: The color-word Stroop effect includes both stimulus-stimulus semantic compatibility and stimulus-response competition components.
effect_claim_quote: the results revealed an effect of SSC and an effect of SRC that was based on short-term associations.
original_title: On the role of stimulus-response and stimulus-stimulus compatibility in the Stroop effect
replication_title: Dissociating Stimulus-Stimulus and Response-Response Effects in the Stroop Task.
replication_journal: Canadian Journal of Experimental Psychology/Revue canadienne de psychologie expérimentale
replication_target_quote: The results using colour words replicated the findings of De Houwer (2003)
outcome_quote: demonstrated both a semantic effect (a difference between same response trials and identity trials) and response competition (a difference between same response trials and different response trials).
review_note: Schmidt and Cheesman explicitly report replicating De Houwer 2003 with colour words and finding both semantic and response competition contrasts. Their color-associate extension had only a semantic effect; this row targets the direct color-word comparison. Machine original was unrelated.

effect_name: Pronoun modulation of perspective in simple action sentences
effect_claim: In simple action sentences, second-person or first-person pronouns promote an actor perspective whereas third-person pronouns promote an external perspective.
effect_claim_quote: Experiment 1 demonstrated that readers embody an actor's perspective when the pronoun you or I is used, but take an external perspective when he is used.
original_title: When You and I Share Perspectives: Pronouns Modulate Perspective Taking During Narrative Comprehension
replication_title: Mentally simulating narrative perspective is not universal or necessary for language comprehension.
replication_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Learning Memory and Cognition
replication_target_quote: Experiment 1 used an extended sample (N = 263) and replicated an interactive influence of pronouns on perspectives adopted during reading simple action sentences
outcome_quote: with You promoting an agent's perspective, and He promoting an onlooker's external perspective.
review_note: Brunyé et al. 2016 Experiment 1 is an extended-sample replication of the simple-action-sentence pronoun by perspective effect from Brunyé et al. 2009. Code only that specified effect as successful. The later extended-narrative Experiment 2 was less robust, which limits generality but does not reverse the direct Experiment 1 result. Original DOI first appeared online in 2008 and is cited in its 2009 journal issue.

effect_name: Difference mindset increases spontaneous visual perspective taking
effect_claim: Priming attention to self-other differences makes speakers more likely to describe an object from another person's visual perspective than a similarity mindset does.
effect_claim_quote: directly priming a difference mind-set made perceivers more likely to spontaneously adopt other people's visual perspectives (Experiment 1)
original_title: When Focusing on Differences Leads to Similar Perspectives
replication_title: Changing views: the effect of explicit perception-focus instructions on perspective-taking
replication_target_quote: we attempted to replicate previous findings showing that a mind-set focusing on self-other differences incites speakers to adopt another’s viewpoint in a subsequent task.
outcome_quote: speakers focusing on self-other differences were just as likely to describe an object’s location from their egocentric perspective as speakers focusing on self-other similarities.
review_note: Damen et al. 2019 explicitly replicated Todd et al. 2011 Experiment 1 picture-comparison mindset prime and visual spatial-description task with a larger sample; the difference versus similarity contrast did not emerge. Their second experiment used explicit perspective instructions and is outside this target. Todd DOI appeared online in 2010 and in the 2011 issue; machine original was unrelated.

effect_name: Ingroup modulation of negative-emotion facial mimicry
effect_claim: Angry and fearful faces from ingroup members elicit stronger facial mimicry than the same expressions from outgroup members.
effect_claim_quote: both studies show that ingroup anger and fear displays were mimicked to a greater extent than outgroup displays of these emotions.
original_title: Convergent and divergent responses to emotional displays of ingroup and outgroup
replication_title: Mimicry of ingroup and outgroup emotional expressions
replication_target_quote: We therefore first aimed to replicate Study 2 of van der Schalk, Fischer et al. (2011), specifically testing the finding of differences in emotional mimicry for models from different ethnic groups.
outcome_quote: The effect of group membership was not replicated, however, similar to the results of the FaceReader data.
review_note: Sachisthal et al. explicitly attempted to replicate van der Schalk et al. 2011 Study 2 using the same emotional face stimuli and a similar student sample. Neither automatic FaceReader coding nor exploratory FACS coding reproduced the ingroup-versus-outgroup modulation of facial mimicry. FACS did recover anger/fear mimicry in general, so code only the group-membership interaction as failed. Later study used within-subjects groups versus original between-subjects. Machine original was a review.

effect_name: False-belief tracking guides anticipatory looking
effect_claim: Twenty-five-month-old children anticipated an actor’s action based on the actor’s false belief in an eye-tracking task.
effect_claim_quote: Our data demonstrate that 25-month-old infants correctly anticipate an actor's actions when these actions can be predicted only by attributing a false belief to the actor.
original_title: Action Anticipation Through Attribution of False Belief by 2-Year-Olds
original_authors: Victoria Southgate, Atsushi Senju, and Gergely Csibra
replication_title: Is implicit Theory of Mind real but hard to detect? Testing adults with different stimulus materials
replication_authors: Louisa Kulke, Marieke Wübker, and Hannes Rakoczy
replication_target_quote: tasks structurally analogous to those used by Southgate et al. [17]
outcome_quote: In the removal conditions, only the FB1 condition was significantly replicated in Study 1, while the more controlled FB2 condition was at chance.
review_note: Corrected the screen’s Kovács et al. 2010 object-detection-RT link to the directly named and cited Southgate, Senju and Csibra 2007 anticipatory-looking study. Kulke et al. conceptually adapted that task for adults with more engaging stimuli. Their full text says the FB1 looking-time effect partly recurred in Study 1, but the controlled FB2 condition and Study 2 did not confirm it; mixed is the authors’ explicit summary. Original participants were 25-month-olds whereas later participants were adults. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W2958996772).

effect_name: Point-loss punishment shifts human choice
effect_claim: In a two-alternative human choice task, contingent money loss acted as punishment and reduced allocation to the punished alternative.
effect_claim_quote: Experiment 1 verified that money loss was an effective punisher in this context.
original_title: Punishment in Human Choice: Direct or Competitive Suppression?
original_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior
replication_title: Punishment in a Procedure for Rapidly Establishing Steady-State Behavior: A Replication
replication_target_quote: We replicated this experiment with the Procedure for Rapidly Establishing Steady-State Behavior (PRESS-B) using point-loss as the punisher.
outcome_quote: Compared to their respective baseline conditions, all punished conditions showed a decreased median proportion of time allocated to the punished alternative.
review_note: The later article cites Critchfield et al. (2003), whose Experiment 1 tested monetary losses superimposed on one choice alternative under concurrent reinforcement. The later study uses PRESS-B and point loss, so the exact schedule differs, but the tested choice-shift effect is the same. The machine-linked 2021 PRESS-B methodological paper was not the original punishment result. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology.

effect_name: Computer instruction improves discrete trial implementation
effect_claim: A video-based observation and rating module improved staff implementation of discrete trial instruction, including novel skills.
effect_claim_quote: The procedure was effective, and the effects extended to novel skills.
original_title: The Influence of Observations and Ratings on Implementation of Discrete Trial Instruction
original_authors: Romer, Vladescu, Marano, Reeve, Sidener, and Campanaro
replication_title: Using Computer-Based Instruction to Teach Implementation of Discrete Trial Instruction: A Replication and Extension
replication_target_quote: The purpose of the present study was to address the gaps in Romer et al. (2021) by assessing the same computer-based instruction module to train relevant staff to implement discrete trial instruction.
outcome_quote: Results suggest computer-based instruction is effective, efficient, and a socially valid procedure to use to teach relevant staff to implement discrete trial instruction.
review_note: The later article explicitly tests the same module as Romer et al. (2021) with relevant staff. Both measure implementation of discrete trial instruction. The original article calls its own design a replication; this row concerns the subsequent Campanaro/Vladescu test. The later journal issue is 2023 but its online publication was 2022. The machine-linked Amador study concerned trial-based functional analysis, not this intervention-outcome pair. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology.

effect_name: Self-relevant prime-target interference in depression
effect_claim: Depressed participants had longer color-naming latencies when both prime and target adjectives were self-descriptive than when only the target was self-descriptive.
effect_claim_quote: For self-descriptive adjectives alone this effect was significant for the depressed group.
original_title: A Structural Analysis of the Self-Schema Construct in Major Depression
replication_title: Self-Schema in Major Depression: Replication and Extension of a Priming Methodology
replication_target_quote: The present study was designed in an effort to replicate earlier research utilizing a priming methodology to examine cognitive organization in depression.
outcome_quote: This effect was obtained for adjectives rated as highly self-descriptive with both depressed patients and normal subjects who were in a heightened state of self-awareness.
review_note: The original abstract defines the effect as longer color-naming latencies when both prime and target are self-descriptive versus target alone, significant for the depressed group. The later abstract reports the same prime-target latency effect in depressed patients and extends it to self-focused nondepressed participants; its references include Segal et al. (1988). The machine-linked 1986 paper did not establish this particular priming result. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology.

effect_name: Concurrent operant analysis can identify functional reinforcers
effect_claim: Concurrent operant analysis outcomes were validated by matched intervention results for two students with low work completion.
effect_claim_quote: intervention results validated COA outcomes for two of these participants.
original_title: An Initial Evaluation of a Concurrent Operant Analysis Framework to Identify Reinforcers for Work Completion
original_authors: Blair P. Lloyd, Kayla R. Randall, Emily S. Weaver, Johanna L. Staubitz, and Naomi Parikh
replication_title: Concurrent Operant Analysis Validation: A Brief Report
replication_authors: Kayla R. Randall, Cameron N. Long, and Andrew J. Bulla
replication_journal: Single Case in the Social Sciences
replication_target_quote: Lloyd et al. (2020) used COAs to develop function-based treatments to increase work completion for four students with emotional/behavioral disorders in a classroom setting as an alternative assessment to an FA.
outcome_quote: Results indicated escape was a reinforcer for Amelia’s choice allocation in the COA and confirmed as a reinforcer for target responding in the COA validation.
review_note: Completed, peer-reviewed ten-page brief report, extending Lloyd et al. 2020 from school work completion to one child’s challenging behavior. The author-uploaded full text explicitly describes the Lloyd study as precedent. The shared narrow finding is that COA outcomes can be experimentally validated as identifying functional reinforcers: two of four original participants and the later single case. The later report is a conceptual extension and does not replicate the original classroom population or work-completion endpoint. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W4408012688).

effect_name: Abstract language primes global visual processing
effect_claim: Priming adjectives rather than verbs produces a more global rather than local perceptual focus.
effect_claim_quote: abstract versus concrete language leads to a more global versus local perceptual focus was supported across 4 experiments
original_title: The magic spell of language: Linguistic categories and their perceptual consequences
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Perceptual effects of linguistic category priming: The Stapel and Semin (2007) paradigm revisited in twelve experiments
replication_target_quote: An initial article reported that priming abstract linguistic categories (adjectives) led to more global perceptual processing, whereas priming concrete linguistic categories (verbs) led to more local perceptual processing (Stapel & Semin, 2007).
outcome_quote: The results yielded no evidence of linguistic category priming effects.
review_note: The 2007 Stapel and Semin original was retracted in 2013 (DOI 10.1037/a0031271) after first-author data fabrication; its reported effect is therefore not a credible established finding. The later independent paper explicitly revisited its adjective-versus-verb global/local paradigm in 12 Dutch and US experiments and found no effect. Both OpenAlex primary Psychology; later references the exact original. This page records the attempted replication of a retracted claim.

effect_name: Parafoveal word information shifts first-fixation location
effect_claim: Words with informative endings draw first fixations farther into the word than words with redundant endings.
effect_claim_quote: In the case of words with redundant endings gaining just one fixation, the fixation was nearer to the beginning of the word than in the case of words with informative endings
original_title: How Do Readers Know Where to Look Next? Local Information Distributions Influence Eye Fixations
original_journal: The Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology Section A
replication_title: Eye movement control in reading: Evidence against semantic preprocessing.
replication_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology Human Perception & Performance
replication_target_quote: The basic finding that they have reported is that the eyes move farther into a word when the information that uniquely identifies the word is at the end of the word rather than at the beginning of the word.
outcome_quote: With a highly accurate eyetracking system, the basic finding could not be replicated.
review_note: Rayner and Morris 1992 explicitly attempted and failed to reproduce Underwood, Clews, and Everatt 1990’s informative-ending first-fixation placement effect with accurate eye tracking. Machine original Inhoff 1990 studied parafoveal preview.

effect_name: Trait social anxiety predicts subjective but not objective speech-task arousal
effect_claim: During an impromptu speech, high trait social anxiety is linked to greater self-rated anxiety and bodily arousal without greater objectively measured physiological arousal.
effect_claim_quote: HTSA participants felt more anxious, perceived greater physiological activation, and exhibited more anxiety behaviour than LTSA participants. Unexpectedly, the two groups did not differ in objectively measured physiological responding.
original_title: Is there less to social anxiety than meets the eye? Emotion experience, expression, and bodily responding
replication_title: Implicit Associations and Social Anxiety
replication_target_quote: This was performed in the context of a partial replication of a previous study, in which Mauss et al. (2004)
outcome_quote: higher trait social anxiety was associated with stronger self‐rated anxiety and stronger self‐rated physiological responses, but not with stronger actual physiological responses.
review_note: Westberg et al. explicitly call their impromptu-speech experiment a partial replication of Mauss et al. 2004. Both report higher subjective but not objective physiological responses in high versus low trait social anxiety. The later IAT addition is outside this effect.

effect_name: Case-matched masked-prime advantage for brand names
effect_claim: Masked identity primes matching a brand name’s standard letter case speed identification more than case-mismatched identity primes.
effect_claim_quote: In the masked priming experiment, we found faster identification times of brand names when they were preceded by an identity prime that matched its standard case configuration than when it did not
original_title: Letter‐case information and the identification of brand names
replication_title: Evidence from masked‐priming that initial identification of brand names is via abstract letter identities
replication_target_quote: The present study attempts to replicate this finding using brand names typically presented in all lowercase (e.g., adidas), all uppercase (e.g., IKEA), or titlecase (e.g., Ford).
outcome_quote: Across three masked-priming experiments, we found no advantage for case-matched identity primes over case-mismatched identity primes.
review_note: Martin and Davis 2019 directly tested the masked-prime case-match advantage reported by Perea et al. 2015, across lowercase, uppercase, and titlecase brands. No advantage appeared in three experiments. Perea DOI first online 2014; issue date 2015.

effect_name: Self-control practice improves handgrip persistence
effect_claim: Two weeks of daily self-control practice improves a physical handgrip measure of self-control relative to a control condition.
effect_claim_quote: Compared with a no-exercise control group, the participants who performed the self-control exercises showed significant improvement in self-regulatory capacity as measured by quitting faster on a hand-grip exercise task following a thought-suppression exercise.
original_title: Longitudinal Improvement of Self-Regulation Through Practice: Building Self-Control Strength Through Repeated Exercise
replication_title: How reliable are the effects of self-control training?: A re-examination using self-report and physical measures
replication_target_quote: our study re-examines the effects of self-control training on established physical and self-report measures of self-control.
outcome_quote: compared to a control condition, the physical measure of self-control did not improve.
review_note: Lee and Kemmelmeier 2017 explicitly revisit Muraven et al. 1999 and use the same handgrip physical measure. This is conceptual: the later training task was non-dominant-hand use, whereas Muraven used posture, mood, or food-monitoring exercises, and the original handgrip test followed thought suppression. The later handgrip measure did not improve.

effect_name: Positive face pairing raises implicit self-esteem
effect_claim: Repeatedly pairing self-relevant information with smiling faces increases implicit self-esteem.
effect_claim_quote: This study demonstrated that implicit self-esteem can be increased using a computer game that repeatedly pairs self-relevant information with smiling faces.
original_title: Increasing Implicit Self-Esteem Through Classical Conditioning
replication_title: Manipulating self and other schemas to explore psychological processes associated with paranoid beliefs: an online experimental study
replication_target_quote: The current study aims to replicate Baccus, Espinosa and Trucharte’s findings
outcome_quote: In contrast to what Baccus et al. (2004) and Espinosa et al. (2018) found, implicit self-esteem levels in the proximity-seeking condition did not increase after the intervention.
review_note: Martínez et al. 2025 explicitly cite Baccus et al. 2004 and test positive self-face classical conditioning with implicit self-esteem as an outcome. Their online proximity-seeking condition did not increase implicit self-esteem. The online presentation and neutral-face control differ from the original computer game.

effect_name: Personal involvement strengthens argument-based persuasion
effect_claim: Strong arguments have a greater persuasive effect when the issue has high personal relevance.
effect_claim_quote: under high relevance, attitudes were influenced primarily by the quality of the arguments in the message
original_title: Personal involvement as a determinant of argument-based persuasion
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: One of the most cited persuasion studies but no success in replication: investigating replication using Petty, Cacioppo, and Goldman (1981) as an example
replication_journal: Annals of the International Communication Association
replication_target_quote: The present study conducts a replication of Petty, Cacioppo, & Goldman, 1981 (PCG) as an example.
outcome_quote: the interaction between manipulated argument quality and manipulated issue involvement was not significant
review_note: The 2018 experiment directly retested Petty, Cacioppo, and Goldman's 1981 persuasion design. Its argument quality by involvement interaction was not significant (F(2, 235)=0.64, p=.528); the source expertise by involvement interaction was also not significant (F(1, 235)=0.97, p=.327). This pair codes the argument quality claim; the study used a new sample and communication setting. The later paper is an OpenAlex-primary Psychology article, and the result was checked in its author-uploaded full text.

effect_name: Variation in culturally informed forensic assessment practices
effect_claim: Forensic evaluators reported uneven use of culturally informed assessment practices.
effect_claim_quote: Self-reported culturally competent practices varied, suggesting that evaluators do not always uphold practice guidelines.
original_title: Forensic Evaluators' Self-Reported Engagement in Culturally Competent Practices
original_journal: International Journal of Forensic Mental Health
replication_title: Current Practices in Incorporating Culture into Forensic Mental Health Assessment: A Survey of Practitioners
replication_journal: International Journal of Forensic Mental Health
replication_target_quote: The current survey represents a replication and extension of a previous survey regarding self-reported culturally-informed practices among forensic evaluators.
outcome_quote: Evaluators reported engaging in a wide range of culturally-informed practices across all domains, some being nearly universal (e.g., considered cultural context when forming diagnosis).
review_note: The later paper explicitly cites Kois and Chauhan (2016) and repeats its survey question in 258 forensic mental health professionals versus 100 originally. Its abstract contrasts nearly universal consideration of cultural context in diagnosis with uncommon referral to more experienced colleagues, matching the original's uneven self-reported practices. This is a descriptive self-report replication, not independent observation of evaluator behavior. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology (queue rank 40).

effect_name: Older word-reading norms overestimate premorbid IQ
effect_claim: Earlier-normed word-reading tests produced higher estimated premorbid IQ than the more recently normed TOPF.
effect_claim_quote: Results indicated that premorbid IQ estimates were significantly different (p < .001) from each other, with the NART producing the highest premorbid IQ estimate and the TOPF the lowest estimate.
original_title: Are Tests of Premorbid Functioning Subject to the Flynn Effect?
replication_title: The Flynn Effect in Estimates of Premorbid Intellectual Functioning in an Australian Sample
replication_target_quote: The current study replicated Norton et al.’s (2016) methodology with a larger and more diverse sample.
outcome_quote: We found a linear increase in estimated FSIQ, with the oldest reading task, the NART, returning the highest scores and the most recent, the TOPF, the lowest.
review_note: The later full paper explicitly identifies Norton et al. (2016) as the study whose NART/NART2/WTAR/TOPF comparison it replicated, with 120 versus 95 Australian adults. Both found older word-reading instruments give higher estimated IQ than TOPF. The machine-linked Flynn (1984) paper concerned historical standardization samples and is background, not the direct original. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology (queue rank 41).

effect_name: Middle-way judgments under contradiction
effect_claim: When shown opposing statements, Chinese participants' plausibility judgments shifted toward intermediate evaluations rather than polarizing.
effect_claim_quote: Chinese participants who read about two contradictory studies, in contrast, expressed beliefs that were intermediate between those expressed by participants who read about only one of the studies.
original_title: Culture, Dialectics, and Reasoning About Contradiction
replication_title: Effect of Social Context on Middle-Way Judgments Among the Japanese
replication_target_quote: In a partial replication of their experiment, we tested our hypothesis that the middle-way judgment responses among Asians are specific to the social domain.
outcome_quote: The results indicate that social context is required for the middle-way seeking responses to occur.
review_note: The later authors explicitly replicated Peng and Nisbett's (1999) contradictory-statement plausibility task in Japanese rather than Chinese participants, varying whether statements were attributed to people or framed as general assertions. The later finding qualifies the original cross-cultural middle-way pattern: it appeared with social attribution, not as an unconditional response to contradiction. The machine-linked Kim and Markus (1999) uniqueness/conformity paper is a different effect. The original quote is from the authors' full-text PDF; later quote from the Japanese journal's English abstract. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology (queue rank 42).

effect_name: COSA lowers sexual recidivism
effect_claim: Participation in Circles of Support and Accountability was associated with lower sexual recidivism than matched controls.
effect_claim_quote: offenders who participated in COSA had a 70% reduction in sexual recidivism
original_title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Professionally-Facilitated Volunteerism in the Community-Based Management of High-Risk Sexual Offenders: Part Two – A Comparison of Recidivism Rates
original_authors: Robin J. Wilson, Janice E. Picheca, and Michelle Prinzo
original_journal: The Howard Journal of Criminal Justice
replication_title: Circles of Support & Accountability: A Canadian National Replication of Outcome Findings
replication_authors: Robin J. Wilson, Franca Cortoni, and Andrew J. McWhinnie
replication_target_quote: sought to replicate these findings using an independent Canadian national sample
outcome_quote: offenders in COSA had an 83% reduction in sexual recidivism
review_note: Relinked from an unrelated 1995 treatment meta-analysis to Wilson et al. 2007 pilot COSA outcome study. The 2009 article identifies the independent national sample and the same sexual-recidivism endpoint. Original scan hosted by the original first author. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W2006860823).

effect_name: Online stigma intervention lowers internalized heterosexism
effect_claim: An online intervention for same-sex attracted men reduced internalized heterosexism relative to a stress-management control.
effect_claim_quote: significant differences on the IH global score and 2 of the 3 IH subscale scores
original_title: A computer-based intervention to reduce internalized heterosexism in men
replication_title: Reducing Internalized Homonegativity: Refinement and Replication of an Online Intervention for Gay Men
replication_authors: Tania Israel, Joshua A. Goodman, Caitlin R. S. Merrill, Yen-Jui Lin, Krishna G. Kary, Em Matsuno, and Andrew Young Choi
replication_target_quote: We refined and replicated an efficacious brief intervention to reduce internalized homonegativity (IH)
outcome_quote: The intervention was efficacious at reducing global IH
review_note: Relinked from Mayfield 2001 instrument development to the Lin and Israel 2012 controlled online intervention. The later paper has the same lead/coauthor and intervention, with a community-recruited original versus non-community MTurk sample. Success is immediate global-IH reduction; the 30-day follow-up was inconclusive. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W3090888600).

effect_name: Belief conflict devalues educational research
effect_claim: Preservice teachers devalued educational research and its sources when evidence conflicted with their prior beliefs.
effect_claim_quote: participants devalued educational research and its sources when scientific evidence conflicted with their prior belief
original_title: When preservice teachers’ prior beliefs contradict evidence from educational research
original_authors: Eva Thomm, Bernadette Gold, Tilmann Betsch, and Johannes Bauer
replication_title: The scientific impotence excuse in education – Disentangling potency and pertinence assessments of educational research

effect_name: Negative information seeking, parenthood expectations, and prenatal worry
effect_claim: Negative parenthood-related information seeking predicts negative expectations, which mediate its relation to prenatal worry.
effect_claim_quote: Additionally, those with a negative interrogation bias were more likely to hold negative expectancies concerning parenthood. The relationship between this bias and prenatal worry was mediated by negative expectancies.
original_title: From Information to Worry: How Selective Interrogation of Information Shapes Expectancies in the Prenatal Period
replication_title: Repetitive negative thinking during pregnancy: The role of biased information seeking and negative prenatal expectations
replication_target_quote: The current study aimed (i) to replicate the findings of a previous study that demonstrated associations between expectations about parenthood, biased information seeking about parenthood-related information, and RNT
outcome_quote: Replicating previous findings, biased information seeking predicted stronger negative expectations, which in turn predicted higher prenatal RNT.
review_note: The original is the 2024 online publication of Mazidi et al. (2025 volume), DOI 10.1007/s10608-024-10551-4. It directly reports parenthood negative-interrogation bias, negative expectations, and prenatal worry. The 2026 article uses RNT wording and replicates the mediated expectation pattern in a new n=126 sample, extending to childbirth and pregnancy domains. The machine-linked 2025 Reading the Negative article concerns perinatal-versus-general information seeking and is not this exact expectations result.

effect_name: Sex-differentiated strength and attractiveness predictors of anger
effect_claim: Physical strength predicts anger more strongly in men, and attractiveness predicts anger more strongly in women.
effect_claim_quote: Consistent with an evolutionary analysis, the effect of strength on anger was greater for men and the effect of attractiveness on anger was greater for women.
original_title: Formidability and the logic of human anger
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
replication_title: Interpersonal leverage: Individual differences in the endorsement of anger and gratitude
replication_target_quote: to replicate the findings of Sell et al. (2009) concerning strength and attractiveness as sex-differentiated predictors of proneness to anger
outcome_quote: Results provide new support for Sell et al.'s finding that strength in men, and attractiveness in women, predict proneness to anger, but contrary to Sell et al. (2009) indicate that physical strength also predicts proneness to anger in women.
review_note: The original is Sell, Tooby, and Cosmides 2009, not the machine-linked 2017 male attractiveness article. The later full empirical three-study paper supports the positive male-strength and female-attractiveness associations but finds a female-strength association contrary to the original sex-differentiated pattern, so the full effect is mixed.

effect_name: Baseline self-harm severity predicts greater ERGT improvement
effect_claim: Greater pretreatment deliberate self-harm frequency predicts greater improvement in self-harm during ERGT follow-up.
effect_claim_quote: However, several indicators of greater severity in domains relevant to this ERGT (i.e., baseline emotion dysregulation and BPD criteria, lifetime and recent DSH, and past-year hospitalization and suicide attempts) predicted better responses during treatment and follow-up across the primary targets of treatment.
original_title: Predictors of treatment response to an adjunctive emotion regulation group therapy for deliberate self-harm among women with borderline personality disorder
original_journal: Personality Disorders: Theory, Research, and Treatment
replication_title: Predictors of improvement in an open-trial multisite evaluation of emotion regulation group therapy
replication_target_quote: Thus, we aimed to replicate previously identified predictors of treatment response to ERGT by investigating demographic, clinical, and diagnostic predictors in 95 women with BPD or subclinical BPD who had participated in an open-trial evaluation of ERGT.
outcome_quote: greater pretreatment DSH frequency was associated with greater improvements in DSH during treatment (b = 0.998, SE = 0.00, p = 0.03) and follow-up (b = 0.997, SE = 0.00, p < 0.01)
review_note: The 2014 original predictor analysis (DOI 10.1037/per0000062), not the machine-linked 2006 ERGT efficacy paper, reported greater baseline/recent self-harm among severity indicators linked to better treatment response. The 2018 multisite predictor study in a separate n=95 sample explicitly sought replication and found pretreatment DSH frequency predicted larger DSH reductions during treatment and follow-up. Other individual predictors differed, so this row targets the DSH-severity predictor only.

effect_name: Elderly male suicide follows an inverted-U relation with HDI
effect_claim: Across countries, elderly male suicide rates had a significant inverted-U relationship with the Human Development Index.

original_title: The relationship between elderly suicide rates and the human development index: a cross-national study of secondary data from the World Health Organization and the United Nations
replication_title: A replication of the relationship between elderly suicide rates and the human development index in a cross-national study
replication_target_quote: designed to replicate this curvilinear relationship between elderly suicide rates and the HDI
outcome_quote: There was a significant curvilinear (inverted U-shaped curve) relationship
review_note: Relinked from an unrelated 2007 elderly suicide paper to Shah 2009 HDI study. The 2010 paper cites Shah 2009a in its references, uses averaged and newer WHO/UN data, and finds the male inverted-U relation. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W2049384206).

effect_name: Low shifting ability strengthens worked-example benefit
effect_claim: Worked examples improved learning relative to problem solving most strongly for learners with lower shifting ability.
effect_claim_quote: worked examples are particularly beneficial for learners with lower shifting ability
original_title: Learning to solve ill-defined statistics problems: does self-explanation quality mediate the worked example effect?
original_authors: Sarah Bichler, Matthias Stadler, Markus Bühner, Samuel Greiff, and Frank Fischer
replication_title: Worked examples, cognitive aptitudes and the self‐explanation mechanism – A replication
replication_authors: Sarah Bichler, Matthias Stadler, Markus Bühner, Samuel Greiff, and Frank Fischer
replication_target_quote: we consider the present study a replication of Bichler et al.
outcome_quote: shifting ability was confirmed as a moderator of the worked example effect
review_note: Relinked from an unrelated review to the later paper’s explicitly named original Bichler et al. 2022 analysis. Each paper analyzes an independent experimental dataset collected in 2016 and 2020 respectively. This row concerns the shifting-ability moderation, which both report; the later paper finds mediation for other cognitive aptitudes, contrary to the original, outside this narrow effect. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W7162107985).

effect_name: Trait mindfulness increases resistance to sunk costs
effect_claim: People higher in trait mindfulness are more likely to resist decisions driven by unrecoverable prior costs.
effect_claim_quote: Study 1 served as an initial correlational demonstration of the positive relationship between trait mindfulness and resistance to the sunk-cost bias.
original_title: Debiasing the Mind Through Meditation: Mindfulness and the Sunk-Cost Bias
replication_title: Mindfulness and decision making: sunk costs or escalation of commitment?
replication_target_quote: The present study extends previous work by replicating the finding that trait mindfulness is positively related to resistance to the effects of sunk costs
outcome_quote: the relationship between trait mindfulness and resistance to the effects of sunk costs was less consistently observed.
review_note: Relinked from an unrelated trait-mindfulness measure to Hafenbrack, Kinias, and Barsade (2014), whose Study 1 reported the positive trait-mindfulness versus sunk-cost-resistance association. The independent published 2020 study directly describes replicating that association, but says it was less consistent than the reduction in escalation of commitment; coded mixed for the narrow sunk-cost-resistance relationship. The later paper is an OpenAlex-primary Psychology research article. The original statement was checked in the author-hosted published PDF; the later result is in the publisher abstract. The preprint DOI 10.31234/osf.io/rzdvt is a separate version and is not used as a discovery alias.

effect_name: Pessimistic forecasts for cold and incompetent social targets
effect_claim: People expect more negative than positive future events for targets perceived as cold and incompetent.
effect_claim_quote: For the univalent negative out-group, the desirability bias manifested in the opposite direction, with participants expecting significantly more negative events than positive.
original_title: Warmth and competence predict overoptimistic beliefs for out-group but not in-group members
replication_title: Sociality of future outcomes moderates the effects of warmth and competence on social optimism bias
replication_target_quote: In the present study, we replicated previous findings with an entirely different set of stimuli while also adding two new levels of complexity.
outcome_quote: respondents manifested a pessimism bias toward the cold-incompetent character regardless of the sociality of the outcomes.
review_note: The 2018 Dricu et al. PLOS study, not the machine-linked stereotype content chapter, directly reported the cold-incompetent target pessimism effect. The 2022 preregistered Nature study used a new participant sample and entirely different event stimuli, explicitly replicated previous findings, and found pessimism for the cold-incompetent target under both social and alone events. Warm target optimism had a sociality boundary; this row targets only the robust cold-incompetent pessimism finding.

effect_name: Regulatory focus predicts field sales performance
effect_claim: Promotion focus predicts better individual sales performance, whereas prevention focus predicts worse performance.
effect_claim_quote: We propose and find that promotion focus positively predicts sales agents’ success, while prevention focus negatively predicts sales success.
original_title: To go or not to go for the sell: Regulatory focus and personal sales performance
replication_title: Regulatory Focus and Individual Sales Performance of Field Marketers: A Constructive Replication
replication_target_quote: We attempt constructive replication of these findings using stronger methodology.
outcome_quote: Our study (N = 156) showed that promotion focus positively, and prevention focus negatively, predicted performance.
review_note: The exact original is Hamstra et al. 2015, not the machine-linked 1996 regulatory-focus theory paper. The 2018 open-access empirical paper explicitly uses a different field-sales sample and improved measures and repeats both directional associations, with somewhat smaller promotion effect.

effect_name: Adolescent borderline traits and hypermentalizing
effect_claim: Adolescent borderline personality traits are associated with hypermentalizing errors on the MASC social cognition task.
effect_claim_quote: Results: Findings suggest a relationship between borderline traits and "hypermentalizing" (excessive, inaccurate mentalizing) independent of age, gender, externalizing, internalizing and psychopathy symptoms.
original_title: Theory of mind and emotion regulation difficulties in adolescents with borderline traits
original_journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry
replication_title: Hypermentalizing as a marker of borderline personality disorder in Italian adolescents: a cross-cultural replication of Sharp and colleagues’ (2011) findings
replication_journal: Borderline Personality Disorder and Emotion Dysregulation
replication_target_quote: We aimed at testing if both dimensionally-assessed and categorically-diagnosed BPD was selectively associated with hypermentalizing errors on the Movie for the Assessment of Social Cognition (MASC) task in Italian adolescent inpatients and community adolescents.
outcome_quote: Both dimensionally-assessed and categorically-assessed BPD showed significant and non-negligible associations with hypermentalizing.
review_note: The exact original is Sharp et al. 2011, not the machine-linked 2009 protocol article. The later Springer full paper describes an independent Italian inpatient sample (n=58) versus the original US sample (n=111) and uses the same MASC measure; both dimensional and categorical BPD were associated with hypermentalizing. The original included adjusted analyses; the later did not replicate every covariate adjustment, so this row targets the MASC-BPD association.

effect_name: Preferred activity presentation increases observed happiness
effect_claim: Presenting preferred activities, with contingent withdrawal, increases observable happiness indices in people with profound multiple disabilities.
effect_claim_quote: Subsequently, classroom staff increased happiness indices through presentation and contingent withdrawal of activities.
original_title: Defining, validating, and increasing indices of happiness among people with profound multiple disabilities
replication_title: INCREASING INDICES OF HAPPINESS AMONG PEOPLE WITH PROFOUND MULTIPLE DISABILITIES: A PROGRAM REPLICATION AND COMPONENT ANALYSIS
replication_target_quote: We replicated a program to increase indices of happiness among people with profound multiple disabilities and conducted a component analysis of the program.
outcome_quote: The program was implemented with 3 adult students and was accompanied by increased happiness indices for each student.
review_note: The canonical first original is Green and Reid 1996, not the machine-linked January 1997 Ivancic et al. paper, which also replicated Green and Reid. The later Green/Gardner/Reid 1997 full empirical paper tested three new adult students and again found increases in observed happiness indices; its component analysis found formally assessed preferred stimuli more consistent than staff opinion.

effect_name: Fertility raises preference for masculine male bodies
effect_claim: Near peak fertility, women prefer more masculine male bodies, especially for short-term mates.
effect_claim_quote: women prefer greater masculinity in male bodies at times when their fertility is likely highest
original_title: Preferences for masculinity in male bodies change across the menstrual cycle
replication_title: Fertile women evaluate male bodies as more attractive, regardless of masculinity
replication_target_quote: we investigated cycle shifts in women's mate preferences for masculine bodies
outcome_quote: male masculine traits did not interact with cycle phase to predict attraction, indicating that women's preferential priorities do not shift
review_note: Little, Jones, and Burriss (2007), cited by the later paper, reported that women's preference for masculine male body shape increases near peak fertility, especially for a short-term partner. Jünger et al. (2018) independently tested masculine-body preferences in 157 women over two cycles with preregistration and natural body stimuli. Overall body attractiveness ratings rose at fertility, but masculinity did not interact with cycle phase. This codes failure of the specific masculinity-preference shift, not absence of every cycle effect. The machine-linked body-odor paper was unrelated. The later full published paper is OpenAlex-primary Psychology.

effect_name: Bitter tastes match lower musical pitches
effect_claim: In explicit taste-to-sound matching, bitter tastes were preferentially matched with lower-pitched musical notes.
effect_claim_quote: umami and bitter tastes were preferentially matched to low-pitched notes
original_title: As bitter as a trombone: Synesthetic correspondences in nonsynesthetes between tastes/flavors and musical notes
replication_title: Trombones Elicit Bitter More Strongly Than Do Clarinets: a Partial Replication of Three Studies of Crisinel and Spence
replication_authors: Quentin J. Watson and Karen L. Gunther
replication_target_quote: partial replication of the crossmodal pitch/taste correspondence of Crisinel and Spence
outcome_quote: unsweetened chocolate being associated with the lowest pitch and sugar with the highest
review_note: Crisinel and Spence 2010 is one of three specifically cited original studies in the later publisher/Crossref reference list, and the direct explicit taste-to-pitch matching study. Watson and Gunther used an independent male college sample. Lower pitch for bitter chocolate was replicated with trombone and averaged instruments, while clarinet alone was nonsignificant. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W2613961782).

effect_name: Matching response character styles increase Rorschach-MMPI convergence

original_authors: Gregory J. Meyer, Robert J. Riethmiller, Regina D. Brooks, William A. Benoit, and Leonard Handler

replication_authors: John M. Stokes, David L. Pogge, and Michele Zaccario

review_note: The later abstract explicitly identifies Meyer et al. 2000 and tests an independent adolescent inpatient sample (n=673), compared with adults in the original. The positive convergence conditional on matching response character styles is directly supported by both results. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W2003344632).

effect_name: Identity-congruent action sounds attenuate auditory N1

The later experiment tested learned key-tone and cue-tone associations in a new sample and found no convincing perceptual or neurophysiological identity-prediction evidence. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W2904152424).

effect_name: Older breast-cancer patients receive less reconstruction support
effect_claim: Medical trainees recommended breast reconstruction after mastectomy less often for older than younger patients with otherwise similar breast cancer cases.

original_title: Ageism in medical students' treatment recommendations: the example of breast-conserving procedures
original_authors: Atul K. Madan, Shaghayegh Aliabadi-Wahle, and Derrick J. Beech
replication_title: Ageism and caring attitudes among nurses in oncology
replication_authors: S. Schroyen, P. Missotten, G. Jerusalem, C. Gilles, and S. Adam
replication_target_quote: Based on previous studies that focused on physicians (Madan et al., 2001, Protière et al., 2010)
outcome_quote: support for immunotherapy, breast reconstruction, and chemotherapy is lower for older patients than for younger patients
review_note: The later full paper explicitly cites Madan et al. 2001 (and Protière et al. 2010) as the prior physician/trainee studies it seeks to replicate in oncology nurses. Both studies use independent provider samples and age-varied breast cancer vignettes; this row concerns less reconstruction support for older patients. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W2236230825).

effect_name: Low social hierarchy predicts situational suppression
effect_claim: In the original U.S. experience-sampling study, participants used more expressive suppression in situations where they felt low in social hierarchy.

original_title: An experience sampling approach to emotion regulation: Situational suppression use and social hierarchy
original_authors: Arman Daniel Catterson, Lameese Eldesouky, and Oliver P. John
replication_title: Situational suppression use and social hierarchy in non-individualistic and hierarchic society: A replication study
replication_authors: Irena Pilch, Lidia Baran, Magdalena Bolek-Kochanowska, Maciej Bożek, Wiola Friedrich, Magdalena Hyla, and Jagoda Sikora
replication_target_quote: The objective of the current study was to replicate an ESM study by Catterson, Eldesouky, and John (2017) on suppression use in daily life, conducted in the USA.
outcome_quote: Contrary to expectations, the relationship between suppression and hierarchy was positive.
review_note: Close experience-sampling replication in Poland. The original low-hierarchy association reversed; both studies found cross-situational variation, so the failed code is limited to the directional hierarchy-suppression effect. The later study found no hierarchy-by-suppression interaction in predicting wellbeing. Publisher states the replication was not preregistered. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology: https://openalex.org/W2803218683.

effect_name: Trait-change goals predict counter-goal conscientiousness and neuroticism change
effect_claim: In the original U.K. 12-month cohort, goals and plans to change Conscientiousness and Neuroticism predicted trait change opposite to the desired direction.

original_authors: Oliver C. Robinson, Erik E. Noftle, Jen Guo, Samaneh Asadi, and Xiaozhou Zhang

replication_target_quote: The current study replicated and extended the methodology of a previous study to investigate whether trait change goals and plans predict change over a year in an Iranian sample of students.
outcome_quote: It was found that goals and plans before and after the 12-month period predicted longitudinal change in Openness to Experience, but no association was found for other traits.
review_note: The same 12-month goals/plans versus Big Five trait-change analysis was repeated in Iranian students. The original counter-goal change for Conscientiousness and Neuroticism was not detected; only Openness showed an association. The later author-accepted manuscript states the study was not preregistered. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology: https://openalex.org/W2998736502.

effect_name: Verbal self-discrimination predicts later wellbeing
effect_claim: Values-oriented self-rules and self-as-context coded from natural speech predicted wellbeing six and twelve months later in the original sample.

original_title: Measuring self and rules in what people say: exploring whether self-discrimination predicts long-term wellbeing
original_authors: Paul W. B. Atkins and Robert G. Styles
replication_title: Measuring perceptions of self and others in what people say: A replication and extension of the functional self-discrimination measure
replication_authors: Robert G. Styles and Paul W. B. Atkins
replication_target_quote: The Functional Self-Discrimination Measure (FSDM) is a method of coding a speaker's verbal discrimination of their own behavior based on Relational Frame Theory (RFT) that predicts wellbeing 6 and 12 months later (Atkins & Styles, 2016).
outcome_quote: In this study, we replicated our original findings with a new sample
review_note: Same authors applied speech coding to a new sample and explicitly reported replicating the original long-term wellbeing prediction. The extension added other-as-context coding; this pair is limited to the original self-discrimination/wellbeing association. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology: https://openalex.org/W2808576049.

effect_name: Narcissism predicts sexual competitiveness in women
effect_claim: In a women-only sample, narcissism within the Dark Triad positively predicted sexual competitiveness.
effect_claim_quote: Regression analyses indicated that DT, and in particular, narcissism, are significant predictors of general and sexual competitiveness.
original_title: Women's sexual competition and the Dark Triad
original_authors: Gregory L. Carter, Zoe Montanaro, Catherine Linney, and Anne C. Campbell
replication_title: Replicating the relationships between Dark Triad traits and female mate-competition tactics in undergraduate women
replication_authors: Scott W. Semenyna, Paul L. Vasey, and Lynne Honey
replication_target_quote: The present study sought to replicate links between DT traits and female-typical mate competition tactics, such as appearance enhancement, gossiping, and indirect sabotage of rivals.
outcome_quote: Each DT trait was positively related to sexual competitiveness, collectively accounting for an additional 13% of the total variance.
review_note: Relinked from an unrelated machine-suggested DOI to Carter et al. 2015, explicitly cited as the prior finding in the later paper. The pair tracks the narcissism-sexual-competitiveness association; the later study included a larger undergraduate women sample and additional covariates. Later OpenAlex primary Field Psychology: https://openalex.org/W2941885737.

effect_name: Altruism outweighs physical attractiveness in long-term mate choice
effect_claim: For long-term partners, women prefer altruistic men even over men who are physically attractive but less altruistic.
effect_claim_quote: men who were just altruistic were rated more desirable than men who were just attractive, especially for LT relationships
original_title: Are Women’s Mate Preferences for Altruism Also Influenced by Physical Attractiveness?
replication_title: Mutual mate choice drives the desirability of altruism in relationships
replication_target_quote: Altruists will be preferred over physically attractive individuals, particularly for long term relationships, as found by Farrelly et al., (2016).
outcome_quote: there was no support for altruism being more important than physical attractiveness
review_note: Farrelly and King (2019) explicitly repeated Farrelly, Clemson, and Guthrie’s (2016) vignette method with a new online sample of 189 men and women (original N=202 women). It tested the claim that altruistic but less physically attractive targets are preferred to attractive but nonaltruistic targets, especially for long-term partnerships. Unlike the original, the later paper found no such advantage; it did reproduce a general long-term preference for altruistic partners. This pair codes only the altruism-over-attractiveness contrast. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology; the machine-linked Buss mate-preferences paper is background rather than the copied study.

effect_name: Sex-specific physiological jealousy responses
effect_claim: When imagining partner infidelity, men and women show different physiological responses to sexual versus emotional infidelity.
effect_claim_quote: All studies showed large sex differences, confirming hypothesized sex linkages in jealousy activation.
original_title: Sex Differences in Jealousy: Evolution, Physiology, and Psychology
original_authors: David M. Buss, Randy J. Larsen, Drew Westen, and Jennifer Semmelroth
replication_title: The Evolution of Sex Differences in Jealousy: Failure to Replicate Previous Results
replication_authors: James W. Grice and Elizabeth Seely
replication_target_quote: findings of prior research (Buss, Larsen, Westen, & Semmelroth, 1992)
outcome_quote: Results generally failed to support the evolutionary hypothesis and to replicate the findings of prior research (Buss, Larsen, Westen, & Semmelroth, 1992).
review_note: The original paper's Study 2 measured heart rate, electrodermal response, and facial-muscle activity while participants imagined sexual and emotional infidelity. Grice and Seely measured physiological reactions to imagined infidelity in a new sample and explicitly report failure to reproduce Buss et al. 1992. The pair is limited to the physiological response claim, not forced-choice questionnaire effects. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W2060392602).

effect_name: Male advantage in self-estimated overall intelligence
effect_claim: Male students estimated their own overall intelligence higher than female students in the US, UK and Japan.
effect_claim_quote: Male participants rated their own overall IQ and that of their fathers, but not their mothers and sisters, higher than did female participants as predicted.
original_title: Male hubris and female humility? A crosscultural study of ratings of self, parental, and sibling multiple intelligence in America, Britain, and Japan
replication_target_quote: It was one of a programmatic series of studies done in over 30 countries that has demonstrated the female "humility" and male "hubris" effect in self-estimated and other-estimated intelligence.
outcome_quote: Results revealed no sex difference in estimates of overall intelligence for both self and parents, but men rated themselves higher on spatial intelligence.
review_note: The original cross-cultural study found higher self-estimated overall IQ among men in distinct American, British and Japanese student samples. The 2012 Russian student sample (N=230) tested the same self-estimate and reports no sex difference in overall IQ, while retaining a male spatial self-estimate advantage. The result is a boundary/failed replication for overall IQ specifically, not for every multiple-intelligence domain.
replication_title: Sex differences in estimating multiple intelligences in self and others: A replication in Russia

effect_name: Higher subjective well-being among BDSM practitioners
effect_claim: BDSM practitioners reported higher subjective well-being than non-practitioner controls.
effect_claim_quote: BDSM practitioners were less neurotic, more extraverted, more open to new experiences, more conscientious, less rejection sensitive, had higher subjective well-being, yet were less agreeable.
original_title: Psychological characteristics of BDSM practitioners
replication_target_quote: This study conducts a close replication to examine personality, attachment, rejection sensitivity, and well-being differences between BDSM practitioners and non-practitioners.
outcome_quote: As predicted, BDSM practitioners showed higher levels of secure attachment, conscientiousness, openness, and well-being while also lower levels of insecure attachments, rejection sensitivity, neuroticism, and agreeableness, countering the stigma.
review_note: The machine-linked 2018 attachment mediation paper was unrelated. The later authors state that they conducted a close replication of the 2013 Wismeijer and van Assen group comparison. Original Netherlands online sample included 902 practitioners and 434 controls; later independent Spanish sample N=1,907 replicated the well-being difference. This row targets subjective well-being only.
replication_title: Not Twisted, Just Kinky: Replication and Structural Invariance of Attachment, Personality, and Well-Being Among BDSM Practitioners

effect_name: Social-skills training improves prosocial behavior in adults with intellectual disability
effect_claim: Individualized social-skills training increased targeted prosocial behaviors in an intellectually disabled adult.
effect_claim_quote: All behaviors improved initially; decrements in skill performance seen over the six months of no treatment were reinstituted in booster sessions.
original_title: Social skills training to teach prosocial behaviors in an organically impaired and retarded patient
original_journal: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
replication_target_quote: Six mentally retarded adults, equally divided into two treatment groups, were provided with individualized social skills training programs.
outcome_quote: treatment was effective for virtually all behaviors across all subjects

effect_name: Monetary rewards can reduce later puzzle engagement

original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: An evaluation of the overjustification hypothesis: A replication of Deci (1971)
replication_target_quote: This study was a direct replication of the landmark study evaluating the overjustification hypothesis conducted by Deci (1971).
outcome_quote: These findings did not provide support for the overjustification effect.

replication_title: Differential perceptions of counselor behavior: Replication and extension
replication_target_quote: Conducted 2 studies with 141 undergraduates in an attempt to replicate and extend the 1976 findings of M. B. LaCrosse and A. Barak (1976).

review_note: Two new undergraduate studies reproduced the form’s sensitivity to perceived counselor differences. A. Barak authored both the 1976 and 1977 papers; this is an overlapping-author replication. Scoped to perceived-difference measurement, not predictive validity of treatment outcomes. Later OpenAlex W2161611140 primary field Psychology.

review_note: Independent conceptual retest in 247 male winners and losers after a physical competition. replication_target_quote: Adopting expansive vs. constrictive postures related to high vs. low levels of social power has been suggested to induce changes in testosterone and cortisol levels, and thereby to mimic hormonal correlates of dominance behavior.

review_note: Independent preregistered conceptual replication of felt-power component in fourth-graders; indirect feeling measure was higher following high-power than low-power poses. Does not test original hormonal or risk-taking components. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology.

replication_target_quote: We planned to investigate this question by asking 200 participants to either perform or imagine a constrictive or an expansive body posture during 2 min and then measure the effect on a gambling decision task and on felt power.
outcome_quote: The results after running 200 participants confirmed that power poses did not affect gambling decision.
review_note: Independent conceptual/direct retest of the original gambling-risk effect with 200 participants assigned to expanded or constricted poses. No gambling decision effect, while felt power increased; outcome is scoped to risk tolerance only. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology.

effect_name: Expansive poses raise felt power

replication_target_quote: We measured enacted duration, risky behavior, and felt power.
outcome_quote: Finally, we did not strongly replicate prior work, but found some support that enacting high-power postures led to riskier behavior and more felt power for some aspects of the sample in exploratory analyses.
review_note: The preregistered primary test did not reproduce the original felt-power effect, consistent with the existing legacy classification of informative failure (N=94).
