replication_authors: Jessica L. Engelbrecht; Matthew Duell; John E. Edlund
review_note: No-key official OpenAlex W4391784795 classifies the published Psychological Reports article as primary Psychology, type article; SAGE confirms first online publication February 12, 2024, despite placement in a later 2026 issue. The later SAGE abstract explicitly identifies Navarrete et al. (2010) Study 1 and a conceptual retest using 2020-election preference measures with Barack Obama retained. The 2010 Elsevier original abstract reports that higher conception risk predicted greater intended Obama support in the 2008 election. The later new sample showed no greater Obama support as conception risk rose. Authors do not overlap; verdict is limited to the Obama-voter-preference fertility association, not all race-perception moderation claims from original Study 2.

effect_name: Global versus local visual processing and creative versus analytic performance

replication_title: Does Global and Local Vision Have an Impact on Creative and Analytic Thought? Two Failed Replications
review_note: Official OpenAlex W2240171675 classifies the later PLOS ONE research article as primary Psychology. Its full text says Study 2 closely replicated Experiment 6 of Förster and Denzler 2012 with 2.5 times the original sample, original stimuli, and new participants; no Navon-induced global/local processing effect on either analytic or creative tasks was found. The original institutional UvA repository preserves the claimed global-versus-local creative/analytic performance effect. CRITICAL HISTORICAL STATUS: SAGE retracted the original article DOI 10.1177/1948550611410890 in 2015 after an institutional finding of manipulated data (https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1948550611410890). The claim is recorded as a retracted original claim, not as reliable evidence. Authors are disjoint.

review_note: Official OpenAlex W4206391469 classifies the later Journal of Scientific Exploration article as primary Psychology and article type. Publisher issue and full-paper PDF show publication December 30, 2021, although OpenAlex indexes 2022. The original 2020 APA journal abstract reports an excess of experiment-versus-control correlations in a 45×45 human-behavior/random-generator matrix (randomization p=.0177). The later paper references exact original DOI 10.1037/cns0000199 and says its two independent new-participant consensus-protocol replications (N=64 and N=40, different sites) were not significant. Harald Walach, Thilo Hinterberger, and Walter von Lucadou authored both studies; this is openly disclosed, with distinct data and additional replication investigators. The verdict records the reported anomalistic-correlation result, without endorsing a psychokinetic or quantum interpretation.

review_note: Published Columbia journal paper tested a new group of 34 Korean native speakers, versus original 46 Korean/Chinese speakers. Overall age-of-arrival association recurred (later r=-.848 versus original r=-.77), but the apparent boundary shifted from 15 to 10 and other age-function details differed. Full-pattern outcome mixed, matching FLoRA coding. Official canonical publisher DOI is 10.7916/salt.v5i2.1571 (OpenAlex W6977726099, primary Psychology); FLoRA uses repository DOI 10.7916/d8f76r2r for the same article, not a separate experiment. No overlapping authors.

review_note: Hagopian et al. 2020 DOI 10.1002/jaba.725 studied six consecutive cases and found more effective competing stimuli after temporary response promotion and blocking were withdrawn. Frank-Crawford et al. 2023 DOI 10.1002/jaba.1009 explicitly states that it retested the 2020 method with additional participants; its 16-case series had improved outcomes after tactic withdrawal in six of eight relevant applications. The scoped claim is that the augmentation can improve later response competition, not that it succeeds for every case. Hagopian and Frank-Crawford authored both papers, and the later paper describes additional participants. Official OpenAlex W4384665110 classifies the later journal article primary Psychology.

outcome_quote: Consistent with the original study, participants (N = 324) higher in Honesty-Humility and Agreeableness showed more prosocial lying.

Reinhardt et al. 2024 explicitly close-replicated the procedure in an independent N=324 sample, again finding positive bivariate links for both Honesty-Humility and Agreeableness. Successful is scoped to that bivariate directional association. Later authors caution that both links disappear when included together in a regression, weakening any claim of Honesty-Humility dominance; this broader interpretive difference is disclosed. Authors disjoint. Official cached OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

(2024), compares its 17 participants with 25 new participants, and reports schedule control of walking speed under preferred-music contingencies in 18/25 (72%). The original Wiley abstract reports selective walking-speed increases/decreases under synchronized music and variability during extinction. Several authors overlap, but the replication collected a distinct sample. Verdict is limited to preferred-music schedule control of walking speed, not identical effect size or every extinction component.

The original SAGE publisher abstract states that reminders of atheist prevalence reduced explicit distrust in Study 3. The later paper was first published online April 20, 2025 despite assignment to a 2026 issue. Original author Gervais participates in the later work, but these are independent new samples. Verdict is scoped to the causal prevalence-information effect on explicit anti-atheist prejudice, not the original correlational or implicit-prejudice studies.

effect_name: Oxytocin lowers self-reported agency in anxiously attached individuals

effect_claim_quote: There was no main effect of oxytocin on agency for the average participant; however, anxiously attached individuals showed a selective decrease in agency (“independent,” “self-confident,” etc.) following administration of oxytocin.
replication_target_quote: The first aim of this research was to replicate the aforementioned oxytocin-attachment avoidance-communion and oxytocin-attachment anxiety-agency findings
outcome_quote: the oxytocin--anxiety-agency effect (P = .014) in a larger (N = 77; within-subject), gender diverse sample.
original_title: Differential Effects of Oxytocin on Agency and Communion for Anxiously and Avoidantly Attached Individuals
replication_title: Effects of Oxytocin on Agency in Anxiously Attached Individuals, a Replication and Extension

replication_authors: Jennifer A. Bartz; Willis Benjamin Klein; Amy J. P. Gregory

The later abstract confirms the oxytocin × attachment-anxiety effect on agency (P=.014); the original SAGE publisher abstract reports a selective agency decrease among anxiously attached participants. Original author Bartz participated in the new study; the samples are independent. Verdict is scoped to conceptual self-reported agency; the new bodily-agency extension did not show oxytocin potentiation.

effect_name: Pointing and tracing improves heart-lesson comprehension

review_note: Springer full text explicitly identifies Macken and Ginns (2014) as the initial heart-material study, says the current work is a conceptual replication changing the instructional language to Chinese, and recruits 84 new adult participants versus the original 42. The original Taylor & Francis publisher abstract finds better comprehension-test performance with pointing/tracing; the later Springer abstract reports the same comprehension advantage. The later terminology outcome was not statistically significant and is excluded from the effect scope. Author Ginns overlaps, but participants are new.

original_title: Maternal Guilt and Shame: The Role of Self-discrepancy and Fear of Negative Evaluation
